findings.claim: The dial moves the book's correlation structure and market beta, not its variance, and the effect is concentrated above 50: effective N falls from 4.4 to 3.1 strategies and the SPY-explained share of book variance triples (10% -> 31%) between calm tape and dial 65+.
findings.numbers: Live-vintage 10d-MA 63d dial, lag-1, 2016-07-20..2026-08-07 (2440 dial days). Bucket <30 (1527d): avg pairwise corr 0.024, eff N (vol-weighted) 4.42, book beta 0.21, R2 0.10, SPY ann +22.6%, book Sharpe 2.77, sd 84 bps. 30-50 (564d): corr 0.022, eff N 4.43, beta 0.28, R2 0.09, SPY +13.8%, Sharpe 3.37. 50-65 (216d): corr 0.085, eff N 3.77, beta 0.40, R2 0.16, SPY -2.7%, Sharpe 2.53. 65+ (133d): corr 0.075, eff N 3.12, beta 0.41, R2 0.31, SPY -24.1%, Sharpe 1.25, sd 74 bps (book sd is FLAT across buckets, 74-86 bps). Pairs: calm tape has no pair above 0.11; at 50-65 LT Trend-St OS Sznl 0.61, OLV-St OS 0.24, LTT-OLV 0.20; at 65+ 52wh-OLV 0.26, OLV-WCDS 0.17; OLV-MonFri goes 0.03 (calm) -> 0.41 (dial>=50).
findings.method: Per-strategy daily MTM on the flat $750k basis (dist/data/strategy_daily.json, tiers collapsed, exchange sessions only), bucketed by lag-1 dial; pairwise correlation among strategies active >10% of bucket days; effective N = 1/(w'Cw) with vol weights; OLS beta of book return on SPY.
findings.n: 2440 dial days, 133 at 65+ (about 5 episodes: Q4-2018, Feb-2020, mid-2021, Dec-2021/Jan-2022, Feb-2026 plus the truncated Aug-2026)
findings.robustness: Reproduces the baseline's L3 table on a cleaned session calendar (the earlier run carried 217 holiday rows). Same ordering on VIX-independent slices (dial>=50 & VIX<20: R2 0.20; dial>=50 & VIX>=20: 0.22). The 65+ bucket is few episodes; treat the 31% as an order of magnitude.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Nothing at the book-scalar level (variance is flat); the control belongs at the factor: hedge the embedded beta when the dial is high. Confirms the baseline plan's L3 diagnosis with cleaner data.
findings.caveat: Current-weights dial (rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage, drift up to ~7 points).

findings.claim: The book's beta to SPY is NOT a fear phenomenon: it is HIGHEST in low-VIX, near-the-highs tape and LOWEST after volatility has arrived. VIX, VIX percentile and SPY-drawdown are the mirror image of the dial as hedge triggers, which is why every non-dial arming rule loses money.
findings.numbers: By lag-1 VIX (2010+): VIX<15 (1438d) beta 0.515, R2 0.21, down-day beta 0.61, SPY +10%, book Sharpe 1.45; 15-20 (1521d) beta 0.40, Sharpe 2.03; 20-30 (959d) beta 0.24, Sharpe 3.03, SPY +18%; 30+ (256d) beta 0.17, down-beta 0.04, SPY +64% ann, Sharpe 3.79, 26 bps/day. By SPY 252d drawdown: dd>10% (452d) beta 0.15, SPY +46%, Sharpe 2.85; dd<2% (2313d) beta 0.44, SPY +6.7%, Sharpe 1.76. Joint dial x VIX (2016-07+): dial>=50 & VIX<20 (261d) SPY -20.1% ann, book Sharpe 1.03, R2 0.20; dial>=50 & VIX>=20 (88d) SPY +16.5%, Sharpe 3.88. Hedge controls (book/SPY/63d, live): VIX>=25 rel 20: -$158.5k, 0 of 15 episodes positive, clustered t -3.85, Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.66; VIX 252d-pctile >=80 rel 60: -$154k, 3/21 positive, t -2.11; SPY dd<-5% rel -3%: -$139k, 2/14 positive, t -2.12; always-hedged: -$478k over 10y (-2.5 bps/day), Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.42, maxDD -8.3% -> -11.5%.
findings.method: Same daily series bucketed by lag-1 VIX level, trailing-252d VIX percentile and SPY distance from 252d high; hedge replays with hysteresis arming on each state variable, 2 bps x |beta| friction per arm event.
findings.n: 4174 sessions 2010+ for the VIX/drawdown buckets; 2527 sessions for the hedge controls; 14-21 armed episodes per control
findings.robustness: Sign is identical on the PIT window (VIX25: -$158.5k; VIXpct80: -$108k; dd5: -$139k). Every control has more episodes than the dial rules and is negative in nearly all of them, so this is not a small-sample verdict.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not arm a hedge, a cut, or any beta control on VIX or on the book's/SPY's drawdown state; the book's edge and its lowest beta both arrive AFTER vol spikes (the dip-buy family's payoff). The dial's value is that it fires in the complacent pre-selloff state where beta is high and SPY's forward drift is negative. Any sizing rule that leans on realized vol as a proxy for the dial will be wrong-signed.
findings.caveat: The 'SPY +64% ann at VIX 30+' cell is 256 days dominated by 2020 and 2022 rebounds; the beta ordering, not the SPY mean, is the robust part.

findings.claim: The dial-armed book beta hedge (baseline P1) SURVIVES the point-in-time dial vintage at threshold 50/45 and passes the pre-registered ship rule; threshold 65/60 is marginal on PIT. Placebo and episode bootstrap say the dial is doing real work over unconditional short-beta carry.
findings.numbers: Book target, SPY, 63d lag-1 beta clipped [-1,2], 2 bps friction. PIT vintage (2018-01-02..2026-07-02, 2136d): dial 50/45 -> 544 armed days, 13 episodes, hedge +$104.3k (2.56 bps per armed day), 10 of 13 episodes positive, mean episode +$8.0k, clustered t 1.68, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.04 (equal-vol ann 37.6% -> 39.7%), maxDD -8.32% -> -8.13%, armed-day Sharpe 1.85 -> 2.44, LOYO 7 of 9 armed years not worse (7/9 hedge PnL positive), episode-bootstrap P(total<=0) 0.046, drop-best-episode total +$71k t 1.27, placebo (500 circular shifts of the armed mask) mean -$90k sd $66k, rank 1.000. PIT 65/60: 318 armed days, 8 episodes, +$55.2k, 6/8 positive, t 0.99, Sharpe 2.90 -> 2.97, LOYO 6/7, bootstrap P(<=0) 0.134, drop-best (Feb-2020 $39.6k) t 0.37. Live vintage (2016-07-20..2026-08-07, 2527d): 50/45 -> 392 armed, 10 episodes, +$35.1k, 7/10 positive, t 0.72, Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.84, maxDD -8.32 -> -8.12, placebo rank 0.970, bootstrap P(<=0) 0.22; 65/60 -> 153 armed, 7 episodes, +$58.6k (5.1 bps/day), 5/7 positive, t 1.37, armed Sharpe 2.04 -> 3.15, placebo rank 0.974, drop-best t 0.85; 50 no-hysteresis +$70.6k t 1.58 (the baseline's 2.90 row). Live on the PIT window: 50/45 +$58.8k, 7/8 positive, t 1.43, Sharpe 2.90 -> 2.99.
findings.method: Hedge PnL = -armed x beta_hat x SPY return x NAV; episodes = armed runs separated by >=21 unarmed sessions; clustered t = mean episode PnL / (sd / sqrt(n)); LOYO = per-calendar-year Sharpe hedged vs unhedged on years with any arming; placebo = circular shift of the armed mask (preserves episode count and lengths, destroys timing). PIT dial from expanding-window diff_mean edges at each year-end, year Y scored with vintage Y-1 (scratch/pit_reestimate.py method; PIT vs live corr 0.89, >=50 agreement 88%; PIT is >=50 on 22.9% of days vs 15.4% live).
findings.n: PIT: 13 episodes / 544 armed days; live: 10 / 392; 65+ rules: 7-8 episodes
findings.robustness: Robust to window (PIT 50/45: 42d +$108k t 1.63; 126d +$110k t 1.67 Sharpe 3.07 maxDD -7.89; shrunk 0.5x63d+0.5xexpanding +$89k t 2.12), to hedge ratio (0.5x/1x/1.5x/2x Sharpe 3.00/3.04/3.01/2.92 PIT; 2.82/2.84/2.81/2.75 live; maxDD worsens to -10.2% at 2x), positive in 7 of 9 PIT years (losing years 2021 -$24k and 2023 -$9.6k). Weak points: the live-vintage 50/45 is only t 0.72 with 4 false-alarm episodes costing -$47k (2017-09 at beta_hat 1.02 and Apr-Sep 2021 at 94 armed days are the two big ones); 65/60 depends on Feb-2020.
findings.implication_for_sizing: P1 can move from 'prereg' to 'paper-track, then ship' as written, with these amendments: threshold 50/45 (not 65), whole-book target, 126d or shrunk beta, 1.0x ratio, SPY/ES instrument. Expected scale: ~1.3 episodes/yr, +$8k per episode, +0.1 to +0.15 full-sample Sharpe, calm carry ~-$5k/yr from false alarms. It is the one dial-conditioned control that clears PIT.
findings.caveat: The PIT series in 2018 is scored by a one-signal vintage (only Seasonal Rank Divergence had an edge) and is the noisiest year; the daily payload ends 2026-08-07 so the Aug-2026 episode is 6 armed days (-$6k) and truncated; signal definitions are today's code (residual lookahead PIT cannot cure).

findings.claim: The hedge earns its money from the dial's negative SPY drift forecast, not from variance reduction: on armed days it removes only ~6% of book sd, and the book's realized beta is asymmetric (larger on up days than down days) so a full OLS-beta hedge gives back more on rallies than it saves on selloffs per unit of move.
findings.numbers: Live dial 50/45 armed days (392): realized beta 0.40 (down-days 0.27, up-days 0.50), ex-ante beta_hat mean 0.50, SPY ann -9.7%; hedge PnL on SPY-down days +$457k, on SPY-up days -$421k; book sd 80.6 -> hedged 76.0 bps. Drift component of hedge PnL $55.9k vs total $35.1k (timing/variance part -$21k). Dial 65+ bucket: beta_up 0.785 vs beta_down 0.261. Ex-ante beta quality: corr(beta_hat, realized next-21d beta) 0.24/0.21/0.22 for 42/63/126d overall, but at dial>=50 it is -0.04/0.02/0.20; RMSE 0.56/0.51/0.43 on a mean realized beta of 0.46. Instrument anatomy on armed days: SPY corr 0.45 (R2 0.20), IWM 0.45 (0.21), QQQ 0.40 (0.16).
findings.method: Split hedge PnL by sign of SPY day; decompose into beta_hat x mean(SPY) drift and residual; regress beta_hat on forward 21d realized beta.
findings.n: 392 armed days live; 2527 days for beta-quality
findings.robustness: Same asymmetry in every dial bucket and in the PIT window (armed sd 74.0 -> 72.6 bps).
findings.implication_for_sizing: (1) Use a 126d or shrunk beta, not 63d: 63d has zero predictive correlation exactly when armed. (2) The hedge is a bet that the dial's conditional SPY mean stays negative; it should be sized to the down-beta (~0.3-0.4x NAV), which is what 1.0x of a 126d/shrunk estimate roughly delivers, and never above 1.5x. (3) Do not describe or justify it as 'variance reduction'. (4) The up/down asymmetry means the book already has convexity at high dial; a cut (0.25x bands) removes that convexity while a hedge keeps it.
findings.caveat: Up/down betas from OLS on ~200 days per sign; the asymmetry is directionally stable but the magnitudes are +-0.1.

findings.claim: Hedge only the dip-buy family + OLV is the wrong target: at high dial the factor exposure migrates to LT Trend ST OS, 52wh Breakout and St OS Sznl, and the sub-book is a minority of both variance and SPY covariance there.
findings.numbers: Dip-buy family (WCDS, MonFri, Monday Dip, IOB, Monthly Weak Close, 3x Bear Fade) + OLV sub-book: share of book variance 36% overall, 25% at dial>=50, 15.6% at dial 65+; sub-book beta 0.14 / 0.14 / 0.11 vs rest-of-book beta 0.09 / 0.27 / 0.30 (rest R2 0.03 / 0.16 / 0.24). Per-strategy SPY covariance share on armed days (live 50/45): OLV 22% (active 45% of armed days), LT Trend 19% (active 18%), 52wh 18% (active 36%, Sharpe -1.8 while armed), St OS Sznl 10%, MonFri 5%, 3x Bear Fade 5%, ATR Gap 5%, Sector BO 4%, OVS 0.1%. Per-active-day betas at dial 65+: LTT 0.55 (down-beta 0.59), St OS 0.55 at 50+, 52wh 0.23 (R2 0.29 at 65+), OLV 0.11 (0.19 at 50+), OVS -0.01. Sub-book hedge replays: live 50/45 +$10k t 0.34; 65/60 +$21.8k t 1.15; PIT 50/45 +$65k t 2.24 (11/13 positive) vs whole-book +$104k t 1.68.
findings.method: Sub-book vs rest regressions by regime; covariance decomposition of book-SPY covariance on armed days; hedge grid rows with target=subbook.
findings.n: 2527 days live; 349 at dial>=50; 133 at 65+
findings.robustness: Ordering identical on VIX/drawdown slices (rest-of-book beta 0.22 at VIX<20 vs 0.06 at VIX>=25).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Target the WHOLE book's beta. If a partial target is wanted for operational reasons, the right sub-book is {OLV, LT Trend ST OS, 52wh Breakout, St OS Sznl}, which is 2/3 of armed-day covariance, not the FAMILY4 the frag bands already cut. Consistent with the baseline's finding that 52wh at dial>=50 (Sharpe -2.2, 125 active days) is an exit question; its 0.23 beta means the hedge covers only part of it.
findings.caveat: Strategy activity shares shift by regime, so covariance shares are partly a 'who is holding what' effect; still, that IS what the hedge must cover.

findings.claim: Instrument: SPY (ES/MES) is the right hedge vehicle; IWM's larger backtest PnL is the small-cap factor's negative drift over 2018-2026, not a better fit, and QQQ is the worst fit at every dial level.
findings.numbers: Book R2 by single factor: all (2527d) SPY 0.106 / QQQ 0.100 / IWM 0.081 / MOM 0.025; dial>=50 (349d) SPY 0.210 / QQQ 0.150 / IWM 0.231 / MOM 0.147; dial 65+ (133d) SPY 0.313 / QQQ 0.242 / IWM 0.286 / MOM 0.177; multi-factor R2 0.34 at 65+. Multi-factor loadings (SPY, QQQ-SPY, IWM-SPY, MOM) for the book at dial>=50: SPY 0.35, QQQ-SPY -0.17 (t -2.0), IWM-SPY +0.15 (t +2.8), MOM +0.10 (t +2.7); all-sample MOM loading 0.09 with t 8.1 (carriers per active day: OLV t 7.6, 3x Fade t 6.0, 52wh t 5.0, LTT t 4.6). Hedge grid dial 50/45, 63d: live SPY +$35k (t 0.72) / QQQ +$17k (0.43) / IWM +$105k (1.74) / adaptive-by-R2 +$50k (0.78); PIT SPY +$104k / QQQ +$74k / IWM +$120k / adaptive +$100k; IWM ann on armed days -31.9% vs SPY -9.7% (unarmed +21.4% vs +20.6%); armed-day R2 SPY 0.202 vs IWM 0.205; hedged maxDD SPY -8.12% vs IWM -8.57%.
findings.method: Single- and multi-factor OLS by regime; momentum factor = 12-1 cross-sectional, top/bottom quintile, equal-weight, monthly rebalance on the 915 sector_map names present in master_prices (ann 1.2%, vol 20.7%, corr(SPY) -0.08); hedge grid by instrument.
findings.n: 2527 sessions; 349 at dial>=50
findings.robustness: IWM's edge disappears once its drift is removed (same R2 as SPY); the QQQ inferiority holds in every regime and both vintages.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Hedge with ES/MES. Do not use NQ. Do not chase IWM/RTY: it would be a standing short-size-factor bet dressed as a hedge. Display the book's momentum loading on the hedge panel: at high dial ~15% of book variance is momentum-factor risk (a momentum-crash exposure the SPY hedge does not touch), carried by OLV/52wh/LTT/3x Fade.
findings.caveat: The momentum factor is built on today's survivors, which biases its short leg; loadings are more reliable than its own mean.

findings.claim: Effective N has been structurally higher since 2016 (more strategies live) and its worst collapses are composition events (one sleeve dominating), not correlation events the dial can see; correlation and beta rise with the number of simultaneously active strategies, and those are the book's best days.
findings.numbers: Rolling 126d effective N by year: 2010-2015 2.1-2.8 (3.1-5.6 active strategies), 2016-2026 3.1-4.4 (4.2-5.9 active). Lowest windows: 2014-10-23 eff N 1.06 (52wh era, corr 0.01, beta63 1.16), 2023-02-06 1.22 (corr 0.58), 2011-08-04 1.34, 2024-12-18 1.68 (dial 56). Spearman of rolling eff N with dial -0.02, with VIX +0.05; rolling beta63 with dial +0.21, with VIX -0.30. Signal-flow states (2010+): 0-2 strategies active (2626d) corr 0.006, beta 0.21, Sharpe 1.78, 6 bps/day; 3-4 active (929d) corr 0.07, beta 0.68, Sharpe 3.46, 26 bps/day; 5-6 active (92d) corr 0.15, beta 1.13, Sharpe 4.70, 58 bps/day, sd 197 bps; trailing-5d signal count >15 (174d) Sharpe 4.15, 44 bps/day.
findings.method: 126d rolling correlation/effective N in 5-day steps; 63d rolling book beta; Spearman vs lag-1 dial and VIX; daily stats by count of strategies with non-zero PnL and by trailing 5-day ledger signal count.
findings.n: 4174 sessions 2010+
findings.robustness: Consistent with the baseline's forecast table (signal density predicts both next-month vol and next-month mean).
findings.implication_for_sizing: No book-level de-risking on correlation spikes or on multi-strategy clusters: the high-beta, high-correlation cluster days are the high-Sharpe days (composition = many dip-buys long into a washout). The only correlation-aware control that does not throw away edge is the dial-armed hedge, which fires in the complacent state before the cluster, not during it. Display eff N and n_active on the hedge panel; do not size on them.
findings.caveat: Effective N is computed on strategies active >10% of the window; low-activity strategies (3x Leader Gap Fade, Monthly Weak Close, Monday Dip) are invisible to it.

findings.claim: A VIX-gated variant of the dial hedge (arm only when dial>=50 AND VIX<20; release when VIX spikes or dial<45) is the strongest specification on PIT and matches the mechanism in Finding 2, but it was found after looking at the data and must be pre-registered rather than adopted.
findings.numbers: PIT: baseline 50/45 +$104k t 1.68, 10/13 positive; + VIX<20 arming gate +$118.5k t 1.97 (10/12); + gate and release at VIX>=25 +$102k t 2.81 (11/12 positive, LOYO 8/9), armed days 479; + gate and release at VIX>=30 +$129k t 2.03, Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.06. Live: baseline +$35k t 0.72; gate + release VIX>=30 +$57.7k t 0.97 (7/10); gate + release VIX>=25 +$28.5k t 0.71 (5 false alarms). VIX-percentile gate (pctile<60, release >=90): PIT +$62k t 1.30, live +$3k t 0.08 (worse). SPY-within-3%-of-high gate: no change live, PIT +$80k t 1.34. Release on SPY dd<-7%: PIT +$83k t 1.49, live +$30k t 0.60. 65/60 + VIX gate/release 25: PIT +$59k t 2.48 (6/8), live +$45k t 1.56 (4/7).
findings.method: Hysteresis state machine with an entry gate and a forced-release trigger, on both vintages, same friction and beta as the primary.
findings.n: 10-13 episodes per variant
findings.robustness: Improves clustered t on PIT in every VIX-level variant but the live-vintage improvement is small and the percentile form is worse; 12 variants were looked at, so the best t (2.81) carries selection.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Write it into P1 as the SECOND-STAGE sensitivity, decision rule fixed now: adopt the VIX<20 arming gate with release at VIX>=30 only if, on the next two out-of-sample armed episodes, it does not underperform the plain 50/45 rule. Intuition supports it (the book's dip-buys want the selloff once it arrives; the hedge should be off by then), which is why it is worth registering, not why it should ship.
findings.caveat: In-sample refinement over 12 variants; treat every t here as inflated by at least one unit.

findings.claim: Calendar seasonality of the market factor exists but is too thin to size on: the book's downside beta and worst Sharpe both cluster in October and January, and its highest beta in December.
findings.numbers: By month (2010+, ~340-380 days each): beta to SPY Dec 0.55 (R2 0.30), Jan 0.49 (down-beta 0.57, Sharpe 1.52), Oct 0.34 (R2 0.23, down-beta 0.38, Sharpe 0.85, 3.9 bps/day), Apr 0.33; lowest Jun 0.14 (Sharpe 1.47), May 0.20, Aug 0.20. Book Sharpe by month: Nov 3.84, Mar 3.18, Feb 3.17, Dec 2.66, May 2.42 vs Oct 0.85, Jun 1.47, Jan 1.52, Aug 1.67. Avg pairwise corr peaks Mar 0.093, Dec 0.073, Nov 0.067 (MonFri-WCDS 0.45 in November, 52wh-IOB 0.43 in October).
findings.method: Regime tables keyed on calendar month, 2010+.
findings.n: ~360 days per month, 16 years
findings.robustness: Not tested out of sample; October's Sharpe is a 2014/2018/2023 story.
findings.implication_for_sizing: No monthly sizing rule from this. If a calendar overlay is ever wanted it belongs on the hedge (a lower arming threshold in Oct/Jan) and needs its own prereg; the dial already fired in Q4-2018 and Dec-2021 without help.
findings.caveat: 16 observations per month; the seasonal-flow analyst's work is the right place for calendar conclusions.

recommendations.change: Promote P1 (dial-armed book beta hedge) from pre-registration to paper-track-then-ship, since it passes the written ship rule on the PIT vintage: threshold 50 arm / 45 release (NOT 65/60, which is t 0.99 on PIT and lives on Feb-2020), target = whole book, instrument = ES/MES, hedge ratio 1.0x, beta = 126d lag-1 OLS (or 0.5x63d + 0.5xexpanding shrunk), clipped [-1, 2], refreshed daily, 2 bps friction per arm event.
recommendations.rule: armed_t = hysteresis(dial_lag1 >= 50 arm, < 45 release); MES contracts = beta_126 x NAV / (50 x ES); release fully when dial < 45; no partial ratios above 1.0x; log every arm/release on the hedge panel with beta_126, beta_63 and the armed-day SPY drift to date.
recommendations.expected_effect: PIT replay 2018-2026: +$104k on flat $750k over 544 armed days (13 episodes, 10 positive, clustered t 1.68), Sharpe 2.90 -> 3.04, maxDD -8.32% -> -8.13%; with 126d beta +$110k, Sharpe 3.07, maxDD -7.89%. Live-vintage: +$35k, Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.84. Expect ~1.3 episodes/yr, about +$8k per episode, calm carry limited to false alarms (~4 in 10 episodes, ~-$5k/yr).
recommendations.confidence: moderate: passes PIT with margin on t (1.68 vs 1.0), bootstrap P(<=0) 0.046, placebo rank 1.000, but 13 episodes and drift-driven

recommendations.change: Do NOT build or keep any VIX-armed, VIX-percentile-armed, or drawdown-armed hedge or beta cut, and do not use realized vol as a stand-in for the dial anywhere in sizing.
recommendations.rule: Negative result to codify beside the book-wide throttle: VIX>=25/20 hedge -$158.5k (0 of 15 episodes positive, t -3.85); VIX pctile 80/60 -$154k; SPY dd<-5%/-3% -$139k; always-hedged -$478k and maxDD -8.3% -> -11.5%.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids a -$14k to -$16k per year drag with the wrong sign in 13-14 of 14-15 episodes; the book's beta is 0.17 and its Sharpe 3.8 when VIX>30.

recommendations.change: Hedge the whole book, not the dip-buy family + OLV; if a partial target is ever wanted, define it as {OLV, LT Trend ST OS, 52wh Breakout, St OS Sznl}.
recommendations.rule: Target series for beta = flat-basis total book MTM. Sub-book (FAMILY4 + Monthly Weak Close + 3x Bear Fade + OLV) is 15.6% of book variance and beta 0.11 at dial 65+ while the rest carries beta 0.30; the four named strategies hold ~69% of armed-day SPY covariance.
recommendations.expected_effect: Sub-book hedge earns roughly half to one third of the whole-book hedge (live 50/45 +$10k vs +$35k; PIT +$65k vs +$104k) for the same operational cost.

recommendations.change: Add a second-stage sensitivity to the P1 protocol, decision rule fixed before the next episode: arming gate dial>=50 AND VIX<20 with forced release at VIX>=30 (or dial<45).
recommendations.rule: Adopt only if it is not worse than plain 50/45 across the next two out-of-sample armed episodes; in-sample PIT +$129k t 2.03 vs +$104k t 1.68, live +$58k t 0.97 vs +$35k t 0.72.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes the hedge during the post-spike phase where the book's beta collapses and its edge peaks; expected to trim false-alarm cost, not to add large PnL.

recommendations.change: Replace the 63d beta in P1 with 126d (or the shrunk blend) and state the hedge in down-beta terms on the panel.
recommendations.rule: corr(beta_hat, realized next-21d beta) at dial>=50: 63d 0.02, 42d -0.04, 126d 0.20; RMSE 0.51 vs 0.43. Realized armed beta 0.40 with up-day 0.50 / down-day 0.27.
recommendations.expected_effect: Same PnL (PIT 126d +$110k vs 63d +$104k) with better maxDD (-7.89% vs -8.13%) and fewer 2017-09-style oversized arms (beta_hat 1.02 that episode).

recommendations.change: Hedge-panel additions (display only): rolling 126d book beta and its down/up split, effective N (126d) and number of active strategies, the book's momentum-factor loading, and per-strategy share of SPY covariance while armed.
recommendations.rule: None of these size anything; the momentum loading (~15% of book variance at dial>=50, carriers OLV/52wh/LTT/3x Fade) is the one factor the SPY hedge does not cover.
recommendations.expected_effect: Makes the size of the single market bet and the un-hedged momentum-crash exposure visible before the hedge is placed.

recommendations.change: Once the hedge is live, re-open the FAMILY4 / 3x Bear / Monthly Weak Close 0.25x band at dial>=50 as a prereg question scored on HEDGED returns (companion to P2).
recommendations.rule: The book at high dial has beta_up 0.79 vs beta_down 0.26; a cut removes that convexity, a hedge keeps it. Decision rule to be written before the run; nothing changes now.
recommendations.expected_effect: Unknown; flagged because the two controls act on the same state and the evidence base for the cut (clustered t -1.96 PIT) is only one notch stronger than the hedge's.

recommendations.change: No book-level scalar, no correlation-spike de-risking, no signal-cluster throttle, and no calendar-month sizing rule.
recommendations.rule: Cluster days (5-6 strategies active) have beta 1.13 and Sharpe 4.7; effective-N collapses are composition events uncorrelated with the dial (Spearman -0.02); month cells are 16 observations each.
recommendations.expected_effect: Preserves the days that carry the book's edge; consistent with the nine dead overlays in the baseline.

negative_results: VIX-level arming (>=25 rel 20) of a beta hedge: -$158.5k over 2016-2026 on flat $750k, 0 of 15 episodes positive, clustered t -3.85, Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.66. Dead.
VIX trailing-252d percentile arming (>=80 rel 60): -$154k, 3 of 21 episodes positive, t -2.11. Dead.
SPY drawdown arming (dd < -5% rel > -3%): -$139k, 2 of 14 episodes positive, t -2.12. Dead.

Always-hedged book beta: -$478k (-2.5 bps/day), Sharpe 2.77 -> 2.42, maxDD -8.3% -> -11.5%. The book's embedded beta is worth +3.2 bps/day in calm tape; only remove it when the dial says the drift has turned.
Threshold 65/60 as the primary arming level: PIT t 0.99 (fails the >=1.0 leg), drop-best-episode t 0.37, bootstrap P(<=0) 0.134; it is a Feb-2020 result. 50/45 dominates on PIT (t 1.68).

Hedge the dip-buy family + OLV only: earns one third to two thirds of the whole-book hedge (live +$10k vs +$35k at 50/45) because the factor exposure at high dial sits in LT Trend / 52wh / St OS Sznl, not in the family.
QQQ as the hedge instrument: lowest R2 in every regime (0.15 at dial>=50 vs SPY 0.21 / IWM 0.23) and half the hedge PnL of SPY.

IWM as the hedge instrument on PnL grounds: its extra +$70k is the small-cap factor's -31.9% annualized drift on armed days, not a better fit (armed-day R2 0.205 vs SPY 0.202) and it worsens hedged maxDD (-8.57% vs -8.12%).
Hedge ratios above 1.0x of beta_hat: Sharpe falls (live 1.5x 2.81, 2x 2.75 vs 2.84) and maxDD widens to -10.2% at 2x.
42d and 63d rolling betas as the hedge ratio: zero predictive correlation with realized forward beta on dial>=50 days (0.02 and -0.04); 126d (0.20) or a shrunk blend is the usable estimator.

Correlation-spike or effective-N de-risking: rolling eff N is uncorrelated with the dial (Spearman -0.02) and with VIX (+0.05); its lows are single-sleeve dominance events (2014-10 eff N 1.06) with no forward content. Not a control.
Signal-cluster throttling: days with 5-6 active strategies have beta 1.13 but Sharpe 4.7 and 58 bps/day; trailing-5d signal count > 15 has Sharpe 4.15. Throttling clusters removes the best days.
VIX-percentile gate on the dial hedge (pctile < 60 arm, >= 90 release): live +$3k t 0.08, worse than the plain rule; the VIX-level gate is the only gate form that helped.
Calendar-month beta/Sharpe seasonality as a sizing rule: 16 observations per month; October (Sharpe 0.85, R2 0.23) and January (down-beta 0.57) are suggestive but untestable here.
caveats: Basis and window: all dollars flat $750k; the per-strategy daily payload (dist/data/strategy_daily.json) ends 2026-08-07, so the live Aug-2026 high-dial episode is only 6 armed days (-$6k) and truncated; the ledger runs to 2026-08-28 but was not used for daily MTM.

Dial vintages: the 'live' series is current-weights and rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage (drift up to ~7 points on the 63d column) with calibration lookahead on SPY forward returns; the PIT series (2018-01-02..2026-07-02) is rebuilt with the scratch/pit_reestimate.py method from the July-2026 signal pickle and cures weight lookahead only, not signal-definition lookahead. PIT 2018 is scored by a single-signal vintage (only Seasonal Rank Divergence had a 63d edge) and is the noisiest year; PIT is >=50 on 22.9% of days vs 15.4% live (corr 0.89, agreement 88%).

Episode counts are small everywhere that matters: 7-13 armed episodes per rule, 133 days at dial 65+, and the hedge's PnL is drift-driven (SPY conditional mean in the armed state), so its value depends on the dial's SPY forecast surviving out of sample. The clustered t, bootstrap, drop-best and placebo statistics are the honest measures; the full-sample Sharpe deltas (+0.07 to +0.15) are small by construction because armed days are 15-25% of the sample.

Hedge mechanics are idealized: beta_hat rebalanced daily at zero cost, 2 bps per arm event only, no futures basis/roll/margin, SPY total-return proxy for ES, no intraday timing. A live MES implementation will lose a few bps per episode more.
The momentum factor is built from today's sector_map survivors (915 names), so its short leg and its mean are survivorship-biased; use its loadings, not its return.

Regime tables use overlapping daily observations; t-statistics on multi-factor loadings are unclustered and overstate significance for the high-dial cells. The correlation and beta magnitudes are the load-bearing numbers, the t's are indicative.

The refined VIX-gated arming rules (Finding 8) were found after inspecting Finding 2 and 12 variants were examined; they are pre-registration candidates and every t there should be read as inflated by about one unit.

Every hedge replay is on the CURRENT ledger, which already contains the 0.25x FAMILY4 bands at dial>=50 and the other overlays; the 'hedge vs cut' comparison the baseline plan argues for was not run here because the bands cannot be undone on the daily series (it needs an engine rerun with frag bands off).

Other analysts are writing into the same scratch folder (cycle_macro_*, flow_conditional_*, seasonality_flow_*, signal_quality_*, within_strategy_adds_*); only the cross_strategy_regime_* files are this study's. No repo code, config, tests or committed data were modified and nothing was committed.

findings.claim: No strategy-by-calendar cell in the ledger survives multiple-comparison correction on the year-clustered test. Calendar seasonality of per-trade QUALITY (avgR, R per unit risk) is not evidenced anywhere in the book once episodes and years are treated as the unit.
findings.numbers: 1,012 trade-level cells tested (15 strategies + book x 10 dimensions; month 192 cells, dow 80, wom 64, holiday 48, opex 48, quarter 64, half 32, TOM 32, earnings-season 64). Year-paired BH-FDR 10% survivors: ZERO in every dimension family (min q = 0.27, book earnings-season). Bonferroni 5%: zero. Episode-clustered FDR survivors: 2, both artefacts (3x Bear Fade 'holiday=none' avgR 0.78 vs -2.69 on a 2-trade complement; Sector BO same, -1.22 on 2 trades). Nominal p<0.05 on BOTH tests with N>=15: only 5 cells (book earnings-season on/off; LT Trend ST OS Fri 0.69 vs 0.26 N=36; LT Trend Tue -0.05 vs 0.38 N=35; MonFri W4+ 0.71 vs 0.34 N=100), i.e. the ~5% false-positive count expected under the null.
findings.method: OVS scale-out tranches collapsed to one row per fill (4,696 -> 3,483). Each cell vs its within-strategy complement: (a) OLS on a cell dummy with cluster-robust SE, clusters = signal episodes separated by >=5 sessions within strategy (book: episodes nested in strategy); (b) year-paired t on cell-minus-complement mean per year. BH-FDR and Bonferroni within each dimension family across strategies+book, and separately within (dimension, strategy).
findings.n: 3,483 fills 2003-01..2026-08; per-strategy N from 14 (Monthly Weak Close) to 1,182 (OVS fills); years 24
findings.robustness: Both clustering schemes agree that nothing survives. Per-strategy month grids (avgR and flow ratio) are in seasonality_flow_cells.json; the largest nominal month cells (OLV Aug 0.35 vs 0.86 N=61; LT Trend Jun 0.08 vs 0.36 N=33; 52wh Oct 0.87 vs 0.46 N=40; IOB Mar 0.69 vs 0.30 N=36) have year-paired p of 0.22 to 0.97.
findings.implication_for_sizing: A strategy x month (or any calendar) multiplier table has no evidentiary basis. Any calendar cell proposed in the plan must be argued from an outside base rate, not from these tables, and even then it fails the replay (next findings).
findings.caveat: Small strategies (3x fades, St OS Sznl, Sector BO, Monthly Weak Close) have 1-14 trades per month cell; absence of evidence there is a power statement, not a negative result.

findings.claim: Fitted calendar-conditional sizing multipliers do not improve the book out of sample in any form, and barely in-sample: the calendar carries almost no exploitable information about expected R.
findings.numbers: trade_mtm replay, 2010-2026 OOS, multipliers = shrunk cell/overall avgR ratio (N0=30, clip 0.5-1.5): strat x month WALK-FORWARD dPnL +2.1%, dSharpe +0.040 (vol-matched +0.040), maxDD +0.10 pt, 10/17 years better, yearly-diff t=1.01; LOYO dPnL -0.9%, dSharpe -0.056, maxDD 2.6 pts WORSE, 7/17 years. IN-SAMPLE (fit on all, apply to all) dPnL +1.0%, dSharpe -0.030, maxDD -2.5 pts. Book x month WF +3.0% / +0.041 / 12 of 17, LOYO -0.046 Sharpe. strat x quarter WF -2.8% / -0.025; strat x half WF -3.1% / -0.036; book half WF -0.5% / +0.031; strat x earnings-season WF -1.8% / -0.006 (4/17 years); strat x opex WF 0.0% / +0.016; strat x TOM WF -1.0% / -0.057; strat x dow WF -0.7% / -0.018. Kelly-form (mu/sigma^2 cells) strat x month WF +4.8% PnL / +0.049 Sharpe, LOYO -0.076.
findings.method: Every trade's daily MTM vector (dist/data/trade_mtm.json, flat $750k) scaled by a multiplier keyed on (strategy, calendar cell of the signal date); book re-summed daily; walk-forward fits on signal years < Y, LOYO on years != Y, Y=2010..2026; overlays also vol-matched to baseline; per-year PnL comparison.
findings.n: 4,696 ledger trades / 3,483 fills; 17 OOS years; baseline 2010-2026 Sharpe 2.05, maxDD -12%
findings.robustness: Direction flips between WF and LOYO for month; every other dimension is <= baseline in both designs; no design clears the plan's own gate (PnL/maxDD +10%, worst year > -15%): best worst-year ratio 0.66-0.78.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not add a calendar layer to the sizing chain. The +2-5% WF PnL from month multipliers is within noise (t 1.0-2.1 on 17 years) and reverses under LOYO.
findings.caveat: Per-strategy 250 bps/day cap and P2 cap interactions are not replayed; multipliers > 1 would bind them more, so any raise is an upper bound. Baseline trade_mtm sum ($4.04M) is 2.3% below the ledger PnL sum ($4.14M) - vectors are reconciled per trade per CLAUDE.md, the gap is treated as rounding and affects levels, not comparisons.

findings.claim: Book daily VARIANCE is genuinely seasonal, but so is the mean, and the two move together because both are driven by open risk (signal flow). The growth-optimal size (mu/sigma^2) is flat across seasons; nothing is left to size.
findings.numbers: Daily basis (flat $750k, 2003-2026): May-Oct sd 63.0 bps/day vs Nov-Apr 83.0 (ratio 0.76; year-paired t=-3.19 p=0.004; Levene p<0.001; sd lower in 19/24 summers); mean 7.06 vs 11.58 bps (t=-2.67, p=0.014; lower in 15/24). Sharpe 1.78 vs 2.22. Kelly ratio May-Oct/Nov-Apr = 1.06 pooled, median across years 1.03. By month: sd ranges 52 (Aug) to 97 (Jan); Aug sd ratio 0.70 (t=-5.67), May 0.74 (t=-3.91), Jul 0.94 (t=-2.33), Sep 0.84 (t=-2.34), Jun 0.84 (t=-2.57); mean open risk 104-141 bps in May-Oct vs 150-206 bps Nov-Jan. Spearman(month sd, month open risk) = 0.77 (p=0.003); log-log elasticity of monthly sd to open risk = 0.51 (legs add in quadrature). After controlling for open risk, only May has a residual (t=-2.49); all other months |t|<1.6.
findings.method: Book and per-strategy daily MTM from strategy_daily.json; cells vs complement with year-paired t on mean and on sd, Levene on returns; open legs and open risk rebuilt from the ledger by day; year-month regression of log(sd) on log(open risk) with residuals by month.
findings.n: 5,925 sessions, 24 years
findings.robustness: Persistence of the within-year month-vol ranking across years is near zero (mean pairwise Spearman of month-sd ranks: book 0.06, 52wh 0.11, OVS -0.04, MonFri -0.08), i.e. WHICH months are wild changes year to year; only the summer-vs-winter level split is stable. Per-strategy: 52wh Nov-Apr Sharpe 1.34 vs May-Oct 0.75 (t=2.1), OVS 1.52 vs 0.66 (t=1.9), ATR Ext 2.18 vs 0.46 (t=2.2), WCDS 1.30 vs 0.77 (t=2.1), OLV the opposite 0.79 vs 1.26 (n.s.).
findings.implication_for_sizing: The seasonal book vol is what ATR sizing plus signal density already produces; a vol-target or season multiplier would cut size exactly when the book is about to earn (the study-1 result that sig5 predicts both vol and mean, restated on the calendar). Priors replay: May-Oct 0.75x -11% PnL with maxDD unchanged (1/24 years better); Nov-Apr 1.25x +14% PnL but Sharpe -0.033, maxDD -3.0 pts, PnL/maxDD -9%.
findings.caveat: Daily-basis cells attribute PnL to the MTM date, sizing keys on the signal date; long-hold strategies (52wh 63d) blur the two.

findings.claim: The dip-buy family is weaker in May-Oct in every member, consistent with the Bouman-Jacobsen 'sell in May' base rate, while the rest of the book shows the opposite sign. It is a real-looking family effect that still does not justify a cut: the summer cell earns positive R per risk and the gap only appeared after 2013.
findings.numbers: Dip-buy core (WCDS, IOB, Monday Dip, MonFri, St OS Sznl, Monthly Weak Close): May-Oct avgR 0.301 (R/risk 0.298, N=486) vs Nov-Apr 0.494 (R/risk 0.476, N=600); episode-clustered t=-2.12 p=0.035 (287 episodes); year-paired t=-1.79 p=0.086 (24 years); LOYO gap [-0.25, -0.14], all negative; 6/6 strategies same sign (IOB -0.22, Monday Dip -0.32, MWC -0.35, MonFri -0.07, St OS -0.23, WCDS -0.33). Extended family (+52wh, LT Trend): 8/8 same sign, t_ep=-2.38. Non-family control (OVS, OLV, fades, ATR, Sector BO): May-Oct 0.550 vs 0.484, LOYO [+0.00, +0.12]. By month for dip-buys: Sep R/risk 0.03 (N=70, PnL $6.8k), May 0.34, Oct 0.24, Jun 0.30, Jul 0.55, Aug 0.37. Expanding-window family gap was POSITIVE through 2013 (+0.13 through 2009, +0.02 through 2012) and only negative from 2014 (-0.18 through 2025). Sleeve daily basis: Kelly ratio May-Oct/Nov-Apr 0.77 (Sharpe 1.04 vs 1.65). Replays (trade_mtm, 2003-2026): dip 0.75x May-Oct dPnL -3.1%, dSharpe -0.011, maxDD 0.00, 6/24 years better; 0.5x -6.3%/-0.030; Nov-Apr 1.25x +1.6% PnL, Sharpe -0.056, maxDD -1.4 pts; walk-forward self-gated 0.75x (on only when the through-Y-1 gap < -0.10: fires 2020, 2024-26) dPnL -0.35%, dSharpe -0.002.
findings.method: Pooled family test with episode-clustered and year-paired t, LOYO of the family gap, per-strategy sign count, non-family control, sub-window scan (Jun-Sep, Jul-Sep, Aug-Sep all weaker than May-Oct itself), trade_mtm replays incl. a walk-forward gated form.
findings.n: 1,086 dip-buy fills, 287 episodes, 24 years
findings.robustness: Survives LOYO and the control comparison; does NOT survive FDR in the strategy-level tables (each member p 0.1-0.4) and is not stable across eras (sign flipped around 2013). Sub-windows narrower than May-Oct are all weaker (Jun-Sep t_ep=-0.84), which argues against a sharp calendar mechanism.
findings.implication_for_sizing: No cut: with the book at ~6% of Kelly (plan section 1) growth is linear in size and a cell with R/risk +0.30 should keep full size; the replay confirms a cut is pure PnL loss with no drawdown benefit. September dip-buys (R/risk 0.03) are the only zero-expectancy cell; list it as a watch item, not a rule. If the plan wants a seasonal appetite tilt anywhere, this family/summer cell is the only one with both an outside base rate and internal evidence; the honest form is 'no boost in Nov-Apr for dip-buys unless GRM rises book-wide'.
findings.caveat: Post-2013 emergence means 12 years of evidence, not 24; the flat-dollar sizing basis and the survivorship of the overflow tier (St OS Sznl overflow rows) both flatter the winter cell more than the summer cell.

findings.claim: Signal FLOW state carries more information than the calendar: OVS's multi-signal days are its best days, single-signal days its worst, and the same holds for the book. This is the one 'flow high AND quality good' cell that survives correction. There is no 'crowded selloff' cell where high flow meets poor quality.
findings.numbers: OVS same-day signal count (fills, tranche-collapsed): 1 signal avgR 0.193 (N=436), 2: 0.334 (208 fills/104 days), 3-4: 0.20 (175), 5-6: 0.32 (103/19 days), 7-9: 0.50 (52/7), 10-15: 0.59 (58/5), 16+: 0.84 (238/7 days). 5+ vs <5: 0.648 vs 0.230, sdR 0.91 vs 1.14, R/risk 0.52 vs ~0.30; episode-clustered t=4.84, q=0.002 (29 episodes, 38 days); 1-signal days t=-3.38 q=0.012. LOYO gap never below +0.335 (max 0.460); 5+ cell avgR > 0 in 10/11 years (2026: -0.17 on 18 fills). Ledger risk on 5+ days median 93 bps, max 210 - none at the 250 cap, i.e. the P2 12-bps rows and the P2 aggregate cap, not the per-strategy cap, keep these days small. OLV same-day 5+ avgR 1.35 (N=33) vs 0.60 solo (N=175). Book: 5+ signals 0.70 vs 0.42 (q=0.012); 1 signal 0.385 vs 0.546 (q=0.063). Trailing-21-session flow relative to the strategy's expanding norm, book: low tercile avgR 0.34 vs 0.53 (t_ep=-3.05, q=0.094), high 0.55. Per strategy the trailing-count pattern is mixed: 52wh falls with prior signals (0.63/0.55/0.39/0.34 at 0/1-2/3-5/6+ prior, N=13 in 6+, the plan's stack finding), OLV rises (0.47/0.63/1.02/0.84), IOB 6+ 0.78 (N=15), LT Trend 6+ 0.23. Fitted strat x trailing-count multiplier: WF dPnL +2.2% / dSharpe -0.052; LOYO -2.6% / -0.042.
findings.method: Per-strategy same-day count and trailing 5/21-session counts (ex same day) from signal dates; episode-clustered dummy tests with FDR per dimension; LOYO of the OVS cluster gap; per-day and per-year listings; trade_mtm walk-forward of a flow multiplier.
findings.n: OVS 1,182 fills / 38 cluster days / 29 episodes; book 3,483 fills
findings.robustness: OVS cluster cell is episode-concentrated (16+ signal days = 7 dates: 2009-01-05, 2009-05-29, 2020-06-04/05, 2022-11-10, 2023-02-01, 2023-12-13) but LOYO-stable and not cap-bound. The 2026 cluster days (Feb 3, Jun 24) were losers (-0.90, -1.10). A generic fitted flow multiplier fails OOS because the per-strategy patterns disagree in sign.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Evidence supports NOT de-rating OVS on high-signal days (the bear-fade same_day_signal_derate logic must not be generalised to OVS) and is a candidate for a pre-registered OVS cluster-day tilt (e.g. 1.25x when same-day OVS count >= 5, or lifting the P2 aggregate cap on those days), gated on episode count and P1/P2 split; it is not shippable from this study. No book-level flow multiplier.
findings.caveat: Same-day count is only known at the PM scan close, which is fine for OVS (T+1 open gate), but P1/P2 composition of cluster days was not separated here; the plan's L2 table already shows OVS 13+ legs at implied rho ~0.

findings.claim: Earnings season is a BETTER period for every strategy after the existing blackouts, the opposite of the 'reduce single-stock risk into earnings' base rate; the blackout/override machinery has already removed the bad cell.
findings.numbers: Data-driven season (top-tercile weeks of +-5-session report counts within year): book avgR 0.560 (N=1,021) vs 0.430 off (N=2,462), R/risk 0.55 vs 0.40; episode t=1.97 p=0.049, year-paired t=2.44 p=0.023, FDR q=0.27 (not surviving). Single-stock strategies (OVS, OLV, LT Trend, 52wh, St OS, ATR Ext, WCDS): 0.520 vs 0.412, 7/7 same sign, LOYO [+0.06, +0.15], t_yr=1.49. Index/ETF strategies: 0.644 vs 0.479, 7/8 same sign, LOYO [+0.12, +0.22]. Flow in season is LOWER (book flow ratio 0.89; OVS 0.69, LT Trend 0.48) because of the blackouts. Daily basis: 52wh in-season Sharpe 1.17 vs 0.85 (t=2.9, p=0.008), LT Trend 0.83 vs 1.21 (t=-2.5), St OS Sznl 1.13 vs 0.04 (t=2.9). Replays: single-stock 0.75x in season dPnL -7.1%, Sharpe -0.03, 0-1 of 17-24 years better; 1.25x +7.1% PnL, vol-matched Sharpe +0.013, maxDD -1.0 pt, 23/24 years better on PnL. Fixed calendar season (days 11-50 of quarter) shows the same sign, weaker (0.477 vs 0.463).
findings.method: Season flag from data/earnings_calendar.parquet counts; per-strategy and pooled family tests (episode-clustered, year-paired, LOYO); trade_mtm replays of +-25% tilts.
findings.n: 1,021 in-season fills, 24 years
findings.robustness: Consistent sign across 14/15 strategies and both season definitions; magnitude modest; not FDR-surviving in the family; matches the earnings-announcement-premium literature (Frazzini-Lamont, Savor-Wilson) as an outside base rate.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not add any earnings-season haircut beyond the existing OVS +-10td blackout and the OLV/St OS Sznl per-name overrides. A 1.25x in-season tilt adds PnL almost linearly with ~zero Sharpe change, which is the same argument as raising GRM and belongs at L4, not in a calendar rule.
findings.caveat: Season is defined from the current earnings calendar (FMP backfill) and is not point-in-time; the per-name blackouts make in-season trades a selected sample (names without a print in the window).

findings.claim: Signal FLOW itself is seasonal for several strategies, mostly structurally (filters), and the book's flow peaks in Dec/Jan/Jun and troughs in Jul; quality in the high-flow months is average, not poor.
findings.numbers: Year-paired normalized monthly shares, FDR 10% survivors: OVS Jul flow 0.48x (4/23 years above even, q=0.005), OVS Oct 0.41x (q=0.024), WCDS Dec 2.22x (16/20 years, q=0.069), WCDS Feb 0.22x, WCDS Aug 0.34x, OLV Dec 0.20x (q=0.005), LT Trend Nov 0.16x, 52wh Sep 0.46x and Dec 0.48x, MonFri Sep 0.52x, book Jul 0.70x (5/24 years above even, q=0.079). Book flow ratios: Dec 1.50 (OVS Dec 1.88x, N=198), Jan 1.26, Jun 1.27, Jul 0.79, Aug 0.81, Sep 0.83, Oct 0.83. Quality in the high-flow months: book Dec avgR 0.45 (R/risk 0.41), Jan 0.49 (0.46), Jun 0.45 (0.32), vs 0.47 overall; OVS Dec 0.43, Jan 0.30, Jun 0.42 vs 0.37 overall. 'Flow high + quality poor' screen (flow >1.25, avgR < rest - 0.15, N>=10): OLV Aug (2.1x flow, 0.35 vs 0.86, N=61, 12 yrs, p_year 0.59, still +$28.8k), LT Trend Jun (1.6x, 0.08 vs 0.36, N=33, p 0.97), LT Trend Mar, ATR Ext Jan, Monday Dip Apr, Sector BO Apr - none below p 0.19 year-paired; replays OLV Aug 0.5x -0.9% PnL / -0.011 Sharpe, LT Trend Jun 0.5x +0.3% / +0.011 (noise). 'Flow high + quality good': 52wh Oct (1.8x, 0.87 vs 0.46, N=40, p 0.46), OLV Jan (1.7x, 1.17 vs 0.70, N=43), IOB Mar (1.4x, 0.69 vs 0.30, N=36), OLV Jul, LT Trend Dec - all p_year > 0.2; 52wh Oct 1.5x replay +1.1% PnL, Sharpe -0.001.
findings.method: Monthly signal counts per strategy-year normalized to the year's total, cell vs rest-of-year paired by year, BH-FDR across 180 cells; quality screens from the trade-level cell table; trade_mtm replays of the named cells.
findings.n: 3,483 fills; 15 strategies x 12 months
findings.robustness: Flow seasonality survivors are all explainable by filter structure (seasonal-rank filters in WCDS/St OS/LT Trend, the OVS blackout removing July/October report windows, OLV's 200-SMA gate in year-end tape) rather than by market seasonality.
findings.implication_for_sizing: There is no crowded-month cell to de-rate: where flow is high the marginal signal is average, where flow is high and quality looks good it does not replicate across years. Signal flow matters as a SAME-DAY state (finding 5), not as a month.
findings.caveat: Flow ratios use the strategy's own active span as the denominator; strategies added recently (3x fades, MWC) have 1-7 years and are excluded from the significance table when < 4 years.

findings.claim: January is the book's highest-variance month and hosts a disproportionate share of drawdown troughs, but the excess variance is episodic rather than persistent, and per-trade quality in January is normal. December's lower trade-R variance is a composition effect (OVS share).
findings.numbers: Book daily Jan sd 96.5 bps (ratio 1.36 vs rest; Levene p<0.001) with mean 7.4 bps, Sharpe 1.22, worst day -4.89%, CVaR5 -222 bps, Kelly ratio 0.43 vs rest; open risk 202 bps (highest). But year-paired sd t=1.06 (p=0.30): only 8/24 Januaries exceed 1.3x the rest-of-year sd (2006, 2008, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2021, 2022, 2025), median ratio 0.99. Drawdown troughs >2% NAV by month: Feb 13, Mar 11, Jun 11, Jan 9, Oct 9, Apr 9; Sep only 3. Worst declustered 21-day windows end in Feb-2014, Jan-2008, Oct-2014, Aug-2015, Jun-2006, Oct-2018, Mar-2007, Jan-2015. Trade-level Jan avgR 0.49 (N=350, R/risk 0.46), i.e. average. December trade-level sdR 1.15 vs 1.39 (Levene q=0.044, year-paired t=-2.4) but OVS is 46.5% of December signals vs 36.5% overall; within-strategy standardized R: Dec sd 0.935 vs 1.006, Levene p=0.064; LT Trend Dec sdR 0.45 vs 0.95 (N=35, p=0.003) is the only within-strategy piece. Dec 1.25x replay: +2.8% PnL, Sharpe +0.003, maxDD -0.3 pt, PnL/maxDD +0.4%.
findings.method: Year-by-year January sd vs rest-of-year; drawdown trough dating on the cumulative flat book; composition check by OVS share and within-strategy standardized R.
findings.n: 24 Januaries; 426 December fills
findings.robustness: Levene (pooled) and year-paired tests disagree for January, which is the signature of a few extreme years, not a seasonal parameter.
findings.implication_for_sizing: No January de-rate and no December up-size: the January tail is dial/episode territory (2008, 2015, 2016, 2021, 2022 all had high open risk into a selloff), which is the L3 hedge question, not a calendar one.
findings.caveat: The trough histogram counts episodes, so Feb/Mar dominance partly reflects January-started drawdowns bottoming a month later.

findings.claim: Friday mark-to-market is weak for the book, consistently across years, but it is a holding-day effect, half structural, and not a signal-date sizing lever.
findings.numbers: Book Friday 3.62 bps/day vs 10.28 other days (sd 66 vs 74), year-paired t=-3.23, Friday worse in 21/24 years (q=0.13 in the dow family). By strategy (Fri vs other, bps/day of NAV): MonFri Reversion -0.06 vs 1.40 (t=-5.9, structurally near-flat on Fridays: fri sd 2.6 vs 16.8), Monday Dip 0.00 vs 0.43 (structural zero), OVS 0.13 vs 1.61 (t=-2.33, 16/24 years), OLV 0.04 vs 1.32 (t=-1.85), IOB 0.06 vs 0.86 (t=-1.64), 52wh 0.75 vs 1.30 (n.s.). Signal-date view: Friday-signal trades avgR 0.564 vs 0.45-0.49 other days (t_ep=1.65, p=0.10), i.e. Friday SIGNALS are fine.
findings.method: Daily strategy MTM by weekday with year-paired t; trade-level dow cell test.
findings.n: 1,186 Fridays, 24 years
findings.robustness: Consistent across years for OVS/OLV/IOB, but a Friday MTM effect on a short book (OVS) matches the well-documented positive Friday drift, and the long strategies' Friday weakness has no mechanism identified here.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Nothing for sizing (sizing keys on signal date). At most a hedge-timing or exit-day question (e.g. whether OVS T+2 exits landing on Fridays should be handled differently) - outside this study's scope and not evidenced.
findings.caveat: Book Friday mean includes the structural zeros of MonFri/Monday Dip, which mechanically lower the Friday average without any loss.

findings.claim: Outside-the-repo calendar priors do not transfer to this book: September is not a bad month, opex week and turn-of-month carry no edge difference, holiday-adjacent sessions are neutral.
findings.numbers: September (signal month): book avgR 0.418 (N=229), R/risk 0.39, positive PnL in 15/23 years, avgR > 0 in 17/23; daily Sep Sharpe 2.21, sd ratio 0.84, only 3 drawdown troughs. Replays: Sep 0.5x -4.5% PnL, Sharpe -0.044, maxDD 0.00, 1/24 years better; Aug-Sep 0.75x -3.9% / -0.031, 3/24. Opex week: book avgR 0.450 (N=897) vs 0.475 other / 0.472 post-opex, p_year 0.63; dip-buy opex 0.75x replay -1.2% PnL, Sharpe +0.008. Turn-of-month (last 2 + first 3 sessions): book 0.404 (N=833) vs 0.488, t_year=-1.34 p=0.19; OVS TOM 0.257 vs 0.418 (N=315, t_year=-2.07 p=0.05, q=0.23), 52wh TOM 0.62 vs 0.49 (p=0.04, q=0.23), Monday Dip TOM 0.91 vs 0.31 (N=28, t_ep=2.29); replays dip-buy TOM 1.25x +1.1% PnL / Sharpe -0.017; book TOM 0.75x -7.0% / -0.004. Holiday adjacency: pre-holiday 0.386 (N=98) vs 0.471, post 0.475 (N=100), p_year 0.37/0.69; daily pre-holiday sd 59 vs 74 (t=-3.5, quiet sessions) with mean 8.2 vs 9.3. Week-of-month: W1-W4+ avgR 0.47/0.43/0.46/0.51, all p > 0.19.
findings.method: Trade-level cells with both tests; trade_mtm replays of the fixed, unfitted prior rules on 2003-2026 and 2010-2026.
findings.n: See per cell; 24 years
findings.robustness: Every prior replay is negative or within +-0.02 Sharpe; the OVS TOM cell (p=0.05, q=0.23) is the only nominal one and the OVS Dec 1.25x / TOM cells cancel each other in December.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Reject: Sep cut, Aug-Sep cut, opex-week dip-buy cut, TOM tilts, holiday tilts. Do not carry index-return seasonality into a book whose trades are conditional entries with ATR exits; the index base rate does not describe the conditional cell.
findings.caveat: The TOM window is the -2/+3 session form; the classic -1/+3 or -4/+1 forms were not scanned (deliberately, to avoid the multiple-window search).

recommendations.change: No calendar-conditional sizing layer of any kind (month, quarter, half-year, earnings season, opex week, turn-of-month, day-of-week, holiday). Record this as a closed negative result in the plan's decision register alongside the book-level throttle.
recommendations.rule: Sizing stays keyed on the signal date's ATR risk, existing overlays and the flow that the signal filters already produce; no multiplier may reference the calendar.
recommendations.expected_effect: Zero PnL/Sharpe change versus current; avoids the -1% to -11% PnL and 0 to -2.6 pt maxDD outcomes of every replayed calendar rule; avoids the 1,000-cell garden of forking paths.
recommendations.confidence: high: 0 of 1,012 cells survive FDR on year-clustered tests; fitted multipliers <= baseline OOS in 17 of 18 rule/design combinations, and the one positive (WF strat x month +0.04 Sharpe, t=1.0) reverses under LOYO

recommendations.change: Add an explicit 'seasonal variance is flow, not risk' clause to the L4 rule: the drawdown-probability frontier is computed on the full-year series and NOT re-derived per season, and no vol-target may key on trailing realized vol that is seasonally low.
recommendations.rule: GRM frontier uses the whole-year bootstrap; May-Oct realized vol (63 vs 83 bps/day) is expected, not a signal to add size, because mean falls in proportion (Kelly ratio 1.03).
recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents the summer 'low vol, add leverage' mistake that a vol-targeted overlay would make: the Nov-Apr 1.25x replay shows what that costs (Sharpe -0.033, maxDD -3 pts for +14% PnL).
recommendations.confidence: high: sd-open-risk Spearman 0.77, elasticity 0.51, year-paired Kelly ratio median 1.03 with sd lower in 19/24 summers

recommendations.change: Pre-register (do not ship) an OVS same-day-cluster tilt: when the PM scan stages >= 5 OVS signals, size each at 1.25x base (P1 and P2), subject to the existing per-strategy 250 bps cap; alternatively lift the P2 aggregate cap to 1.5x on those days. Decision rule written before the run: episode-clustered t >= 2 on the 5+ vs <5 gap with the 2026 episodes included, LOYO gap floor > +0.20, no worst-day deterioration in the replay beyond 0.5 pt, P1/P2 split reported separately.
recommendations.rule: OVS_same_day_count >= 5 -> risk mult 1.25 (candidate; prereg only). Complements the plan's L2 finding that OVS legs at 13+ open are near-independent (rho ~0).
recommendations.expected_effect: Cell is 451 fills / 38 days / 29 episodes at avgR 0.65 vs 0.23 (R/risk 0.52 vs ~0.30); ledger risk on those days median 93 bps so a 1.25x adds ~25 bps of staged risk on ~2 days a year; expected +$1-2k per cluster day, upside bounded by the 250 cap, episode-concentrated (7 dates carry the 16+ bucket).
recommendations.confidence: moderate: q=0.002 and LOYO-stable, but 29 episodes and the two 2026 cluster days lost; must not be generalised (52wh shows the opposite stack effect)

recommendations.change: Do not extend any earnings-season haircut beyond the existing OVS blackout and the OLV / St OS Sznl per-name size overrides; explicitly reject the base-rate 'trim single stocks in reporting season' idea.
recommendations.rule: Earnings handling stays per-name (blackout / override), never per-season.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids -7.1% PnL (single-stock 0.75x in season, 0-1 of 17-24 years better); in-season trades that pass the blackouts run avgR 0.52-0.64 vs 0.41-0.48 off-season, 14/15 strategies same sign.
recommendations.confidence: moderate-high: LOYO gap [+0.06, +0.15] for single-stock strategies, p=0.023 nominal at book level, q=0.27

recommendations.change: Dip-buy family in May-Oct: keep full size; add a WATCH ITEM with a written trigger rather than a rule. Trigger: if the family's expanding May-Oct minus Nov-Apr gap stays below -0.15 AND the September dip-buy cell (currently R/risk 0.03, N=70) is <= 0 after 20 more September fills (~2029), re-open as a 0.75x Sep-only appetite decision; otherwise leave alone.
recommendations.rule: No change now. Watch: dip-buy family May-Oct gap (currently -0.19, LOYO [-0.25,-0.14], 6/6 members) and dip-buy September R/risk.
recommendations.expected_effect: A cut today costs 3.1% of book PnL (0.75x) for zero maxDD change; the gated walk-forward version of the same cut was -0.35% PnL, i.e. it would have fired in only 4 of 17 years and lost in each. At 6% of Kelly a +0.30 R/risk cell keeps full size.
recommendations.confidence: moderate: family effect is real-looking (t_ep -2.1, base-rate aligned, control opposite-signed) but post-2013 only and never large enough to beat its own PnL cost

recommendations.change: Retire the following calendar ideas from any future study list (negative-registry entries): September 0.5x, Aug-Sep 0.75x, May-Oct 0.75x book, Nov-Apr 1.25x book, December 1.25x, Q4 1.25x, opex-week dip-buy cut, turn-of-month tilts, holiday-adjacent tilts, OLV August cut, LT Trend June cut, 52wh October boost, OVS December boost, January de-rate, Friday de-rate.
recommendations.rule: Listed rules are closed; a revival needs a new mechanism plus a pre-registered single-cell test, not a table scan.
recommendations.expected_effect: None on PnL; saves future research budget. Replay outcomes (2003-2026): Sep 0.5x -4.5% PnL; May-Oct 0.75x -11.3%; Nov-Apr 1.25x Sharpe -0.033/maxDD -3.0; Dec 1.25x +0.003 Sharpe; opex dip-buy 0.75x -1.2%; book TOM 0.75x -7.0%; OLV Aug 0.5x -0.9%; LT Trend Jun 0.5x +0.3%; 52wh Oct 1.5x -0.001 Sharpe; OVS Dec 1.25x +0.013 Sharpe (14/24 yrs).

negative_results: Strategy x month sizing multipliers (shrunk avgR ratios, N0 30/60, clips 0.5-1.5 / 0.7-1.3, mean and Kelly forms): walk-forward +0.04 to +0.05 Sharpe (t 1.0-2.1, within noise), LOYO -0.03 to -0.08 Sharpe with maxDD 1.7-2.6 pts worse; in-sample fit itself only -0.03 Sharpe. Closed.

Strategy x quarter, strategy x half-year, book x half-year, strategy x earnings-season, strategy x opex, strategy x turn-of-month, strategy x day-of-week fitted multipliers: every one <= baseline Sharpe in walk-forward and/or LOYO (range -0.065 to +0.031), 4-12 of 17 years better. Closed.

Fitted signal-flow multiplier (strategy x trailing-21-session signal count bucket): WF +2.2% PnL / -0.052 Sharpe, LOYO -2.6% / -0.042. Per-strategy flow-quality patterns disagree in sign (52wh falls with prior flow, OLV/IOB rise), so no generic flow rule exists.

External calendar priors replayed unfitted: September 0.5x (-4.5% PnL, 1/24 yrs), Aug-Sep 0.75x (-3.9%), May-Oct 0.75x (-11.3%, maxDD unchanged), Nov-Apr 1.25x (+13.7% PnL but Sharpe -0.033, maxDD -3.0 pts, PnL/maxDD -9%), Dec 1.25x (+0.003 Sharpe), Q4 1.25x (Sharpe -0.022), dip-buy opex 0.75x (-1.2%), dip-buy TOM 1.25x (Sharpe -0.017), book TOM 0.75x (-7.0%), single-stock earnings-season 0.75x (-7.1%, 0-1 yrs better). All closed.

'Crowded month' hypothesis (high flow AND poor quality): no cell with N>=10 has year-paired p < 0.19; the largest (OLV Aug 0.35 vs 0.86, N=61) still earns +$28.8k and its 0.5x replay costs 0.9% of PnL. High-flow months (Dec/Jan/Jun) show average quality.

Variance seasonality as a sizing input: month-vol rankings do not persist across years (mean pairwise Spearman 0.06 for the book); after controlling for open risk only May has residual low vol (t=-2.5). January's excess variance is 8 episodic years (median Jan/rest sd ratio 0.99). December's lower trade-R variance is OVS composition (within-strategy standardized Levene p=0.064).
Holiday adjacency (pre/post market holiday): trade-level p_year 0.37/0.69; pre-holiday sessions are quieter (sd 59 vs 74 bps) with the same mean. Week-of-month W1-W4+: all p > 0.19.
Earnings-season haircut for single-stock strategies: wrong sign (in-season better in 7/7 single-stock strategies, LOYO all positive).
caveats: Vintage: ledger data/backtest_trades_full.parquet as on disk 2026-09-02 (gha:33608560596 per the plan), trade_mtm.json and strategy_daily.json built 2026-08-07 (last MTM date 2026-08-07). The dial series was not used in this study (calendar cells only); dial-conditioned re-tests belong to the cross-strategy/regime analyst.

Multiple comparisons: 1,012 trade-level cells and ~1,500 daily-basis cells were tested; families were defined per dimension across strategies+book (fam_dim) and per (dimension, strategy); q-values are reported per family. A single pre-specified hypothesis (e.g. the dip-buy summer gap or the earnings-season sign) is judged on its own nominal p plus LOYO, and is labelled accordingly.

Replays scale each trade's daily MTM vector by a multiplier and re-sum; the per-strategy 250 bps daily cap, the OVS P2 aggregate cap, the OLV ticker notional cap and the cross-strategy overlap clamp are NOT re-applied, so multipliers > 1 overstate the achievable raise and multipliers < 1 slightly understate the saving. The trade_mtm sum ($4.040M) is 2.3% below the ledger PnL sum ($4.137M); all comparisons are baseline-vs-overlay on the same vectors so the gap does not affect signs.

Sizing basis is flat $750k; the overflow tier's survivorship bias (CLAUDE.md) flatters long dip-buy and overflow OLV/St OS cells, which are exactly the cells in the summer-vs-winter family comparison; the winter cell is flattered more.

Calendar attribution differs by surface: trade-level cells key on the SIGNAL date (what sizing can act on); daily-basis cells key on the MTM date (what the account experiences). 52wh's 63-day holds and OVS/OLV time exits make the two disagree (e.g. Friday, WCDS December), and only the signal-date view is a sizing statement.

Earnings season 'data' definition uses the current FMP-backfilled calendar (not point-in-time, 1985-2027 coverage); the fixed-calendar definition (days 11-50 of the quarter) gives the same sign with weaker magnitude. Turn-of-month is the -2/+3 session window only; opex week is Mon-Fri of the third-Friday week; holidays are inferred from SPY session gaps.
OVS tranches were collapsed to one row per fill for the trade-level tables (R = sum PnL / sum risk), so OVS N is fills (1,182), not ledger rows (2,483); the plan's per-trade tables use rows.

Strategies with short histories (3x fades 2020+, 3x Leader Gap Fade, Monthly Weak Close 14 fills, St OS Sznl 58) cannot support month cells; their absence from the survivor list is a power statement. Low-N cells that look extreme (e.g. Sector BO Sep avgR 4.1 on 6 fills, 3x ETF Fade Sep 6.04 on 1) were excluded by the N>=10 screens and should not be quoted.

The dip-buy summer gap is post-2013 in the expanding-window record (positive through 2012); 12 years of a 24-year sample is what supports it, and the recommended watch trigger is written to that fact.
