findings.claim: Across the book the marginal add is the HIGHER-edge leg, not a clone: in OLV, OVS, WCDS, LT Trend ST OS and 3x ETF Overbot Fade, legs entered while the strategy already has positions open average more R than solo legs; the only negative marginal cell anywhere is 52wh Breakout at >= 6 open legs, and only in the 2010+ era.
findings.method: Per-leg open-leg count at entry from the full ledger (fills only; OVS tranches collapsed to trades), episode = chain of overlapping legs; episode-clustered t vs the solo bucket; LOYO floor of that t; 4,000-resample episode bootstrap.
findings.n: 2,521 trades over 8 strategies (OLV 315, 52wh 256, OVS 1,270 trades from 2,483 tranche rows, WCDS 268, LT 246, 3x ETF 87, 3x Bear 55, 3x Leader 24); 2003-2026.
findings.robustness: Clustered t vs solo: OVS 13+ 4.6 (LOYO floor 4.4, 6/6 years positive), OVS 6-12 2.6 (1.9, 8/10), LT 3-5 2.65 (2.0, 8/10), OLV 6-12 2.0 (1.5), WCDS 2-open 1.8 (1.3). Spearman(R, n_open) among adds: OLV +0.16, OVS +0.18, LT +0.22, 3x ETF +0.24, WCDS +0.05, 52wh +0.03.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Any add rule that cuts the n-th leg for being the n-th leg cuts the book's best legs. Within-strategy sizing should grade UP with sleeve depth (or at least not down) everywhere except 52wh; the baseline's 'OLV stacks are one bet with rising per-leg edge' generalises to OVS, WCDS and LT.
findings.caveat: Fills-only ledger with survivorship in the overflow tier; depth is counted on filled legs, live would also see working limits.

findings.claim: Sector concentration and same-ticker stacking are not clones in edge terms: legs entered with 2+ same-sector legs open, and OLV legs added to a ticker already held, have HIGHER avgR than other adds; ex-ante trailing-63d return correlation with the open names carries no negative information about a leg's R in any strategy.
findings.numbers: 2+ same-sector open: OLV 1.16R (N 51, t 2.24 vs solo, LOYO 1.90; vs other adds +0.37R bootstrap P=0.11), OVS 0.69R (N 290, t 4.7, LOYO 3.7, 11/11 years), LT 0.62R (N 30, t 3.5, LOYO 2.1). OLV same-ticker adds 0.98R (N 103, t 2.1 vs solo, LOYO 1.59), rising with depth in the ticker: 1 open 0.86R (72), 2 open 1.06R (24), 3+ open 1.92R (7, 7/7 wins). Spearman(R, rho63) among adds: OLV -0.04, OVS +0.16, LT +0.15, WCDS +0.15, 52wh +0.01; rho>0.6 cut replay loses PnL per $ risk in OLV (0.790->0.762), OVS (0.298->0.284), WCDS (0.281->0.243), LT (0.301->0.289), 3x ETF (0.690->0.645).
findings.method: sector_map.parquet (+ manual map for 3x ETFs), same-sector/same-ticker open counts at entry, trailing-63d daily-return correlation with each open name (window ending the session before entry), bucket tables with clustered t, replay of 0.5x cuts keyed on each feature.
findings.n: OLV 229 adds, OVS 911, LT 112, WCDS 112, 52wh 215, 3x ETF 52.
findings.robustness: OLV 2+ same-sector cell is concentrated in 2021/2025/2026 (energy, financials, utilities) and one negative 2026 Industrials cell (N 4, -0.4R); OVS/LT same-sector effects are broad (OVS 11/11 years). Same-ticker vs other-adds difference is not significant (P=0.15) but the sign is the opposite of 'clone'.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not cut OLV/OVS/LT adds for sector or ticker overlap; the baseline's same-ticker clamp logic (IOB SPY+QQQ) does NOT transfer to OLV, whose same-ticker adds are its best cell because the second signal in the same name is a deeper washout. Keep OLV's 50%-NAV ticker cap only as catastrophe insurance (8 clipped legs ever, avgR 1.17, $2.6k cost).
findings.caveat: Sector map is today's classification (no history); 3x ETF sectors hand-mapped; 41 ledger tickers unmapped and treated as singleton sectors.

findings.claim: The Euler variance lens and the edge lens disagree only where rho is high (OLV, WCDS), and at the book's ~6% of full Kelly the edge lens governs: the growth-rate variance tax on a marginal leg is second order, so the growth-optimal add rule with a FIXED sleeve budget (Kelly concurrency factor) loses to the edge-only rule at equal risk in every strategy where correlation is high, and only ties or helps where rho ~ 0.
findings.numbers: PnL per unit Euler variance, solo vs deep adds: OLV 61 vs 36 (6-12 open; efficiency 0.58x) while PnL per $ ATR risk is 0.45 vs 1.08 (2.4x); OVS 34 vs 23 (6-12) / 75 (13+); WCDS 19 vs 33-42 (adds better on BOTH lenses); LT 48 vs 76 (both lenses); 52wh 35 vs 10 (worse on both). Implied pairwise rho from leg MTM: OLV 0.73 (0.93 at 2-3 legs, 0.86 at 7-12), WCDS 0.50, OVS 0.12, 3x Bear 0.11, LT 0.08, 52wh 0.04, 3x ETF 0.00. Walk-forward Kelly-concurrency rule (m = edge ratio / (1 + n*rho)) vs current PnL per $ risk: OLV 0.651 vs 0.790, OVS 0.280 vs 0.298, WCDS 0.281 vs 0.281, LT 0.314 vs 0.301, 3x ETF 0.724 vs 0.690. Variance-parity rule 1/sqrt(1+n*rho): OLV 0.678, OVS 0.279, WCDS 0.261, LT 0.292 (all worse). Kelly tax as a share of the marginal leg's mu at f/f* = 0.06: rho 0.5 n 4 -> 24%, rho 1.0 n 8 -> 90% (only the OLV 7+ cell approaches parity).
findings.method: Per-leg daily MTM from master_prices closes (entry/exit at fill prices, residual to booked PnL on the exit day; reconciles exactly), Euler share = sum over the leg's days of leg_pnl x sleeve_pnl; implied rho from sd(sleeve)/(sd1*sqrt(n)); walk-forward edge multipliers estimated on all other years with N0=20 shrinkage to the solo mean.
findings.n: 17,188 leg-days of MTM across 2,521 trades; sleeve-day counts by leg bucket: OLV 397/307/97/49, OVS 615/298/104/48/26, 52wh 735/1101/476/162.
findings.robustness: Kelly-concurrency rule loses in OLV in every year band; edge-only walk-forward rule matches current PnL/risk for OLV (0.791 vs 0.790) and beats it for OVS (0.309), WCDS (0.310), LT (0.319), 3x ETF (0.726); 52wh is the one strategy where the walk-forward edge rule loses (0.440 vs 0.527), i.e. its depth buckets are noise.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Size adds by marginal expected R, not by marginal sleeve variance. Correlation matters for this book only through the drawdown constraint (which the principal relaxed) and through the L3 market-factor hedge, not through per-leg sizing. Where adds are better on both lenses (WCDS, LT) the reallocation is unambiguous.
findings.caveat: Euler shares are ex post on realized MTM; a live rule can only use ex-ante rho, which showed no relationship to R.

findings.claim: OLV's signal-recency ladder is keyed on the wrong variable. Because it counts same-ticker signal days, it halves 81% of solo legs (the 0.48R cell) but also 43-49% of legs entered into 3+ open OLV names (0.93-1.15R). A ladder keyed on sleeve depth, or the max of the two rungs, keeps the appetite cut on the weak cell and stops cutting the strong one.
findings.numbers: Current ladder rung by sleeve depth: solo mean rung 0.54 (81% at 0.5x, avgR 0.48); 1-2 open 0.64 (49% at 0.5x, 0.62R); 3-5 open 0.70 (43% at 0.5x, 0.93R); 6+ open 0.70 (43% at 0.5x, 1.15R). Replays 2005-2026 (PnL / risk deployed / PnL per $ risk / exit-basis worst-21d / exit maxDD / MTM maxDD): current ladder $418k / $529k / 0.790 / -14.0k / -20.6k / -40.6k; no ladder $643k / $845k / 0.761 / -17.1k / -27.4k / -56.1k (the ladder costs $225k over 21y, +3.7% quality); depth ladder [0.5 solo, 0.7 at 1-2 open, 1.0 at 3+] $534k / $648k / 0.825 / -13.4k / -19.6k / -54.1k; max(recency rung, depth rung) $543k / $662k / 0.820 / -13.4k / -19.6k / -54.1k (+$125k raw, +$16k at equal risk, 15 of 20 years PnL/risk >= current); depth ladder with 1.25x at 6+ open $584k / $696k / 0.839 (+$26k at equal risk); sleeve-cap / sqrt-n / Kelly-concurrency variants 0.65-0.68 (lose).
findings.method: Ledger Size_Mult decomposed into ladder rung x residual (earnings override 15/52.5, cap clips); candidate multipliers applied to unit PnL with the residual retained; realized-at-exit and MTM sleeve metrics; equal-risk rescaling.
findings.n: 315 OLV legs, 86 episodes, 2005-2026; 141-189 legs change under the depth variants.
findings.robustness: Depth-OR-ticker ladder PnL per $ risk >= current in 15/20 years; the exit-basis worst-21d and maxDD are better, the MTM maxDD is worse only because the footprint grows 25% (at equal risk MTM maxDD -43.3k vs -40.6k). The ladder's own rationale (leg-1 avgR 0.56-0.82 vs 1.1-1.4 for leg-3+) is the same fact seen here.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Re-key the OLV ladder to max(ticker-recency rung, sleeve-depth rung). This is the one within-strategy change that improves total PnL, PnL per unit risk AND the realized worst-21d at once. The 2026-07-29 open-count ladder was retired for operational reasons (reset on chain exit, blind to unfilled limits), not evidence; the fix is to count open legs plus working OLV limits, not to drop depth as the key.
findings.caveat: Depth counted on filled legs; live should include working entries (the T+3 fill window means up to 3 days of unfilled limits are invisible to both engine and scan).

findings.claim: OVS's per-strategy 250 bps daily cap is the binding within-strategy control and it lands on OVS's best cell: path-1 fills entered with >= 6 OVS legs open are the highest-edge OVS trades but book a fraction of solo size because the cap is pro-rated across the day's STAGED signals.
findings.numbers: P1 avgR by depth (N, booked bps per fill): solo 0.23 (161, 53.8), 1-2 open 0.27 (146, 47.0), 3-5 0.54 (101, 32.1), 6-12 0.77 (90, 22.9), 13+ 0.82 (163, 4.4). Largest day 2023-12-13: P1 fills at 2.5 bps each. P1 depth>=6 cell by year positive 8/10 (2020: 87 legs 0.89R at 3.9 bps/fill; 2023: 96 legs 0.77R at 3.8 bps). Replay P1 depth>=6 x1.5 (~cap 375 bps on cluster days): OVS PnL $607k -> $699k (+15%), PnL/risk 0.298 -> 0.327, worst day -26.1k -> -35.3k (2021-01-27), worst-21d unchanged -38.4k, MTM maxDD -51.6k -> -55.3k, active Sharpe 1.88 -> 1.84; x2: $791k, worst day -44.4k, maxDD -66.7k. P1 solo 0.75 / depth>=3 x1.5: $706k, 0.336 PnL/risk (+13%), maxDD -60.7k. P2 x2 everywhere: worse (0.280).
findings.method: Path inferred from Size_Mult (>=0.7 = P1), depth from open OVS trades at entry; cluster-day up-size replayed as a proxy for a higher per-strategy cap (pro-rata scaling is linear in the cap); MTM tails from leg vectors.
findings.n: 1,270 OVS trades / 359 episodes; 253 P1 legs at depth >= 6 across 10 years.
findings.robustness: Depth>=6 vs solo: clustered t 2.6 (6-12) and 4.6 (13+), LOYO floors 1.9 / 4.4, episode-bootstrap P < 0.001, 8/10 years positive; 2+ same-sector adds 0.69R t 4.7 (11/11 years). The tail cost is concentrated in one day (2021-01-27, the short squeeze), which is exactly the day the cap was documented to bound.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Raise the OVS per-strategy daily cap from 250 to 375 bps effective (P2 aggregate cap unchanged); the expected value is +$92k/23y and PnL/risk +10% for a worst day ~35% worse. Consistent with the book's 'signal density is the edge' finding: the cluster days are where OVS pays, and the cap is a scalar throttle on exactly those days.
findings.caveat: The replay scales fills; a real cap change also scales staged-but-unfilled rows and interacts with the P2 aggregate cap. Requires aligned changes in order_staging (OneDrive) PER_STRAT_DAILY_CAP_DOLLARS, build_trade_ledger and the engine cap. The 2021-01-27 day is the single-day tail the 250 cap exists for.

findings.claim: WCDS and LT Trend ST OS: same-day cluster adds are the edge, cluster days are not high-dial days for WCDS, and LT's cluster adds keep their edge at dial 50+ while its solo legs go negative at 65+. A solo 0.75x / adds 1.25x reallocation raises PnL per unit risk with LOWER sleeve maxDD in both.
findings.numbers: WCDS: same-day adds 0.73R (N 75, t 2.7, LOYO 2.1, bootstrap P 0.021) vs solo 0.21R (156); later adds (1-2 td) 0.28R (51). Per signal day: 1 fill 0.14R avg ($579/day, 149 days), 2 fills 0.43R ($3.8k), 4-5 fills 0.93R ($14.4k/day, 7 days). Replay solo 0.75 / adds 1.25: $337k -> $362k on 5% LESS risk, PnL/risk 0.281 -> 0.317 (+13%), +$43k at equal risk, MTM maxDD -60.8k -> -55.1k, worst-21d -31.1k -> -33.1k; the 250 bps cap binds on 9 of 194 signal days at 1.25x (capped variant still +$12k at equal risk). Cluster days 2016+: mean dial 15.6, 0% at >= 50 (no frag-band interplay). LT: 3-5 open 0.63R (25, t 2.65, LOYO 2.0, P 0.009) vs solo 0.22R (134); 2+ same-sector 0.62R (30, t 3.5, LOYO 2.1). Replay solo 0.75 / adds 1.25: $233k -> $242k on 4% less risk, PnL/risk 0.301 -> 0.327 (+9%), +$20k at equal risk, worst-21d -15.5k -> -12.5k, maxDD -21.2k -> -19.1k. LT adds x lagged dial 2016+: 3+ open 0.79R (<50, N 3) / 0.58R (50-65, 21) / 0.63R (65+, 8); solo 0.38 / 0.05 / -0.12 (48/15/14); 1-2 open 0.49 / 0.32 / 0.02.
findings.method: Same-day-prior counts, per-day cluster tables, replay with the strategy's booked overlays (frag band, P/C fear) retained and the add multiplier composed on top; dial = 10d MA of 63d, lag-1, current-weights vintage.
findings.n: WCDS 268 legs / 156 episodes; LT 246 legs / 134 episodes; LT 2016+ dial cells 3-48 legs each.
findings.robustness: WCDS adds vs solo positive in 18/22 years; LT 3-5 open positive 8/10 years; both reallocations improve maxDD and PnL/risk simultaneously, so they are not footprint effects.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Ship solo 0.75x / adds 1.25x on WCDS and LT (composes with WCDS's frag band and L1 tilt). For LT this also reframes the pending P2 exemption re-test: the 65+ damage is in solo and 1-2-open legs, not in the cluster adds.
findings.caveat: LT dial cells are small and on the recompute vintage (rows before 2026-07-02); WCDS Size_Mult carries a legacy 1.5x/0.66x seasonal tilt that the replay leaves in place.

findings.claim: 52wh Breakout: the baseline's 0.5x at >= 5 open legs is the wrong threshold, and the >= 6 cell is tail insurance rather than an edge claim: it is not negative across history, but it owns 88% of 52wh's worst 21-day MTM window.
findings.numbers: 2010+: exact-5 open 1.71R (N 13, 69% win, $87.6k), >= 6 open 0.08R (23, 35% win, $7.5k); pre-2010 >= 6 open 0.92R (17, 53% win, $61.6k); full-history >= 6 vs rest -0.10R, episode-bootstrap P(<=0) = 0.57, 90% CI [-0.74, +0.74]. Worst 21d MTM window 2014-01-17..02-14: -$59.5k with deep-stack legs -$52.3k of it (10 of 15 legs open); 2014-10-16 window -$43.4k, 58% deep. Replays: >= 5 at 0.5x -$68.5k raw, -$9.4k at equal risk (cuts the 1.71R cell); >= 6 at 0.5x -$34.6k raw (-$36.5k ex-2014, i.e. cost sits in 2006-07), +$7.5k at equal risk, sleeve worst-21d -59.5k -> -33.3k, MTM maxDD -78.1k -> -61.5k; >= 6 at 0x -$137k raw, -$21.6k at equal risk. Walk-forward edge rule on 52wh depth loses (0.440 vs 0.527): its depth buckets are noise. Sector-share >= 50% at 3+ open: -0.75R but N 6.
findings.method: Open-leg depth at entry, era split, worst-window attribution from leg MTM, episode bootstrap over 41 breakout episodes.
findings.n: 256 legs / 41 episodes; deep cell 40 legs over 5 years (2006, 2007, 2013, 2014, 2019).
findings.robustness: Sign flips by era; the 2010+ negative cell is 4 episodes and 2014 dominates the tail. Nothing about depth is stable enough for a walk-forward rule.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not ship >= 5. A 0.5x at >= 6 is defensible only as declared variance/tail insurance (cost -$35k/22y raw, near zero at equal risk, halves the Feb-2014-type window) with a written re-exam trigger; the plan's decision #3 should be reworded and re-thresholded accordingly.
findings.caveat: Small N, era-dependent, 2014 is one episode; pre-2010 legs were in a different universe vintage.

findings.claim: Combined within-strategy package (OLV depth-OR-ticker ladder, OVS P1 x1.5 at depth >= 6 as a proxy for a 375 bps cap, WCDS and LT solo 0.75 / adds 1.25; 52wh and 3x fades unchanged) improves the 8-strategy sleeve on PnL, PnL per unit risk and Sharpe with worst-21d and maxDD slightly better and one worse day.
findings.numbers: 8-strategy sleeve MTM 2005-2026: PnL $2.509M -> $2.758M (+$249k, +9.9%) on risk +2.5%; PnL per $ risk 0.414 -> 0.444; ann. Sharpe 1.73 -> 1.77; ann PnL $112k -> $123k; worst day -$36.0k -> -$43.9k (2021-01-27); worst-21d -$71.3k -> -$68.4k (2014-02-14); maxDD -$83.9k -> -$81.0k (2014-02-03); at equal risk +$183k, worst day -$42.9k, maxDD -$79.0k. By year: 17 of 22 better; +$200k excluding the best year (2021, +$50k); worst year 2024 -$3.8k. Per strategy raw: OLV $418k -> $543k, OVS $607k -> $699k, WCDS $337k -> $362k, LT $233k -> $242k.
findings.method: Leg-level MTM vectors scaled by the package factor per leg, summed across the 8 strategies; no cross-strategy or non-target strategies included; caps not re-applied except as noted.
findings.n: 2,521 trades, 5,400 sleeve days 2005-2026.
findings.robustness: 17/22 years better, gain survives dropping the best year, worst-21d and maxDD do not deteriorate; the only tail that worsens is the OVS short-squeeze day.
findings.implication_for_sizing: The within-strategy layer is worth ~+10% of these strategies' PnL at flat quality-adjusted risk; it is additive to the L1 base-bps tilt and independent of the dial.
findings.caveat: Sleeve-level only (the 8 target strategies); book-level maxDD interactions with IOB/MonFri/Monday Dip not measured here; OVS proxy assumes the cap scales linearly.

findings.claim: The 3x fades carry no actionable within-strategy structure at their sample size; the 3x Bear same-day derate is neutral at equal risk.
findings.numbers: 3x Bear (N 55): no-derate replay PnL/risk 0.665 vs current 0.677, -$1.7k at equal risk; adds vs solo +0.07R P 0.36; 1 same-sector add 1.15R but N 7. 3x ETF fade (N 87): adds 1.25 +$4.2k at equal risk, 6-12 open 1.76R (N 19, 3 episodes), adds vs solo P 0.23; same-ticker or same-sector 0.5x cuts lose (0.679 / 0.661 vs 0.690). 3x Leader (N 24): 1-2 td stack adds 4.3R on 5 legs, same-day adds -0.64R on 5 legs, one episode each.
findings.method: Same bucket tables and replays; derate inferred from fills per signal date.
findings.n: 55 / 87 / 24 trades.
findings.robustness: Every cell is 1-3 episodes.
findings.implication_for_sizing: No change; keep the derate as the documented appetite rule; do not add stacking rules to the fades.
findings.caveat: Fill counts understate staged signal counts, so the inferred derate is approximate.

recommendations.change: OLV: re-key the signal-recency ladder to max(ticker-recency rung, sleeve-depth rung), depth rung = 0.5x when no OLV legs are open (filled or working), 0.7x with 1-2 open, 1.0x with 3+ open; keep same-ticker adds at full size and keep the 50%-NAV ticker cap.
recommendations.rule: mult = max(recency_rung(ticker, 21td), depth_rung(n_open_OLV_legs_incl_working)); composes with the earnings override and frag/PC bands as today.
recommendations.expected_effect: Replay 2005-2026: PnL $418k -> $543k (+$125k), PnL per $ risk 0.790 -> 0.820, exit-basis worst-21d -14.0k -> -13.4k, exit maxDD -20.6k -> -19.6k, MTM maxDD -40.6k -> -54.1k (footprint +25%; -43.3k at equal risk), PnL/risk >= current in 15/20 years. Adding a 1.25x rung at 6+ open lifts PnL/risk to 0.839 (+$26k at equal risk).
recommendations.confidence: moderate (evidenced cell structure, clustered t 1.6-2.0, LOYO floors 1.0-1.5, bootstrap P 0.007-0.017; the ladder itself remains an appetite cut)

recommendations.change: OVS: raise the per-strategy daily cap from 250 to 375 bps effective (P2 aggregate cap 1.125% unchanged); do not add sector or ticker clamps.
recommendations.rule: order_staging PER_STRAT_DAILY_CAP_DOLLARS['Overbot Vol Spike'] = 375 bps x NAV; engine process_signals_fast cap_bps per strategy; build_trade_ledger aligned.
recommendations.expected_effect: Proxy replay (P1 fills at depth >= 6 x1.5): OVS PnL +$92k/23y (+15%), PnL/risk 0.298 -> 0.327, worst day -26k -> -35k (2021-01-27), maxDD -52k -> -55k, worst-21d unchanged; +$58k at equal risk.
recommendations.confidence: moderate-high on the cell (t 2.6-4.6, LOYO 1.9-4.4, P < 0.001, 8/10 years), moderate on the magnitude (cap change also scales unfilled rows)

recommendations.change: WCDS: solo 0.75x / adds 1.25x (adds = any WCDS leg entered with >= 1 WCDS leg open, dominated by same-day clusters).
recommendations.rule: mult = 0.75 if n_open_WCDS == 0 else 1.25; composes with frag_risk_bands / pc_fear_bands and the L1 tilt; the 250 bps cap stays.
recommendations.expected_effect: PnL $337k -> $362k on 5% less risk, PnL/risk 0.281 -> 0.317 (+13%), +$43k at equal risk, MTM maxDD -60.8k -> -55.1k, worst-21d -31.1k -> -33.1k; cap trims 9 of 194 days.

recommendations.change: LT Trend ST OS: solo 0.75x / adds 1.25x.
recommendations.rule: mult = 0.75 if n_open_LT == 0 else 1.25 (same-sector clusters explicitly NOT cut).
recommendations.expected_effect: PnL $233k -> $242k on 4% less risk, PnL/risk 0.301 -> 0.327 (+9%), +$20k at equal risk, worst-21d -15.5k -> -12.5k, maxDD -21.2k -> -19.1k. At dial 65+ the cluster adds are the only LT legs with edge (0.63R vs solo -0.12R), which should be folded into the P2 exemption re-test.
recommendations.confidence: moderate (t 2.65, LOYO 2.0, P 0.009 for depth >= 3; 8/10 years)

recommendations.change: 52wh Breakout: replace the plan's 0.5x at >= 5 open with 0.5x at >= 6 open, labelled tail insurance, or drop it.
recommendations.rule: mult = 0.5 if n_open_52wh >= 6 else 1.0; re-exam at +15 legs in the cell; retire if the cell's avgR >= 0.4 then.
recommendations.expected_effect: Raw -$35k/22y (nearly all pre-2010), +$7.5k at equal risk, sleeve worst-21d -59.5k -> -33.3k and MTM maxDD -78k -> -61k (the Feb-2014 window is 88% deep-stack legs). The >= 5 version costs -$9.4k at equal risk because the exact-5 cell is 1.71R.
recommendations.confidence: low (episode bootstrap P 0.57; era-dependent; 4 post-2010 episodes)

recommendations.change: Do not adopt any correlation-, sector-, same-ticker- or stack-age-keyed cut in OLV, OVS, WCDS, LT or the 3x fades; do not adopt a Kelly-concurrency (1 + n*rho) per-leg rule or a sleeve risk budget anywhere.
recommendations.rule: Add sizing is keyed on marginal expected R only; correlation is handled at L3 (factor hedge) and by the drawdown rule at L4.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids the measured losses: rho>0.6 cuts -0.02 to -0.04 PnL/risk in every strategy; Kelly-concurrency rule OLV 0.651 vs 0.790, OVS 0.280 vs 0.298; OLV sleeve caps 0.74-0.77 (baseline); same-ticker 0.5x on OLV 0.715.

recommendations.change: 3x fades: no change (keep the 3x Bear same-day derate as an appetite rule).
recommendations.rule: unchanged
recommendations.expected_effect: Derate is neutral at equal risk (0.665 vs 0.677 PnL/risk); no stacking rule clears N.
recommendations.confidence: high that nothing should change; low on any direction

negative_results: Ex-ante trailing-63d return correlation of a new name with the open names predicts nothing about the leg's R in any strategy (Spearman -0.04 to +0.16 among adds); rho > 0.6 cuts lose PnL per $ risk in OLV, OVS, WCDS, LT and 3x ETF fade.
Same-sector 2+ cuts lose everywhere they bind (OLV 0.790 -> 0.732, OVS -> 0.280, LT -> 0.287, 3x ETF -> 0.661); same-sector clusters are better legs in OLV, OVS and LT.
Same-ticker 0.5x on OLV loses (0.715 vs 0.790): OLV's same-ticker adds are its best cell (0.98R; 1.92R at 3+ deep), the opposite of the IOB SPY/QQQ clone case.

Kelly-concurrency per-leg rule (edge ratio / (1 + n*rho)) and variance parity (1/sqrt(1 + n*rho)) lose at equal risk wherever rho is high (OLV 0.651 / 0.678 vs 0.790; WCDS 0.281 / 0.261 vs 0.281) and only tie or help where rho ~ 0 (LT 0.314, 3x ETF 0.724); confirms the baseline's OLV sleeve-cap rejection from the growth side.

Late-add cuts (stack age > 5 td at 0.5x) lose in OLV (0.764 vs 0.790) and 52wh (neutral at equal risk, -$209k raw); stack age carries no edge information except that 3x fade day-1-2 re-fires are better than same-day clusters at N 5-41.
52wh depth buckets are noise: the walk-forward edge rule on 52wh depth loses (0.440 vs 0.527), the >= 6 cell flips sign by era (0.92R pre-2010, 0.08R 2010+), and >= 5 catches a 1.71R cell.
Removing the OLV ladder outright (flat 1.0x) raises PnL $225k but lowers PnL/risk (0.761 vs 0.790) and worsens every tail; the appetite cut is real, only its key is wrong.
Doubling OVS P2 sizing everywhere loses (0.280 vs 0.298); P2 adds are not where OVS's cluster edge lives (P2 3-5 open 0.13R).
3x Bear same-day derate removal: neutral (0.665 vs 0.677), nothing to gain or lose at N 55.
caveats: All figures are on the fills-only, full-rebuild ledger (vintage gha:33608560596, flat $750k), which carries overflow-tier survivorship (21 of 22 major 2020s delistings absent); OLV, OVS and LT are overflow-heavy, so their add-cell avgR values are upper bounds.

Open-leg depth is counted on FILLED legs; live OLV/OVS/LT also have working limits (OLV T+3 window), so a live depth rule should count open positions plus working entries; engine parity would need the same convention.

The OVS cap replay scales filled rows by 1.5x as a proxy for a 375 bps cap; a real cap change scales staged rows (including unfilled) and interacts with the P2 aggregate cap; per-fill booked risk on the biggest days (2.5-4 bps) shows the cap pro-rates over staged signals, which the ledger does not record.

Realized-at-exit tails (worst-21d, maxDD) follow the baseline's convention; MTM tails come from per-leg daily vectors built from closes with entry/exit at fill prices and the residual on the exit day; sleeve Sharpe is on active days only.
Dial cells (LT adds x dial) use the current-weights recompute vintage before 2026-07-02, lag-1, and are 3-48 legs each; the PIT re-estimate is required before any dial-conditioned add rule.
Sector map is today's classification with no history; 3x ETFs hand-mapped to underlying sector; 41 unmapped tickers treated as singleton sectors (never match).

The combined-package numbers are for the 8-strategy sleeve only and do not re-apply the per-strategy 250 bps cap after up-sizing (WCDS/LT capped variants are reported separately: cap binds on 7-9 days each at 1.25x); book-level interaction with the non-target strategies and with the L1 tilt is not measured.
Small-N cells are flagged as such: 52wh >= 6 (40 legs, 5 years), OLV same-sector 2+ (51 legs, mostly 2021/2025/2026), OLV 3+-deep same-ticker (7 legs), all 3x-fade cells (1-3 episodes).

The Size_Mult decomposition for OLV infers ladder rungs from booked multipliers (0.5/0.7/1.0 and their earnings-override products); 8 cap-clipped legs at 0.8x residual were identified and retained in every candidate.

findings.claim: Signal flow forecasts NEXT-trade expectancy in the three mean-reverting families (dip_buy, oversold_hold, short_fade): a high-flow day is a size-UP state, not a crowded-selloff state. It forecasts nothing for the breakout family.
findings.numbers: Flow = trailing 5d count of the family's raw engine candidates, inclusive of the signal day (staged signals, not fills). Terciles within family, 2005-2026: dip_buy (<=3 / 4-5 / >=6 candidates) avgR 0.216 / 0.657 / 0.569, PnL-per-risk 0.212 -> 0.572, hi-lo +0.35R, episode-cluster t=2.70 (p=0.01); f21 (<=7/8-11/>=12) 0.246/0.379/0.695, t=3.60. oversold_hold (<=3 / 4-8 / >=9) avgR 0.317/0.571/0.855, PnL/risk 0.314->0.835, t=3.00 (p=0.007); f21 0.268/0.568/0.860 t=3.30. short_fade (<=26 / 27-97 / >=98) avgR 0.298/0.367/0.678, PnL/risk 0.331->0.687, t=3.21 (p=0.003); same-day f1 t=3.66; book 5d b5 t=3.22. OVS same-day own-count cells: 1 signal avgR 0.07 (N=76), 2: 0.08 (58), 3-4: 0.31 (112), 5-8: 0.27 (207), 9+: 0.48 (803). Cross-family breadth (distinct strategies firing that day) for dip_buy: 1 strat 0.05R (N=168), 2: 0.32 (340), 3: 0.55 (266), 4+: 0.73 (217). breakout f5 hi-lo -0.07R (t=-0.21); 2016-26 f5 hi-lo -0.89R (t=-1.68, N 24 vs 62).
findings.method: Ledger trades (OVS near/far tranches summed) joined to flow counts built from the re-generated candidate list; within-family terciles; mean-difference SE by episode-cluster bootstrap (episode = family signal dates <= 5 td apart, 600 resamples); per-year Spearman sign counts; 2005-15 vs 2016-26 era split; fills-based flow run as a cross-check.
findings.n: 3,483 trades 2003-2026 (3,360 from 2005): dip_buy 991 / oversold_hold 618 / short_fade 1,430 / breakout 321. Hi-flow episodes: dip_buy 68 (vs 253 lo), oversold_hold 20 (154), short_fade 26 (206).
findings.robustness: Per-year Spearman(flow,R) positive in 82% of 22 years (dip_buy f5), 82% (oversold_hold f5), 84% (short_fade f5), 58% (breakout). Era split f5 hi-lo: dip_buy +0.37R (t 1.9) 2005-15 / +0.24 (t 1.5) 2016-26; f21 +0.25 / +0.43 (t 2.3); oversold_hold +1.02 (N_hi=10) / +0.43 (t 2.1); short_fade +0.30 (t 1.5) / +0.41 (t 2.8). Same sign and larger t on the fills-based flow (dip f5 3.7, oversold 2.7, short 5.7), which is fill-selection-contaminated and therefore only a cross-check. 63d windows and book-level open-leg counts are weaker and less stable (see negatives).
findings.implication_for_sizing: For dip_buy / oversold_hold / short_fade, flow is an expectancy variable of about the same size as anything else in the book (top tercile earns 1.7-2.7x the PnL per unit risk of the bottom tercile). The sign is unambiguous: size up (or at least stop trimming) when many setups fire together; the 'crowded selloff' reading is wrong for this book. Breakouts get no flow rule.
findings.caveat: Outcome data are fills only (ledger); flow is measured on raw candidates BEFORE the earnings blackout and OVS T+1 gap gate, so OVS counts run ~16x its fills. Overflow-tier survivorship flatters levels, not the hi-vs-lo contrast.

findings.claim: The flow effect is not the dial, VIX, trend, realized vol or drawdown state in disguise; inside the dial's high zone the dip-buy effect disappears, which is where the frag/P-C bands already own sizing.
findings.numbers: Rank regression R ~ rank(f5) + rank(control), episode-clustered t on the flow term: dip_buy 4.32 alone -> 4.12 with VIX, 4.31 with SPY 21d return, 4.31 with SPY 21d realized vol, 4.21 with SPY drawdown; oversold_hold 4.06 -> 3.62 / 3.86 / 4.00 / 4.26; short_fade 3.26 -> 2.27 / 3.37 / 2.91 / 3.03. 2016-07+ with the lag-1 10d-MA 63d dial: dip_buy 2.17 -> 1.99 (dial t 0.23); oversold_hold 2.83 -> 4.62 with the dial term at t=-3.87 (flow high AND dial low is the best cell); short_fade 2.82 -> 2.83 (dial t 1.11). Spearman(f5, VIX) = 0.15 / 0.23 / 0.30; (f5, dial) = 0.06 / 0.36 / -0.42. Within dial terciles (2016+): dip_buy flow hi-lo +0.54R (t 2.1) at dial < 6, +0.28 at 6-30, +0.03 (t 0.1, N 55 vs 64) at dial >= 30. oversold_hold hi-lo +0.41 / +0.76 (t 2.0) / +0.64 (t 1.7) across dial terciles.
findings.method: OLS on percentile ranks with episode-cluster bootstrap SE (500 resamples); hi-vs-lo flow cells inside control terciles; controls from master_prices (SPY, ^VIX) and rd2_fragility (current-weights vintage, lag-1).
findings.robustness: Coefficient barely moves under any single control; the only material attenuation is VIX for short_fade (t 3.3 -> 2.3), consistent with breadth of overbought vol spikes partly being VIX itself.
findings.implication_for_sizing: A flow rule adds information beyond the dial and cannot be replaced by a VIX rule. The dip_buy flow boost should be gated OFF at dial >= 50 (the family bands already cut/zero there and the flow edge is absent in that zone); no gate is needed for oversold_hold or short_fade.
findings.caveat: Dial series is the current-weights recompute vintage before 2026-07-02, not PIT; the 2016+ dial-tercile cells are 20-80 trades each.

findings.claim: Family flow forecasts the sleeve's next-21d realized vol AND mean AND Sharpe together: high flow is high-variance and high-Sharpe, so vol-targeting against flow would cut exactly when the sleeve is best paid; at the sleeve level the growth-optimal per-leg size is roughly flat for the stacked families because variance rises with the (correlated) leg count.
findings.numbers: Spearman(trailing 5d family candidates, next-21d sleeve realized vol / mean): dip_buy 0.13 / 0.12, forward Sharpe hi-flow tercile 2.18 vs lo 1.60; oversold_hold 0.25 / 0.19, 2.54 vs 1.68; short_fade 0.41 / 0.29, 2.70 vs 1.30; breakout 0.32 / 0.11, 1.04 vs 0.81; book 0.18 / 0.26, 3.31 vs 1.75 (book flow5 partial rank coefficient on vol given trailing 21d vol: 0.17). Forward mu/var relative to unconditional (sleeve Kelly-relative), hi vs lo flow5 tercile: dip_buy 1.24 vs 0.93; book 1.32 vs 0.81; oversold_hold 0.94 vs 1.04; short_fade 1.08 vs 0.98.
findings.method: dist/data/strategy_daily.json per-strategy daily MTM collapsed to families (flat $750k); forward 21d realized vol/mean vs trailing candidate counts; per-year Spearman sign counts; forward mu/var by tercile.
findings.n: 3,414-5,319 sleeve-days per family, 2006-2026 (17-21 years).
findings.robustness: Per-year positive share (vol / mean): book flow5 81% / 76% of 21 years; short_fade 90% / 76%; oversold_hold 83% / 83%; dip_buy 76% / 90%; breakout 100% / 59%. flow63 is the least stable horizon (43-62% on mean).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Confirms the earlier book-level finding (sig5 Spearman 0.24 vol / 0.22 mean) at the family level and explains the walk-forward pattern below: flow buys expectancy per unit risk, and for stacked families it buys it with proportional variance, so the rule is a PnL/risk lever (and a growth lever under the brief's no-drawdown-constraint stance), not a Sharpe lever.
findings.caveat: Sleeve daily series includes flat days and mechanically scales with exposure; strategy_daily.json is the 2026-08-07 site build while the ledger runs to 2026-08-28.

findings.claim: Walk-forward (expanding window, annual re-fit, 2010-2026, cap re-applied): a per-family 5d-flow multiplier raises PnL per unit risk 4-15% and total PnL 4-20% with Sharpe flat-to-up in dip_buy and short_fade and flat in oversold_hold; every breakout variant is at or below baseline.
findings.numbers: Rule: tercile thresholds and mults = 1 + 0.5*(rpr_bucket/rpr_all - 1) clipped [0.5,1.5] fit on years < Y from 2005, applied to year Y, scaled to equal training risk, per-strategy 250 bps cap re-applied. dip_buy f5 two-sided: PnL $1.266M -> $1.523M (+20%), PnL/risk 0.466 -> 0.538, Sharpe 1.53 -> 1.57, maxDD -$72.6k -> -$76.6k, 15/17 years better, worst year -11%; f5 up-only +8.4%, 15/17, worst year -4%. oversold_hold f21 two-sided: $679k -> $810k (+19%), PnL/risk 0.541 -> 0.579, Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.33, maxDD -$39.4k -> -$53.4k, 13/17; f5 up-only +6.5% Sharpe 1.29 12/17; f21_rel two-sided +5%, Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.38, maxDD -$36.7k, 9/17. short_fade f5 two-sided: +3.7%, Sharpe 1.18 -> 1.19, 11/17; nstrat1 (distinct strategies firing) two-sided: $923k -> $1.013M (+9.8%), Sharpe 1.18 -> 1.21, maxDD unchanged, 15/17, worst year -3%. breakout: f5 two-sided Sharpe 0.90 -> 0.87, s21 0.79, f21_rel two-sided +11% PnL but maxDD -$82k -> -$106k. Book (f5 rules on the three reverting families, breakout down-only): PnL $3.51M -> $3.87M (+10.4%) at +3.2% risk, PnL/risk 0.491 -> 0.525, Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.25, maxDD -$92.9k -> -$98.4k, worst 21d -$71.4k -> -$69.3k, 15/17 years better. Final (2026) fits: dip_buy f5 q1=3,q2=5 mults [0.74,1.28,1.25]; oversold_hold f5 q1=2,q2=6 [0.80,0.92,1.38], f21 q1=5,q2=13 [0.75,0.99,1.36]; short_fade f5 q1=23,q2=104 [0.89,1.00,1.27]; nstrat1 dip_buy [0.77,1.15,1.45] (q1=2,q2=3).
findings.method: Per-trade daily MTM vectors rebuilt from master_prices closes and reconciled to booked PnL (max residual 0.00), so Sharpe/maxDD are true daily; cap re-applied per (strategy, signal date) using the recovered cap scale (placed total = cap/scale on bound days).
findings.n: OOS trades 2010-2026: dip_buy 775, oversold_hold 534, short_fade 1,227, breakout 248; 17 test years.
findings.robustness: Years-better and worst-year columns above; two-sided fitted mults never leave [0.74, 1.45]; the recency-normalised 21d form (f21_rel) is the only variant that improves maxDD in oversold_hold. oversold_hold's worst relative year (-80%) is 2012 on a $7k base.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Family-level 5d flow is the workhorse horizon; 21d adds for oversold_hold at a maxDD cost; same-day cross-family breadth (nstrat1) is the best single variable for short_fade. Expect roughly +4-10% book PnL for +3% risk with Sharpe unchanged-to-slightly-up.
findings.caveat: Fitted in-sample mults each year (shrunk 50%, clipped); early test years train on 2005-09 only. Ledger survivorship and the fills-only outcome set apply.

findings.claim: Unfitted fixed rule (0.75x at or below the low tercile, 1.25x at or above the high tercile) is Sharpe-neutral and PnL/risk-positive: flow sizing is a growth lever, and its up-only half is the part that pays; the down-size half is a variance/efficiency rule that costs PnL.
findings.numbers: Book 2010-2026, thresholds dip_buy f5 3/6, oversold_hold 2/7, short_fade 23/104 (breakout untouched), cap re-applied. Two-sided eq-risk: PnL +4.4% (+$153k), PnL/risk 0.491 -> 0.512, Sharpe 2.199 -> 2.195, maxDD -$92.9k -> -$102.4k, 13/17 years better, calendar-year bootstrap P(gain <= 0) = 0.0004 (5th pct +$74k). Up-only 1.25x: PnL +5.0% at +4.2% risk, Sharpe 2.197, maxDD -$102.8k, 17/17 years better, worst year +1%. Down-only 0.75x: PnL -5.7% at -9.1% risk, PnL/risk 0.509, Sharpe 2.207, maxDD -$87.6k (better), 3/17 years better. Per family (eq-risk two-sided): dip_buy PnL/risk 0.466 -> 0.494, Sharpe 1.521 -> 1.484; oversold_hold 0.541 -> 0.574, 1.327 -> 1.300; short_fade 0.407 -> 0.418, 1.177 -> 1.179; breakout 0.703 -> 0.675, 0.870 -> 0.812. Threshold sensitivity (dip_buy): t_hi 5 / 6 / 7 -> 12 / 7 / 6 of 17 years better, Sharpe 1.508 / 1.484 / 1.509; the fitted form's mid-bucket 1.28x (i.e. '<=3 -> 0.75x, else 1.25x') is what made the walk-forward Sharpe rise. Mults 0.5/1.5 are worse than 0.75/1.25 on Sharpe in every family (1.40 vs 1.48, 1.10 vs 1.30, 1.01 vs 1.18, 0.64 vs 0.81).
findings.method: Same replay engine as the walk-forward with pre-set multipliers and integer candidate-count thresholds (so the only in-sample choice is the threshold); year-block bootstrap of the annual gain.
findings.robustness: Up-only beats baseline in 17/17 years; two-sided in 13/17; sensitivity to +-1 on each threshold shown above (direction stable, magnitude moves 2-5 points of PnL).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Under the brief (drawdown not a binding constraint), ship the UP-only 1.25x leg; treat the 0.75x low-flow leg as the optional variance-neutral funding of it (two-sided eq-risk +4.4% PnL, Sharpe flat, maxDD +10%). Neither is a Sharpe improvement; both improve return per unit of ATR risk deployed.
findings.caveat: Thresholds are the 2026 expanding-window terciles (in-sample for the level, out-of-sample for the multipliers); the underlying flow must be counted from raw candidate masks live, not from staged rows.

findings.claim: The per-strategy 250 bps daily cap binds on exactly the high-flow, high-expectancy days, so it captures a NEGATIVE share of the flow effect: it fights the up-size the evidence supports. Partial relief (cap x1.5 on high-flow days) is free on every tail metric; full removal is not.
findings.numbers: Cap binds on 20.9% of trades (130 strategy-days). Share bound / mean cap scale in the top f5 tercile: dip_buy 11.8% / 0.96, oversold_hold 25.7% / 0.88, short_fade 78.0% / 0.38, breakout 0% / 1.00. avgR on cap-bound vs unbound trades: OVS 0.62 vs 0.20 (101 bound days, mean scale 0.35), Weak Close 0.96 vs 0.24 (11 days, 0.68), 3x ETF Overbot Fade 1.25 vs 0.52 (9 days, 0.52), LT Trend ST OS 0.49 vs 0.29 (4 days, 0.52), OLV 1.59 vs 0.69 (5 days, 0.74). Of a 1.25x up-size on hi-flow days, re-applying the cap removes 15% (dip_buy), 25% (oversold_hold), 83% (short_fade). Uncapped counterfactual on filled rows, top-f5 tercile: dip_buy PnL $553k -> $603k, oversold_hold $315k -> $365k, short_fade $371k -> $1.31M, but cap x99 on short_fade hi-flow days: Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -$44k -> -$127k (the cap does real tail work in OVS; worst OVS signal day -$26.7k capped). Unfitted relief, cap x1.5 on days in the family's top f5 tercile (thresholds from pre-2010 data): dip_buy +$31k (+2.4%), Sharpe 1.521 -> 1.542, maxDD and worst-21d identical; oversold_hold +$21k (+3.1%), Sharpe 1.327 -> 1.301, maxDD -$39.4k -> -$39.5k; short_fade +$77k (+8.3%), Sharpe 1.177 -> 1.184, maxDD/worst-21d identical; x2.0: dip +3.6% (Sharpe 1.552), short_fade +15.8% (Sharpe 1.173), maxDD identical. Book, cap x1.5 on hi-flow days for the three families: PnL +3.8% (+$132k), risk +2.0%, PnL/risk 0.491 -> 0.499, Sharpe 2.199 -> 2.222, maxDD -$92,866 vs -$92,867, worst-21d identical, 10/17 years better and the other 7 identical. Combined up-only 1.25x + cap x1.5: PnL +9.9%, risk +6.8%, Sharpe 2.224, maxDD -$102.8k (+10.7%), 17/17 years better.
findings.method: Per-row cap scale recovered as Risk_flat / (Risk bps x NAV x Size_Mult) (verified <= 1.0001 everywhere; Size_Mult is pre-cap by the engine's own comment); placed total on bound days = cap/scale exactly; relief replayed as new_scale = min(1, k x cap / placed); daily MTM Sharpe/maxDD as above.
findings.n: 2010-2026 OOS trades per family as above; hi-flow day shares 14-37% per family.
findings.robustness: Relief x1.5 leaves maxDD and worst-21d byte-identical in dip_buy and short_fade because the binding tail days are not the hi-flow-tercile days that get relief at k=1.5; the k=99 blow-up shows the tail is real and lives at the extreme of the same variable.
findings.implication_for_sizing: The cleanest flow rule in this study is on the cap, not on the base bps: a flow-aware cap (250 -> 375 bps effective on the family's top-tercile flow days) adds ~4% book PnL with Sharpe up and identical tails. Do not remove the cap on high-flow days; the tail protection at cap-scale 0.1-0.3 (OVS 9+ signal days) is what keeps OVS's worst day at -$27k.
findings.caveat: Relief replay assumes the same set of fills at higher size (fill-independent cap decision, as live). On non-bound days placed total is lower-bounded by filled nominal, so the rule's re-trim there is slightly understated. Live order_staging's placed totals should be checked against the ledger's implied ones before shipping.

findings.claim: Existing flow-shaped overlays are consistent with the evidence: OLV's recency ladder cuts the isolated (low-flow) signal, which is the weak one; 3x Bear Fade's same-day derate has no expectancy support and should be kept only as a variance rule; the 52wh deep-stack cut is consistent with breakouts having no flow edge.
findings.numbers: OLV rung x strategy 21d flow: at the 0.5x rung avgR 0.58 (low flow, N=91) / 0.77 (mid, 57) / 0.85 (high, 68); 0.7x rung 0.42 / 0.83 / 0.98 (N 19/22/18); 1.0x rung 0.58 / 1.26 / 0.94 (5/17/18). OLV open-leg count (fills, entered before signal day) hi vs lo: oversold_hold 0.849 vs 0.336, t=3.12, positive in 94% of years. 3x Bear ETF Overbot Fade same-day own-count cells: 1 -> 0.64R (N=30), 2 -> 0.37 (9), 3-4 -> 0.85 (16); its family-flow t (f5) = -0.11. 52wh Breakout same-day 1 vs 2: 0.50 vs 0.80 (N 215/32), no cap binding ever.
findings.method: Cross-tabs on the candidate-flow trade table.
findings.n: OLV 315 trades; 3x Bear Fade 55; 52wh 250.
findings.robustness: Directionally consistent with the plan's L2 findings (OLV leg-1 avgR 0.56-0.82 vs 1.1-1.4 for leg-3+).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Keep the OLV ladder; a flow multiplier composes with it (first-iteration OLV signal on a high-family-flow day = 0.5 x 1.25 = 0.625x). Do not add a flow-based down-size to 3x Bear Fade beyond the existing variance derate.
findings.caveat: Small cells for 3x Bear Fade; the OLV rung is per-ticker while flow is family-level.

recommendations.change: Flow-aware per-strategy daily cap for the three mean-reverting families (dip_buy, oversold_hold, short_fade); breakout unchanged
recommendations.rule: cap_bps = 250 normally; 375 (x1.5) on any day the family's trailing-5d raw candidate count (inclusive of today, counted from the same filter masks daily_scan already evaluates, BEFORE earnings blackout / T+1 gates) is at or above its tercile threshold: dip_buy >= 6, oversold_hold >= 7, short_fade >= 104. Applied in order_staging's per-strategy cap stage and the engine's cap post-pass (cap_bps x strat mult already exists as a hook). Never x99: full removal blows the OVS tail.
recommendations.expected_effect: 2010-2026 replay: book PnL +3.8% (+$132k), risk deployed +2.0%, PnL/risk 0.491 -> 0.499, Sharpe 2.199 -> 2.222, maxDD and worst-21d byte-identical (-$92.9k / -$71.4k). Per family: dip_buy +2.4% Sharpe 1.52 -> 1.54; short_fade +8.3% Sharpe 1.18 -> 1.18; oversold_hold +3.1% Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.30.
recommendations.confidence: moderate-high: unfitted rule (thresholds from pre-2010 data in the check), mechanical mechanism (the cap binds on avgR-0.62 OVS days vs 0.20 unbound), tails unchanged; verify live placed totals vs the ledger's implied ones first

recommendations.change: Up-only family flow multiplier on base bps (new sizing step after 2b, before the recency ladder; composes multiplicatively with every overlay)
recommendations.rule: mult = 1.25 when the family's trailing-5d candidate count >= threshold (dip_buy >= 6 AND dial 10d-MA 63d < 50; oversold_hold >= 7; short_fade >= 104), else 1.0. No breakout carrier. Optional variance-neutral funding: 0.75x when the count <= 3 / 2 / 23 respectively (two-sided form).
recommendations.expected_effect: Up-only, 2010-2026, cap re-applied: book PnL +5.0% at +4.2% risk, PnL/risk 0.494, Sharpe 2.197 (flat), maxDD -$92.9k -> -$102.8k, 17/17 years better, worst year +1%. Combined with the cap relief: +9.9% PnL, +6.8% risk, Sharpe 2.224, maxDD -$102.8k, 17/17. Two-sided eq-risk instead: +4.4% PnL at equal risk, Sharpe 2.195, maxDD -$102.4k, 13/17, year-bootstrap P(gain<=0)=0.0004. Fitted walk-forward form (mid bucket also 1.25x for dip_buy) did better: book +10.4% PnL, Sharpe 2.20 -> 2.25, 15/17.
recommendations.confidence: moderate: expectancy evidence is strong (t 2.7-3.3, per-year 82-84%, survives dial/VIX/trend controls, both flow sources) but the rule is Sharpe-neutral because high-flow legs are one correlated bet; this is a growth/appetite decision of exactly the kind the brief invites. Pre-register the post-ship review: PnL/risk on the first 60 hi-flow trades >= 1.3x the concurrent lo/mid-flow trades, else retire.

recommendations.change: Horizon and variable choice, per family
recommendations.rule: Use the family 5d count as the primary state (most stable year by year: 82-84% positive). oversold_hold may add the 21d count (f21 t 3.3, walk-forward +19% PnL) only if a 35% wider sleeve maxDD is acceptable; f21_rel (21d count / trailing-252d mean) is the maxDD-friendly form (Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.38, maxDD -$39k -> -$37k). short_fade's best single variable is same-day cross-family breadth nstrat1 (>= 3 strategies firing: walk-forward +9.8%, Sharpe 1.18 -> 1.21, 15/17) but it depends on the number of strategies in the book; keep as the second-stage candidate. Do not use 63d windows or book-level open-leg counts.
recommendations.expected_effect: See finding 4 for per-variable walk-forward numbers.

recommendations.rule: Keep the plan's 52wh 0.5x at >= 5 open legs as the family's only flow-shaped control; no cap relief (the cap never binds there); no family multiplier.
recommendations.expected_effect: Every breakout flow variant replayed at or below baseline Sharpe (0.87 base; 0.81-0.85 for two-sided forms); f21_rel two-sided +11% PnL with maxDD -$82k -> -$106k, rejected.
recommendations.confidence: high (negative result across 17 variables and 3 rule forms)

recommendations.change: Retain OLV recency ladder and 3x Bear Fade same-day derate as they are
recommendations.rule: OLV: unchanged (0.5x / 0.7x / 1.0x by trailing-21d own-ticker signal count); its direction agrees with the flow evidence (isolated signal is the weak one). 3x Bear Fade: keep same_day_signal_derate as a variance rule only; its cells show no expectancy gradient. A family flow multiplier composes on top (first-iteration OLV on a hi-flow day = 0.625x).
recommendations.expected_effect: None in expectation; prevents a wrong-signed 'crowded selloff' cut from being added to the family.

negative_results: Size-DOWN on high flow (the 'crowded selloff' hypothesis) is wrong-signed for every mean-reverting family: the top-flow tercile has the highest PnL per unit risk in dip_buy (0.572 vs 0.212), oversold_hold (0.835 vs 0.314) and short_fade (0.687 vs 0.331); the fixed down-only 0.75x rule costs 5.7% book PnL for 9.1% less risk.

Breakout family: none of 17 flow variables (own/family/book counts at 1/5/21/63d, breadth, open legs, relative flow) forecasts R at family level (cluster t between -1.5 and +1.0; s21_rel t 2.7 fails walk-forward with maxDD -$82k -> -$106k). Nothing to size.

63d flow windows add nothing beyond 5d/21d: sleeve-level flow63 has the weakest per-year stability (43-62% on forward mean); trade-level f63 t 3.0 (dip) / 1.3 (oversold) / 2.0 (short) with per-year positive shares 68% / 71% / 68%, below the 5d window.
Book-level open-leg count (open_b) is not a sizing state: t 0.09 (dip_buy), 2.4 (oversold_hold, which is just OLV stacks), 2.2 (short_fade), per-year stability 45-65%.

Full removal of the per-strategy cap on high-flow days (x99): short_fade Sharpe 1.18 -> 0.93, maxDD -$44k -> -$127k; oversold_hold Sharpe 1.33 -> 1.22. The cap's tail work in OVS (scale 0.1-0.35 on 9+ signal days) is real.
Aggressive fixed multipliers 0.5x/1.5x are worse than 0.75x/1.25x on Sharpe in every family (dip 1.40 vs 1.48, oversold 1.10 vs 1.30, short 1.01 vs 1.18, breakout 0.64 vs 0.81) and worse on maxDD.

Sleeve-level Kelly (forward mu/var) is flat with flow for oversold_hold (0.94 hi vs 1.04 lo) and short_fade (1.08 vs 0.98): flow raises per-trade expectancy but the extra legs are correlated, so no family flow rule improved daily Sharpe by more than ~0.05 in the unfitted replay. Flow-conditional sizing is not a Sharpe lever in this book.

Gating the dip_buy flow rule to dial < 50 changes little in dollars (-1.3% vs -0.8% for the ungated two-sided rule; band-zone trades are already 0.25x/zeroed) but the dial-tercile cell shows the effect is absent at dial >= 30 (+0.03R, t 0.1), so the gate is correct on evidence, not just on composition hygiene.
caveats: Flow is measured on engine RAW candidates re-generated this session (generate_candidates_fast with the full liquid+overflow book; earnings blackout, OVS T+1 gap tier, same-symbol precedence and fill-window are NOT applied to the counts). OVS therefore has ~16x more candidates than fills (20,740 vs 1,256). A live rule must count the same raw masks; counting staged rows would shift every threshold.

Outcomes are fills only (data/backtest_trades_full.parquet, full-rebuild ledger; overflow-tier survivorship flatters levels). Signals that never filled carry no R, so the hi-vs-lo contrast is on filled trades conditional on staged flow.

Cap-scale recovery assumes Risk_flat_750k = Risk bps x NAV x Size_Mult x cap_scale (engine comment: Size_Mult is pre-cap; verified cap_scale <= 1.0001 on all rows; 20.9% of trades bound, 130 strategy-days). On unbound days the placed total is lower-bounded by filled nominal, so re-trims of a boosted rule on those days are slightly understated (rule gains slightly overstated, by at most the 15-25% cap-absorption shares reported).

Walk-forward multipliers are fitted (shrunk 50%, clipped [0.5,1.5]) and the fixed-rule thresholds are the 2026 expanding-window terciles; early test years (2010-2012) train on 2005-2009 only. Episode clustering uses a 5-td gap; hi-flow episodes are few for oversold_hold (20-26) and short_fade (26-30).
Dial control uses data/rd2_fragility.parquet's 10d-MA 63d, lag-1, current-weights vintage (rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage, not PIT); the dial-tercile cells are 20-80 trades.

Sleeve-vol tests use dist/data/strategy_daily.json (2026-08-07 site build) while the ledger runs to 2026-08-28; replays rebuild per-trade daily MTM from adjusted master_prices closes reconciled to booked PnL (max residual 0.00), so Sharpe/maxDD levels differ slightly from the plan's strategy_daily-based numbers (book baseline Sharpe here 2.20 on 2010-2026).
The 'cap x1.5 on high-flow days' replay keeps the same fills at larger size (fill-independent cap, as live) and does not model any market impact of larger OVS baskets on 9+ signal days.

Other analysts' files share the scratch folder (cross_strategy_regime_*, cycle_macro_*, seasonality_flow_*, signal_quality_*, within_strategy_adds_*); this study's scripts and results are the flow_conditional_* files only. No repo code, config, tests or committed data were modified; the candidate dump downloaded three engine indicator-cache parquets from R2 into data/bt_indicator_cache/ as a side effect of the engine's normal caching.

findings.claim: Vol / drawdown STATE moves per-trade EDGE, not per-trade variance, book-wide and in both mechanism families: the book earns roughly 60% more R per unit risk when SPY is 3-10% off its 252d high (or realized vol is 12-30) than when SPY is within 3% of its high in dead-calm tape. sdR is flat across these states.
findings.numbers: Book trade level (2003+, regime at signal-date close): spy_dd<3 avgR 0.369 N=2659 vs 3-10 avgR 0.602 N=1234; diff vs rest -0.193 (t_cluster -3.08) and +0.203 (t +2.72); year-sign consistency 3 pos/19 neg (<3) and 17 pos/6 neg (3-10); sd_ratio 1.00/1.05. rv21<12 avgR 0.358 N=1974 (t -2.70, 4/16 years); VIX<15 0.352 N=1246 (t -2.20, 7/10); VIX 30+ 0.645 N=399 (t 1.84, 9/3); Kelly-relative (mu/var vs unconditional): VIX<15 0.70, 20-30 1.34, 30+ 1.34; spy_dd<3 0.82, 3-10 1.20. Daily basis (lag-1): VIX<15 Sharpe 1.29 (5.1 bps/d, sd 63) vs 20-30 2.54 vs 30+ 3.18 (17.7 bps/d, sd 88); rv21<12 1.36 vs 20-30 2.81; spy_dd<3 1.61 vs 3-10 2.57 vs 10-20 2.85. Families: mean-reversion family rv21<12 avgR 0.352 vs 0.504 (t -2.49, LOYO effect range -0.18..-0.12, 5/15 years), spy_dd<3 0.364 vs 0.538 (t -2.54, 3/19), VIX30+ 0.641 vs 0.422 (t 1.86, 10/2); momentum family (52wh, Sector BO) spy_dd<3 0.417 vs 1.190 (t -2.23, 2/6), 3-10 1.297 (t 2.18, 6/2).
findings.method: Trade-level avgR by regime bucket, CR1 cluster-robust t (in-regime trades clustered by regime episode with 21-session gap merge, out-of-regime by signal month), leave-one-year-out effect range and per-year sign counts; daily-basis Sharpe from strategy_daily.json with lag-1 regime; re-estimated on subsets outside live controls.
findings.n: 4,696 trades 2003-01 to 2026-08; daily series 2003-01 to 2026-08-07 (5,926 days); cell Ns as listed
findings.robustness: Survives outside every live control: on dial<50-or-pre-dial trades spy_dd<3 t -3.15 (N=2428), rv21<12 t -3.08 (N=1840); on Size_Mult>=0.99 trades t -3.33 / -2.90. Year-sign counts are the strongest in the study (3/19, 17/6, 4/16). Holds in both families with the same sign. sdR ratio 0.93-1.09 in every vol bucket, so it is an edge effect at the trade level; daily sd does rise with VIX (63 -> 88 bps) but mean rises faster.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Kelly-relative says ~0.7-0.8x in calm-at-highs tape and ~1.2-1.35x in 3-10% pullbacks / VIX 20-30. But converting this into a scalar buys little (see the negative results): family walk-forward on rv21 gives PPR 0.491 -> 0.532 (+8%), 14/17 years better, Sharpe 2.818 -> 2.834, maxDD -8.17 -> -7.41; fixed book 0.75x at rv21<12 gives Sharpe 2.515 -> 2.568, 18/22 years, +$142k risk-matched over 24y. Real edge gradient, small sizing value: the right place to use it is strategy mix (L1) and OLV's own tilt (finding 6), not a book scalar.
findings.caveat: Regimes are at the signal-date close (implementable in the PM scan); the gradient is partly between-year (pullback years are good years), which is why per-year timing captures only part of it. Mechanism is the liquidity-provision premium (reversal returns scale with VIX, Nagel 2012) and matches base rates from outside the repo.

findings.claim: The book's realized risk deployment is INVERTED relative to this edge gradient: it carries 3-4x more open risk in the calmest, lowest-edge tape than in stress, because the long-hold strategies (52wh 63d, OLV stacks, LT Trend) accumulate inventory in calm tape while stress is served by 2-5 day strategies. Book variance by regime is a position-count phenomenon, not a per-trade sdR phenomenon.
findings.numbers: Open risk (sum of Risk_flat over open trades, bps of NAV, lag-1 regime, 2005+): rv21<12 mean 204 / p90 412 vs rv21 30+ mean 51 / p90 152; VIX<15 204 vs VIX 30+ 73; spy_dd<3 191 vs 10-20 75 vs bear>20 55; midterm 184 (highest cycle bucket, p90 416). Signal flow (trades per 252 regime-days): 52wh 19.8 at VIX<15 vs 0 at 30+; OLV 30.9 at VIX 15-20, 6.8 at <15, 1.7 at 30+; IOB 30.9 at 30+ vs 4.7 at <15; MonFri 32.6 vs 6.7; book 154/yr at VIX<15 vs 284 at 20-30. Daily book sd 63 bps at VIX<15 vs 88 at 30+ despite the 3x open-risk gap.
findings.method: Daily open-risk reconstruction from ledger entry/exit dates; trade counts normalized by regime day counts.
findings.robustness: Structural (a bookkeeping fact of hold lengths), not a statistical estimate.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Explains the plan's finding that signal density predicts both vol and mean. Any regime control should act on the calm-tape INVENTORY builders (52wh/OLV/LT Trend base bps and holds), which is the L1 tilt and the P4 exit question, not a scalar on entries in stress where open risk is already low.
findings.caveat: Open risk is entry-risk (stop distance x shares) summed, not MTM exposure; flat $750k basis.

findings.claim: Presidential cycle: midterm years carry the lowest per-trade edge in the book and the highest daily variance, and 5 of 6 midterm years sit below the other-year mean; but the effect is concentrated in OVS (already tilted 0.75x) and the residual book-wide effect is not significant once clustered by year.
findings.numbers: Book trade level: midterm avgR 0.266 (N=1136) vs election 0.472 / post-election 0.556 / pre-election 0.510; t_cluster -4.63; LOYO effect range -0.28..-0.23; year-cluster Welch t -2.17 (6 midterm years vs 18; 5/6 below; midterm years 2006 0.36, 2010 0.54, 2014 0.17, 2018 0.24, 2022 0.27, 2026 0.19). Daily: midterm Sharpe 1.48 (7.7 bps/d, sd 82 = 1.14x) vs post-election 2.81, election 2.00, pre-election 1.71; Kelly-rel 0.59. Per strategy year-clustered: OVS path 1 midterm 0.156 vs 0.366, t -2.00, 6/6 years below; MonFri 0.247 vs 0.517 t -1.64 (3/4); IOB t -0.96; LT Trend t -0.91; 52wh t -0.96; OLV t +0.05; WCDS t +1.05 (opposite sign). Book ex-OVS: 0.376 vs 0.512, year t -1.33 (5/6 below). SPY in-sample base rate (calendar years 2001+): midterm mean +1.7% (median +12, min -21.6), post-election +17.1, pre-election +15.6, election +7.5; intra-year maxDD midterm -16.6% vs pre-election -11.8 / post -13.6. Signal flow midterm: OLV 18.2/yr vs 6.8-8.4 in election/pre-election, LT Trend 14.3, 52wh 13.1 vs 6.8 in election years; open risk highest.
findings.method: Trade-level clustered t and year-level Welch t (year = the only honest cluster for a calendar-year regime); SPY calendar-year returns and intra-year drawdowns by cycle year from master_prices.
findings.n: 6 midterm years (2006-2026) vs 18 others; 1,136 midterm trades
findings.robustness: Year-clustered t -2.17 book / -2.00 OVS; ex-OVS t -1.33 (not significant). H1/H2 split (0.219 vs 0.346) is inconsistent by year (H1 worse in 2006/2010/2022/2026, H2 worse in 2014/2018). Walk-forward per-strategy cycle table: d_PPR +0.001, Sharpe -0.10, maxDD -1.7pt worse; pooled book table: PPR +3.7%, Sharpe -0.045, maxDD -1.3pt. Fixed rule 0.75x midterm ex-OVS: Sharpe 2.515 -> 2.521, risk-matched maxDD -8.17 -> -8.63 (worse). Single-strategy WF OVS/cycle: PPR +8.6%, 9/17 years, Sharpe 1.10 -> 1.16.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Keep OVS cycle_risk_mults {2: 0.75} (re-confirmed 6/6). Do NOT extend a midterm cut to the book: Sharpe-neutral and worse drawdown after risk matching, because the book's drawdowns are not in midterm years (2008/2020 election, 2015 pre-election). The midterm phenomenon is better read as elevated inventory (OLV/LT Trend/52wh flow) in slow-resolving dips than as a sizing lever. Outside base rate (recalled, not computed here): since 1950 midterm years average the weakest returns and deepest intra-year drawdowns of the cycle (~-17%) with the low typically in Q2-Q3 and pre-election years positive ~90% of the time; consistent with the in-sample table.
findings.caveat: Six episodes; 2026 is in-sample and live; the SPY base-rate table is 6-7 years per bucket and dominated by 2008 (election) and 2022 (midterm).

findings.claim: The risk dial is a calm-at-highs instrument that is nearly orthogonal to, and mildly inversely related to, the vol/drawdown regimes. Consequently frag_risk_bands, pc_fear_bands and the dial_filters capture NONE of the vol-regime edge variation, and a vol-state control would act on disjoint days from the bands (no double counting).
findings.numbers: Days 2016-07+ (current-weights dial): P(dial>=50 | VIX 30+) = 3.9%, | rv21 30+ = 0.0%, | spy_dd 10-20 = 0.7%, | bear>20 = 0.0%, | spy_dd<3 = 20.7%; 86.6% of dial>=50 days have SPY within 3% of its high and 52% have rv21<12. PIT dial (2018+): P(pit>=50 | VIX 30+) = 3.2%, | rv21 30+ = 1.0%, | spy_dd<3 = 34%. P(pc_fear ON | VIX 30+) = 50%, | VIX<15 = 3.6%. Family band carriers (2016-07+): VIX 30+ cell N=66, share at dial>=50 = 0%, avgR 1.108; rv21 20-30 N=92, 0% at dial>=50, avgR 0.845; spy_dd 3-10 N=137, 5% at >=50. Regime effects re-estimated on dial<50-or-pre-dial trades are unchanged (spy_dd<3 t -3.15, rv21<12 t -3.08, midterm t -3.77).
findings.method: Day-level cross-tabs of each regime bucket vs the dial; trade-level cell re-estimation on subsets outside the live controls; family carriers split by dial>=50.
findings.n: 2,457 dial days; 2,343 PIT days; 4,696 trades
findings.robustness: Same picture on current-weights and PIT dial.
findings.implication_for_sizing: A vol/drawdown-state tilt and the fragility bands are complementary, not redundant: the bands quarter/zero the family at fragile highs, the vol gradient says the family (and OLV/OVS) earn most in 3-10% pullbacks and VIX 20-30, where the dial is almost never >=50. Nothing in the existing overlay stack already captures the vol-state gradient; the existing OVS cycle tilt captures the bulk of the cycle effect.
findings.caveat: Dial rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage; PIT series covers 2018-01 to 2026-05-07 (pit_signals.pkl end).

findings.method: Per-cell clustered t + LOYO; single-strategy walk-forward (Kelly-relative bucket multiplier fit on the strategy's own trades before year Y, shrink N0=30 toward 1, clip [0.5,1.5], applied to year Y; strategy-only PPR, risk-matched realized-at-exit Sharpe/maxDD, years-better count); fixed-rule ledger replays raw and risk-matched.
findings.n: OLV 299 trades 2010+ (315 total); 52wh 190; IOB 183; OVS P1 2,076
findings.robustness: OLV/spy_dd: 11/15 WF years, 16/17 fixed-rule years, survives every subset. Others: 8-10 of 16-17 years (coin flip) or N<45.
findings.implication_for_sizing: One shippable per-strategy candidate: OLV 1.25-1.5x when SPY is 3-10% off its 252d high at the signal close (composes with the recency ladder and ticker cap; OLV is bandless so no dial interaction). The rest are prereg-or-park.
findings.caveat: Multiple comparisons: 14 axes x ~4 buckets x 16 strategies ~ 900 cells; ~45 |t|>2 cells expected by chance, so only cells with a mechanism + LOYO + walk-forward are cited. OLV ledger survivorship (overflow tier) flatters absolute avgR; the relative state effect is less exposed.

findings.claim: Which regimes move VARIANCE rather than edge: at the trade level almost none (sdR ratio 0.93-1.09 everywhere except bear>20 0.80 and 12-1-momentum-negative 0.90); at the daily book level variance rises in backwardation, P/C fear ON, VIX 30+, spy_dd 3-10 and midterm years, but only credit widening and midterm years raise variance WITHOUT raising the mean.
findings.numbers: Daily book (lag-1): backwardation sd 104 bps (1.45x) mean 19.0 bps (2.1x) Sharpe 2.89; VIX 30+ sd 88 (1.22x) mean 17.7 (2.0x) Sharpe 3.18; spy_dd 3-10 sd 88 (1.21x) mean 14.2 (1.6x) Sharpe 2.57; pc_fear ON sd 90 (1.25x) mean 12.2 (1.37x) Sharpe 2.15 vs mid 2.29; credit widening sd 87 (1.20x) mean 9.1 (1.02x) Sharpe 1.66 vs flat 2.43; midterm sd 82 (1.14x) mean 7.7 (0.86x) Sharpe 1.48; mom12-1 negative sd 54 (0.74x) Sharpe 2.53 vs pos 1.95; bear>20 sd 47 (0.66x) Sharpe 1.97; SPY below 200d sd 69 (0.95x) Sharpe 2.36 vs above 1.92. Per-strategy variance-only cells (N>=15): St OS Sznl election years sdR 2.39 (1.40x) / rising rates 2.17; IOB VIX 15-20 sdR 1.57 (1.26x, avgR 0.11); 3x ETF Overbot Fade pre-election sdR 0.95 (0.67x).
findings.method: Daily sd/mean ratios vs unconditional; trade sdR ratios; classification edge / variance / both.
findings.n: 5,926 days; cells as listed
findings.robustness: Descriptive; the credit-widening and midterm variance-up-edge-flat pattern is consistent with the open-risk reconstruction (both are high-inventory states).
findings.implication_for_sizing: No variance-only regime justifies a cut: where variance rises, mean rises more (Kelly-relative >1), and the two exceptions (credit widening, midterm) are inventory-driven and already Sharpe-neutral under a cut. Bear-market / negative-momentum tape is LOWER variance with equal-or-better Sharpe, so a trend-state cut is wrong-signed.
findings.caveat: Daily series is flat-basis MTM through 2026-08-07; realized-at-exit replays understate intra-hold variance.

findings.claim: How much the existing controls already capture: cycle_risk_mults captures most of the cycle effect (OVS is 46% of midterm trades and the only strategy with a year-clustered t <= -2); frag_risk_bands / pc_fear_bands / dial_filters capture none of the vol-state gradient (they act on disjoint days); P/C fear state has no book-level edge content on its own.
findings.numbers: OVS midterm: Size_Mult mean 0.41 vs 0.61-0.69 in other cycle years (tilt is live in the ledger); OVS P1 midterm by year 2006 0.36, 2010 0.29, 2014 -0.16, 2018 0.11, 2022 0.24, 2026 0.10, all below the 0.366 other-year mean. Book ex-OVS midterm year t -1.33. pc_fear book cells: fear ON diff +0.026 (t 0.28, 9/8 years), complacent +0.074 (t 0.92), mid -0.074 (t -1.04); family carriers 2016-07+ pc_fear ON N=106, 16% at dial>=50 (avgR 0.746 there vs 0.730 below). Family live vs Size_Mult-stripped PnL by VIX: 30+ $231k live vs $274k unbanded (Size_Mult 0.82 from derates/overrides, not bands); <15 $189k vs $217k. 52wh dial_filters <30 confines it to calm tape where rv21<12 is 65% of its trades at 0.30R (its worst cell) while its 12-20 cell is 0.99R: the dial gate and the vol gradient point in different directions for 52wh.
findings.method: Ledger Size_Mult audit by regime; cell re-estimation on subsets; cross-tabs.
findings.n: as listed
findings.robustness: Structural / descriptive.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Nothing proposed here double-counts an existing overlay. The one interaction worth noting is 52wh: a rv21 tilt would cut the majority of its dial-gated trades, i.e. it is really an L1 base-bps or an exit (P4) question.
findings.caveat: Size_Mult embeds every live overlay plus scale-out tranches (OVS P1 Size_Mult ~0.57 reflects 40/60 tranche rows), so it is only a coarse attribution.

Pooled book tables on the vol axes do better on PPR (+6-8%, 13-15/17 years) but are Sharpe-flat (+0.01 to -0.03).

SPY 200d trend and 12-1 momentum: no edge effect (diff +-0.004 / +0.066); the below-200d / negative-momentum tape is LOWER variance (0.95x / 0.74x) with higher Sharpe (2.36 / 2.53), so a trend-state cut is wrong-signed. spy_200 per-strategy WF: maxDD -12.1 (worst of all axes).

Era/episode artefacts rejected without a mechanism: 3x ETF Overbot Fade election-year cell (1.78R, N=29, t 7.8; 2020/2024) and P/C-complacent cell (2.03R, N=19); Monday Dip 12-1 momentum cell (rest N=9); St OS Sznl contango-mild (-0.43R, N=23, sdR 2.3); 3x Leader Gap Fade credit-flat (N=16).

IOB credit-widening / VIX-level tables improve IOB maxDD dramatically (-8.3 -> -5.2 / -3.5) but on 8-9 of 17 years: a one-episode (Aug-2015) effect, not a regime rule.
Weak Close Decent Sznls: every regime table is negative out of sample (credit21 -11%, rv21 -11% PPR); its midterm effect is the opposite sign of the book's (+1.05 year t).
caveats: Dial vintage: rows before 2026-07-02 in data/rd2_fragility.parquet are the recompute vintage (drift up to ~7 pts on 63d); all 'current' dial cells use it. The PIT dial (cycle_macro_pit_dial.parquet) was rebuilt with the scratch/pit_reestimate.py method and covers 2018-01-01 to 2026-05-07 (pit_signals.pkl end), so the Aug-2026 episode is current-weights only.

Trade regimes are evaluated at the SIGNAL-DATE close (implementable in the PM scan); P/C fear is lag-1 like pc_fear.py; daily-series regimes are lag-1. A live rule would see the same information the study used.

R_Multiple is size-independent, but PnL_flat_750k and Size_Mult already embed every live overlay (frag bands, P/C tables, recency ladder, earnings override, cycle mult, derates, OVS tranches) - rule replays therefore compose ON TOP of the live book, and 'risk-matched' scales the whole rest of the book uniformly by base_risk/new_risk.

Rule and walk-forward replays use realized-at-exit daily PnL (exit-date booking), not MTM; Sharpe levels differ from the plan's MTM numbers (2.5 vs 2.8) and intra-hold variance is understated; maxDD differences are indicative only.

Multiple comparisons: ~900 strategy x bucket cells across 14 axes; ~45 cells with |t|>2 are expected by chance. Findings cite only cells with a mechanism plus LOYO plus walk-forward. Year-sign counts treat each year as one observation regardless of N.

Episode clustering: in-regime trades are clustered by regime episode (runs merged across gaps < 21 sessions), out-of-regime by signal month; for long-run regimes (SPY above 200d, momentum positive) this leaves very few in-regime clusters (14-89) and the t-stats there are conservative.
Walk-forward fits depend on the shrinkage (N0=50 pooled/family, 30 single-strategy) and clip [0.5,1.5]; different priors move the small gains by a few percent but not their sign.

Ledger survivorship flatters OLV/overflow absolute avgR; relative regime effects are less exposed but not immune. Six presidential cycles is a small-episode inference by construction; 2026 is in-sample and live.

Outside base rates cited for the presidential cycle (post-1950 midterm weakness and ~-17% intra-year drawdowns, pre-election ~+16%) are recalled from the literature, not computed here; the in-sample 2001+ SPY table is 6-7 years per bucket and dominated by 2008 and 2022.
Daily per-strategy series (strategy_daily.json) end 2026-08-07; the ledger runs to 2026-08-28. Nothing in the repo was modified; all outputs live under scratch/ultracode_sizing_2026-09-02/.
