findings.claim: OVS (Overbot Vol Spike) expectancy rises monotonically with the extremity of its own short-window rank filters: the bottom tercile of signals (mean of rank_2d/5d/10d/21d below ~94) earns roughly a third of the rest. This is the one within-strategy quality tier that clears every pre-registered bar (N, monotone, cluster t, LOYO >= 70%, mechanism).
findings.numbers: Terciles of filter extremity (mean rank minus the 85 threshold): T0 avgR +0.18 (N 423, win 0.59, sd 1.08), T1 +0.45 (N 423, win 0.70, sd 0.99), T2 +0.51 (N 424, win 0.72, sd 1.06); Spearman +0.16; episode-clustered t +5.38 (217 episodes); LOYO sign agreement 80% of 20 usable years; by-year Spearman positive in 17/24 years. Fixed cut mean rank <94: N 392 avgR +0.17 win 0.59 vs >=94 N 878 avgR +0.47 win 0.71 (mu/sigma^2 ratio 3.1x). Holds in Liquid (0.13 / 0.45 / 0.54 by cell) and Overflow (0.19 / 0.44 / 0.49), inside path 1 (0.29 / 0.52 / 0.67, N 191/236/234) and path 2 (0.06 / 0.36 / 0.29, N 201/223/185), and in all four eras (T0 = 0.16 / 0.22 / 0.20 / 0.16 vs T2 = 0.67 / 0.38 / 0.53 / 0.41 for 2003-09 / 2010-16 / 2017-21 / 2022-26). Multivariate with the T+1 gap (the live 2-path variable) and 5-day book signal count: extremity t +2.60 independent of gap (t +5.18) and density (t +5.44); rank_252d adds nothing (t -0.82). Single windows: rank_5d (<92: +0.19, N 295; >=97: +0.52, N 502) and rank_10d (+0.17 / +0.46) carry it; rank_2d weaker (+0.28 / +0.50); rank_21d saturated (779/1270 at >=97 because of the 3-consecutive rule). Fixed rule 0.5x at <94 on equal total risk: 17/24 years better, R per unit risk 0.298 -> 0.337 (+12.9%), daily PnL sd x1.06, worst year -$13.9k (2020, the 228-trade cluster year); symmetric version (<94 0.5x, >=97 1.25x): 16/24 years, +16.5%, sd x1.08. Walk-forward tercile version (cut-points and multipliers refit each year on expanding history, risk-neutral): +19.7% PnL, 13/18 years better, worst year -$14.9k. Threshold sensitivity for the bottom cut: <92 13/24 +2.1%, <93 17/24 +7.6%, <94 17/24 +12.9%, <95 17/24 +13.3%, <96 18/24 +10.1%. If NOT redeployed the cut costs -$36k over 24 years (half of the cell's $72k PnL) against $607k OVS total, while removing 33% of OVS staged risk.
findings.method: Collapsed-tranche ledger trades; within-strategy terciles; OLS of R on the z-scored feature with episode-clustered sandwich SE (episodes = OVS signals chained while gaps <= 5 td); LOYO with training-year cut-points; fixed-rule year-by-year evaluation with the multiplier rescaled so risk-weighted mean = 1 (a rule cannot win by adding risk); expanding-window walk-forward tercile sizing.
findings.n: 1,270 OVS trades (2,483 tranche rows), 217 episodes, 24 years; bottom cell N 392
findings.robustness: Survives LOYO (80%), both universe tiers, both gap paths, all four eras, conditioning on gap and signal density, and a threshold sweep 93-96. Not robust to: the single worst year (2020) under risk-neutral redeployment; midterm years (bottom cell +0.10 N 87 vs +0.17 N 183 above it, i.e. the whole strategy is weak in midterm years, gradient flattens).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Implementable in daily_scan from the same rank_ret_{2,5,10,21}d columns the filter already reads and replayable point-in-time in the engine. Propose a bottom-tier cut (0.5x when mean short-window rank < 94), NOT a top-tier boost: the gradient is mostly 'bottom tercile is half expectancy', the boost adds only +3.6% for one fewer winning year, and the P1 60 bps size already sits at the strategy's exact-Kelly f* per the plan's L1 table. Composes multiplicatively with path/cycle/scale-out/caps. Win rate and expectancy move together here (+0.12 win, +0.30R), so this is not the deleted meta-labeller's P(win) trap.
findings.caveat: Cut-point 94 and multiplier 0.5 were chosen after seeing the tercile tables; the walk-forward tercile version (+19.7%, 13/18) is the clean out-of-sample check. Rule evaluation ignores the per-strategy 250 bps and P2 aggregate caps (a smaller bottom cell frees cap room on cluster days, which if anything helps); engine replay needed before ship. Ledger survivorship flatters the overflow tier.

findings.claim: Book-wide signal flow (trailing 5-session signal count) tiers per-trade expectancy across most strategies: quiet-book signals are half-expectancy. But it is not a per-trade sizing tier: the edge is already expressed mechanically (more signals -> more risk deployed) and the year-by-year fixed rule fails for OVS; the finding belongs to the cap layer.
findings.numbers: Pooled strategy-fixed-effect slope +0.148R per 1 sd of book_sig_5td, cluster t +3.90 (1,317 episodes), LOYO 75% of 24 years. Lo-vs-hi tercile positive in 10 of 13 strategies: OVS 0.19 -> 0.53 (N 423/468, LOYO 91%/11), LT Trend ST OS 0.06 -> 0.45 (N 66/94, LOYO 100%/8), OLV 0.43 -> 0.84, IOB 0.04 -> 0.49, WCDS 0.20 -> 0.44, 3x Bear 0.10 -> 0.75 (N 17/23); negative: 52wh 0.93 -> 0.39 (N 58/136), MonFri 0.50 -> 0.46, Sector BO, St OS Sznl (small N). Fixed rule OVS book_sig_5td <= 3 -> 0.5x: only 9/24 years better (+9.7% R/risk, gain concentrated in 2009/2016/2020/2021 cluster years); walk-forward tercile version +27.3% 12/18 but same-day count version -33.6% 4/18 (unstable). LT Trend ST OS <= 2 -> 0.5x: cells +0.12 (N 101, win 0.56) / +0.51 (N 81) / +0.39 (N 64); 12/17 years better, +18.3%, LOYO 73%, t +2.25. Cap interaction: strategy-days staging >= 240 bps (cap-bound) carry risk-weighted avgR 0.84 (9 days, 56 trades) vs 0.41 on <100 bps days (2,009 days); OVS days with 7+ signals average avgR 0.75 across 348 trades on 19 days, with mean staged risk only 111 bps because the P2 aggregate cap (112.5 bps effective) binds.
findings.method: Pooled OLS with strategy demeaning and episode-clustered SE; per-strategy terciles; fixed-rule yearly evaluation on equal risk; day-level risk-weighted avgR by staged-bps bucket from the ledger's filled rows.
findings.n: 3,483 trades / 1,317 episodes pooled; OVS 1,270; LT Trend 246
findings.robustness: Sign robust (LOYO 75% pooled, 10/13 strategies) but the per-trade rule is cluster-year dependent (OVS 9/24). Non-monotone for LT Trend (peak in the middle tercile).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not add a per-trade upsizing multiplier on signal density: it would compound concentration on exactly the days the caps exist to bound, and the plan's L4 already showed signal density predicts book vol and mean equally. Where the evidence bites is the cap design: cap-bound days are the highest-expectancy days (0.84 vs 0.41), so any cap loosening should come from this layer (see the OVS P2 cap finding). The LT Trend quiet-book cut is better expressed through the family market-pullback band below (same mechanism).
findings.caveat: Signal counts are FILLED ledger signals (staged-but-unfilled invisible), so live counts run higher; rule cut-points would need re-basing on the scanner's staged count. book-wide count is a cross-strategy state, not a within-strategy feature.

findings.claim: The OVS path-2 aggregate daily cap (0.75% nominal / 1.125% effective) trims the best path-2 days and bounds almost nothing.
findings.numbers: 202 of 609 P2 trades were capped (Size_Mult below the 0.2 nominal); capped trades avgR +0.37 vs uncapped +0.18 (capping happens on cluster days, which are the good days). Uncapping all P2 rows to the 12 bps effective size: +$49.5k over 24 years = 8.1% of OVS total PnL ($607k); worst single-day extra -$1.4k, best +$11.9k; positive in 11 of the 14 years with any capping.
findings.method: Counterfactual from the ledger's Size_Mult: uncapped risk = 12 bps x cycle mult x $750k; extra PnL = (uncapped - booked risk) x R, summed by day and year.
findings.n: 609 P2 trades, 202 capped, 14 capping years
findings.robustness: 11/14 years positive; concentrated in 2009/2016/2020/2021/2023 cluster years by construction.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Raise or remove the P2 aggregate cap (e.g. 0.75% -> 1.5% nominal). It is the one OVS cap whose bound (-$1.4k worst extra day) is smaller than the expectancy it forgoes; the per-strategy 250 bps cap still bounds the worst day. Combined with the extremity cut above, the freed cap room goes to higher-extremity P2 rows (P2 low-extremity cell is +0.06R, N 201).
findings.caveat: The plan's cap study kept the 250 bps per-strategy cap for the worst single day; this finding is about the separate P2 aggregate cap only. Engine replay with the cap raised is the confirmation step.

findings.claim: Single-stock dip-buys (OLV, LT Trend ST OS, Weak Close Decent Sznls, Monday Dip) earn half their expectancy when SPY is within 2% of its 252-day high; the mechanism is mostly beta (index pullbacks in uptrends recover over the hold), so it is a market-timing tilt rather than idiosyncratic alpha. It clears the LOYO bar at the family level but OLV alone does not walk forward.
findings.numbers: Family cells: SPY > -2% from high N 425 avgR +0.31 win 0.62 vs <= -2% N 570 avgR +0.61 win 0.73 (mu/sigma^2 2.6x). Per strategy near-high vs off-high: OLV +0.44 (N 146) vs +1.04 (N 169); LT Trend +0.18 (51) vs +0.36 (195); WCDS +0.24 (166) vs +0.50 (102); Monday Dip +0.24 (49) vs +0.65 (59); St OS Sznl reversed +0.45 (13) vs +0.31 (45). Pooled strategy-FE cluster t -2.87; LOYO 73% of 22 years; fixed rule 0.5x near-high on equal risk: 15/24 years better, R/risk 0.411 -> 0.466 (+13.4%), worst year -$37k; threshold sweep -1/-2/-3/-5%: 17/15/15/12 years better, +5.8/+13.4/+10.8/+8.3%. Era: near-high +0.17/-0.12/+0.58/+0.33 vs off-high +0.30/+0.54/+0.80/+0.73 (2017-21 nearly flat). Beta channel: SPY forward 10-day return after the signal +1.25% off-high vs +0.46% near-high; for OLV, R loads 0.26R per 1% SPY over the hold (t 6.5) and the gradient's t falls from -2.47 to -1.40 on the SPY-residual (residual by tercile 1.00 / 0.57 / 0.70, non-monotone). OLV-only walk-forward tercile sizing: spy_hi252_dist -6.2% (5/9 years), spy_ret21 +3.8% (7/9), breadth_chg21 +6.8% (8/9). Index dip-buys show the OPPOSITE (MonFri near-high +0.54 vs +0.37/+0.46; IOB +0.59 vs +0.29/+0.34).
findings.method: Pooled OLS with strategy demeaning and episode-clustered SE; LOYO on the binary flag; fixed-rule yearly evaluation on equal risk; alpha/beta decomposition by regressing OLV R on SPY hold return and re-testing the gradient on the residual.
findings.n: 995 family trades; OLV 315 / LT Trend 246 / WCDS 268 / Monday Dip 108 / St OS Sznl 58
findings.robustness: Family LOYO 73%, 4 of 5 strategies agree, threshold-stable from -1% to -3%; weak in 2017-21; OLV alone fails walk-forward; largely a beta effect.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Candidate FAMILY band (not per-strategy): 0.5x on OLV, LT Trend ST OS, WCDS, Monday Dip when SPY closes within 2% of its 252d high; exclude St OS Sznl and every index dip-buy. It is PIT-clean (a price state, no fitted weights) unlike the retired OLV dial band, but it is a market-timing bet with a base-rate rationale (post-2000 short-horizon index mean reversion after pullbacks in uptrends), so it must be judged alongside the plan's L3 hedge, which removes part of the same factor: if the hedge ships, re-test on hedged returns before adding the band. Pre-register rather than ship.
findings.caveat: The near-high cell overlaps the high-dial episodes (distribution at highs); a rule here partly re-creates the retired OLV dial cut by another name. Worst year -$37k under risk-neutral redeployment.

findings.claim: Within-strategy gradients on the risk dial are an artifact of the current-weights recompute vintage: on identical OLV trades the point-in-time dial shows no gradient. Do not tier any strategy on the live dial series.
findings.numbers: OLV terciles on the current-weights dial: +1.16 / +0.78 / +0.49 (N 86 each, cluster t -3.24, LOYO 80% of 5 years); on the same 211 trades with the sibling PIT vintage-lagged dial: +1.22 / +0.67 / +0.98 (t +0.03, non-monotone). Multivariate 2016+: current dial t -2.90 next to spy_ret21 t -2.51; with dial_pit instead: dial_pit t +0.32. Pooled across strategies: current dial slope -0.09R/sd t -1.99 (LOYO 82%/11) vs PIT dial -0.05R/sd t -1.21 (LOYO 56%/9). OVS dial terciles +0.42 / +0.40 / +0.26 (t -1.46, n.s.).
findings.method: Same tercile / clustered-t / LOYO battery run on both dial vintages over the common trade set.
findings.n: 211 OLV trades with both vintages; 2,104 trades with a dial reading
findings.robustness: The current-vintage result is itself LOYO-stable, which is exactly what calibration lookahead produces; the PIT check is decisive.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Confirms retiring the OLV band and the repo's PIT discipline; every dial-conditioned within-strategy claim (including the plan's trade-level 65+ table) must be re-scored on the PIT series before it sizes anything. Price-state substitutes (SPY off-high, 21d return, breadth change) carry the same information without the lookahead.
findings.caveat: PIT dial series is the sibling analyst's reconstruction (cross_strategy_regime_pit_dial.parquet, 2017+ with 10d MA); its vintage weights are per-year re-estimates, not the live weights.

findings.claim: Existing overlays vs the evidence: the OLV recency ladder cuts the weakest rung and is directionally right; the OLV PRE-earnings size override sits on a cell with no expectancy or tail deficit, while the deficit lives POST-print (a near-miss); the gap-up derate's gradient exists in WCDS too (uncarried) and not in IOB; the St OS Sznl override and 3x Bear same-day derate are consistent with the ledger.
findings.numbers: OLV recency rungs (ledger proxy = prior filled OLV signals in 21 td): rung0 +0.68 (N 206, win 0.70), rung1 +0.82 (N 72), rung2+ +1.11 (N 37); 2016+: +0.74 / +0.79 / +1.05. OLV pre-earnings override cell (-10..0 td to print): N 57 avgR +0.80 win 0.70 sd 1.50 worst -2.9 vs rest N 258 +0.75 win 0.72 sd 1.39 worst -2.9; regression flag slope -0.08R (t -0.34). OLV post-print: 0-10 td since earnings +0.16 (N 18), 11-21 +0.44 (N 68), 22-42 +0.71 (N 71), 43+ +0.99 (N 149); <=21 td flag slope -0.53R (t -1.97), cells +0.38 (N 86, win 0.63) vs +0.90 (N 229, win 0.76); LOYO only 60% of 15 years; by era <=21 vs rest: 2003-09 +1.02 vs -0.49 (N 10/6, reversed), 2010-16 +0.39 vs +0.82, 2017-21 +0.84 vs +1.01, 2022-26 -0.15 (N 34) vs +0.92; fixed 0.5x rule 11/17 years +9.8%. Earnings-calendar coverage of OLV trades 100/100/99/91% by era. St OS Sznl override cell (-5..-1 td): N 9 avgR -0.49 vs +0.47 outside. Gap-up > 0.25 ATR vs rest: Monday Dip +0.31 (N 31) vs +0.53, MonFri +0.24 (N 78) vs +0.51 (t -1.73), WCDS +0.23 (N 91) vs +0.40 (t -0.92, LOYO 67%/18, fixed 0.5x rule 16/22 years +11.6%), dip-buy family pooled t -1.78; IOB opposite +0.52 (N 37) vs +0.32; live carriers' fixed-rule scores: MonFri 16/23 years +3.8%, Monday Dip 9/15 +1.9%. 3x Bear same-day: n=1 +0.68 (N 35), n=2 +0.64 (N 10), n>=3 +0.58 (N 10). None of the OLV market-state gradients is captured by the rung (partial t after conditioning on rung: spy_ret21 -2.97 -> -2.97, breadth_chg21 -3.94 -> -4.09).
findings.method: Cell comparisons on the collapsed ledger; regression with both earnings-window flags plus SPY off-high; LOYO on binary flags; fixed-rule yearly evaluation.
findings.n: OLV 315 (301 with earnings data); WCDS 268; MonFri 348; Monday Dip 108; 3x Bear 55
findings.robustness: Ladder direction stable 2016+; post-earnings deficit era-concentrated (2022-26) and LOYO 60%; WCDS gap gradient consistent in sign with the two live carriers but weak on its own.
findings.implication_for_sizing: (1) Keep the OLV ladder. (2) Review the basis of the OLV pre-earnings override: 57 ledger trades show neither lower avgR nor a worse tail; unless it exists for an un-modelled reason (live gap risk through the print), restoring base size recovers expectancy; moving the window to <=21 td AFTER the print is the near-miss to re-examine at +20 trades. (3) Extend gap_size_derate to WCDS (same entry type, same magnitude as the carriers); do not extend to IOB or Monthly Weak Close. (4) St OS Sznl override and 3x Bear derate: leave.
findings.caveat: Rung counts are filled-signal proxies (live mask counts run higher). The pre-earnings cell holds through the print by construction, so any live damage would have to be a fill/gap effect the engine does not model.

findings.claim: 52wh Breakout signals opened in very quiet SPY tape (21d realized vol < 10%) earn a quarter of the rest; near-miss on LOYO, collinear with VIX.
findings.numbers: SPY rv21 < 10%: N 114 avgR +0.19 win 0.32 sd 1.92; 10-14%: N 87 +0.70 win 0.46; >= 14%: N 55 +0.95 win 0.56. Tercile version +0.10 / +0.54 / +0.93, cluster t +2.01 (149 episodes), LOYO 80% of 10 years; quintiles +0.33 / +0.18 / +0.31 / +0.91 / +0.91 (a step near the 60th percentile, not a smooth gradient). Fixed rule 0.5x below 10%: 12/18 years better, R/risk 0.527 -> 0.622 (+18.1%), day-sd x1.08, worst year -$7.4k, cluster t +2.44; binary LOYO 64% of 14 years. Multivariate spy_rv21 t +0.58, VIX t +1.13, dist200 t -0.13 (rv21 and VIX are the same state).
findings.method: Terciles, clustered t, LOYO, fixed-rule yearly evaluation; walk-forward tercile sizing +27.7% (10/17 years, worst -$11.3k).
findings.n: 256 trades, 149 episodes (63-day holds cluster heavily)
findings.robustness: Fails the 70% LOYO bar on the binary (64%); tercile LOYO 80%; 10/17 walk-forward years.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Mechanism is plausible (vol clustering plus the leverage effect: a 63-day momentum hold opened at a realized-vol trough spans a likely vol expansion, which for equities is down-skewed; the plan's L3 already shows 52wh loses -2.2 Sharpe when the dial rises during holds). Pre-register a 0.5x tier at SPY rv21 < 10% (or VIX < ~13) and grade it with the exit-side P4 protocol rather than shipping on this evidence.
findings.caveat: Few independent episodes; 52wh is the strategy the plan's L1 cuts to 0.73 already, so a further 0.5x on 45% of its signals compounds to a large footprint cut.

findings.claim: Negative results across the requested feature families: ATR% of price, distance from the 200d SMA, liquid-vs-overflow tier, days since the strategy's last signal in the ticker, VIX level, P/C fear state, sector breadth, OLV's own filter extremity and 52wh open-leg count do NOT tier expectancy inside any major strategy at the pre-registered bar.
findings.numbers: ATR%: OVS terciles +0.33 / +0.41 / +0.40 (t +0.99), OLV +1.13 / +0.43 / +0.73 (non-monotone), 52wh +0.70 / +0.41 / +0.48; consistent with the plan's L0. Distance from 200d SMA: OVS +0.43 / +0.34 / +0.37 (t -0.81), OLV +0.71 / +0.82 / +0.75. Liquid vs overflow avgR: OVS +0.39 (N 316) vs +0.38 (954) t -0.12; 52wh +0.54 (60) vs +0.52 (196); LT Trend +0.40 (61) vs +0.29 (185) t -0.93; OLV +0.97 (87) vs +0.68 (228) t -1.34; ATR Ext Gap +1.25 (12) vs +0.69 (59); St OS Sznl +1.02 (11) vs +0.18 (47) t -2.19 (only N 11 liquid). Days since last signal: no strategy passes (OVS +0.38 / +0.24 / +0.39). VIX: pooled +0.11R/sd t +3.63 but LOYO 67%; within strategy nothing passes (OVS +0.30 / +0.33 / +0.51 t +1.81; 52wh t +2.06 LOYO 60%; Monday Dip non-monotone). P/C fear pct (lag-1): LT Trend +0.52 / +0.27 / +0.19 (t -2.63, LOYO 80% of only 5 years, walk-forward +7.1% 6/8) - the OPPOSITE sign to the family P/C bands' 'fear ON = boost' logic, on thin data; pooled t -1.41. Sector breadth: only WCDS (+0.62 / +0.42 / -0.00, t -2.73, LOYO 73%) and it fails the walk-forward consistency of its sibling move1_atr rule (12/22 years, reversed in 2022-26). OLV filter extremity: +0.74 / +0.82 / +0.71 (OLV's edge does not scale with how oversold). 52wh open-leg count terciles +0.52 / +0.46 / +0.59 (flat at the tercile cut of 3; does not contradict the plan's >= 5-open cell, which this cut does not isolate). WCDS move1_atr and sector breadth: cluster t -2.5 / -2.8 jointly but LOYO 61-63% and 2022-26 reversal (+0.78 / +1.12 / +1.15).
findings.method: Same tercile / clustered-t / LOYO / walk-forward battery; liquid-vs-overflow by clustered t on the tier dummy.
findings.n: 594 strategy x feature tests over 3,483 trades; 46 with |t| >= 2 and monotone (27 expected by chance), 14 passing the full rule (1-2 expected by chance)
findings.robustness: Family-wise: the passing set is well above chance but individual weak passers (IOB vrp, LT Trend P/C, 52wh spy_rv21, WCDS sector breadth) are within the false-positive budget and were graded accordingly.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Leg-level ATR sizing is the right unit (no vol-power change); no tier by universe tier; no VIX-, P/C-, or dial-conditioned within-strategy tiers. The plan's L0 and its 'dial moves covariance, not edge' conclusion both hold at the trade level.
findings.caveat: Overflow-tier stats carry survivorship (upper bound). Sector breadth uses only the ~815 ledger tickers with sector labels.

recommendations.change: OVS bottom-extremity cut: size any OVS signal whose mean of rank_ret_2d/5d/10d/21d is below 94 at 0.5x (composes multiplicatively with path, cycle, scale-out and caps; replayed point-in-time in strat_backtester sizing step 3b from the same rank columns).
recommendations.rule: mult = 0.5 if mean(rank_2d, rank_5d, rank_10d, rank_21d) < 94 else 1.0; no top-tier boost
recommendations.expected_effect: On equal total OVS risk: +12.9% R per unit risk (0.298 -> 0.337), 17/24 years better, daily-PnL sd x1.06, worst year -$13.9k (2020). If the freed risk is not redeployed: -$36k over 24 years (of $607k OVS PnL) for a 33% smaller OVS staged-risk footprint; cell win rate 0.59 vs 0.71, avgR +0.17 vs +0.47. Walk-forward tercile form: +19.7% PnL, 13/18 years.
recommendations.confidence: moderate-high (LOYO 80%, all eras/tiers/paths, mechanism = reversal scales with prior move); confirm with an engine replay including caps before ship

recommendations.change: Raise or remove the OVS path-2 aggregate daily cap (path2_daily_cap_pct 0.75% nominal / 1.125% effective).
recommendations.rule: path2_daily_cap_pct: 0.75 -> 1.5 (nominal), or remove; keep the per-strategy 250 bps cap
recommendations.expected_effect: +$49.5k over 24 years (+8.1% of OVS PnL) from 202 capped P2 trades whose avgR is +0.37 vs +0.18 uncapped; worst single-day extra loss -$1.4k, best +$11.9k; positive in 11 of 14 capping years.

recommendations.change: Pre-register (do not ship) a family band on single-stock dip-buys when SPY is within 2% of its 252-day high.
recommendations.rule: For OLV, LT Trend ST OS, Weak Close Decent Sznls, Monday Dip: mult = 0.5 if SPY close / max(SPY high, 252d) - 1 > -2% else 1.0; exclude St OS Sznl and all index dip-buys (MonFri, IOB, Monthly Weak Close show the opposite sign). Gate: PIT-clean by construction; re-test on hedged returns if the L3 beta hedge ships; require the 2017-21-style flat era not to dominate.
recommendations.expected_effect: Family: +13.4% R per unit risk on equal risk (0.411 -> 0.466), 15/24 years better, LOYO 73%, worst year -$37k; per strategy 0.5x years-better: OLV 12/17 (+12.2%), WCDS 13/22 (+21.3%), LT Trend 10/17 (+6.0%), Monday Dip 9/15 (+13.1%). Mostly a beta channel (SPY fwd 10d +1.25% off-high vs +0.46% near-high).
recommendations.confidence: moderate-low (market-timing tilt; OLV alone fails walk-forward; overlaps the retired OLV dial band's episodes)

recommendations.change: Extend gap_size_derate to Weak Close Decent Sznls (same Limit(Open - 0.25 ATR) entry as the two live carriers).
recommendations.rule: WCDS execution gap_size_derate = {threshold_atr: 0.25, mult: 0.5, dir: 'up'}; applied by order_staging at the T+1 open exactly as for Monday Dip / MonFri
recommendations.expected_effect: Cell N 91 avgR +0.23 win 0.62 vs +0.40 rest; fixed rule 16/22 years better, +11.6% R/risk on equal risk (live carriers score 16/23 and 9/15 on the same test). Alignment/appetite change of the same size as the existing overlay, not an evidenced edge (t -0.92, LOYO 67%).

recommendations.change: Review the OLV pre-earnings size override (earnings_size_override -10..0 td -> 10 bps nominal) against its original basis; the ledger shows no expectancy or tail deficit in that cell.
recommendations.rule: If the override's rationale was expectancy: restore base size in -10..0 (cell avgR +0.80, N 57, worst -2.9R, same as the rest). Log a re-exam trigger for a POST-print cut: mult 0.5 when <= 21 td since the last print, to be adopted only if the cell stays below +0.5R after +20 more trades (currently +0.38 N 86 vs +0.90, LOYO 60%, 2022-26 concentrated).
recommendations.expected_effect: Restoring the pre-print size recovers ~2/3 of that cell's risk at +0.80R (about +$8k/24y at ledger sizes); the post-print cut would have added +9.8% R/risk (11/17 years) but is not yet at the bar.

recommendations.change: Do NOT add per-trade multipliers on book-wide signal density, VIX, P/C fear state, ATR%, 200-SMA distance, universe tier, or the current-weights dial inside any strategy.
recommendations.rule: Negative results codified: signal density is already expressed mechanically and the fixed OVS rule wins only 9/24 years; the OLV dial gradient (t -3.2) vanishes on the PIT dial (t +0.03); the rest never clear the bar.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids ~6 false-positive tiers out of the 594-test family (27 |t|>=2 monotone hits expected by chance vs 46 observed).

recommendations.change: Pre-register only: 52wh Breakout 0.5x when SPY 21d realized vol < 10% (or VIX < ~13).
recommendations.rule: mult = 0.5 if SPY rv21 < 10% at signal close; grade with the exit-side (P4) protocol on hedged returns
recommendations.expected_effect: Cell N 114 avgR +0.19 win 0.32 vs +0.80 rest; fixed rule 12/18 years, +18.1% R/risk, day-sd x1.08; LOYO 64% (below bar).

negative_results: Dial-conditioned within-strategy tiers: OLV's dial gradient (+1.16/+0.78/+0.49, t -3.24, LOYO 80%) is a current-weights-vintage artifact; the PIT dial on the same 211 trades gives +1.22/+0.67/+0.98 (t +0.03). Pooled PIT dial slope t -1.21. Consistent with the retired OLV band and the July PIT gate.

OLV market-pullback tiers alone (SPY off 252d high, 21d return, 21d breadth change): in-sample t -2.5 to -3.9, but the gradient is ~60% beta (SPY fwd10 +1.8% vs +0.05% by tercile; residual t -1.40, non-monotone) and walk-forward tercile sizing fails (spy_hi252_dist -6.2% 5/9 years; spy_ret10 -12.8% 4/9); 2017-21 era flat (+1.09/+1.00/+0.91).

Per-trade signal-density multipliers: OVS book_sig_5td <= 3 -> 0.5x wins 9/24 years; same-day count walk-forward -33.6% (4/18); WCDS book_sig_5td t +7.19 but walk-forward -14.1% (2/15). Sign is real (pooled t +3.9, 10/13 strategies) but it is a cluster-year phenomenon the book already expresses through signal count and the caps.
OLV filter extremity (how oversold): +0.74/+0.82/+0.71, t -0.69. OLV's edge does not scale with rank depth (unlike OVS).
OLV recency-rung interaction: none of the market-state gradients is absorbed by the ladder (partial t unchanged), and the ladder's own gradient (+0.68/+0.82/+1.11) already cuts the weakest rung.
ATR% of price (Range %): no strategy monotone (OVS +0.33/+0.41/+0.40; 52wh +0.70/+0.41/+0.48); confirms the plan's L0 (inverse-vol ATR sizing is the right unit).
Distance from 200d SMA / 50d SMA / 252d high for the ticker: nothing passes in any strategy (OVS dist200 t -0.81; OLV t -0.17; Monday Dip hi252_dist Q4 -0.10 on N 22 only).
Liquid vs overflow tier: no expectancy difference in OVS (+0.39 vs +0.38), 52wh (+0.54 vs +0.52), LT Trend (t -0.93), OLV (t -1.34), ATR Ext (t -1.04); St OS Sznl t -2.19 rests on N 11 liquid trades.
Days since the strategy's last signal in the ticker: no strategy passes (OVS +0.38/+0.24/+0.39; Monday Dip only via one N-22 quintile).
VIX level: pooled t +3.63 but LOYO 67%; within strategy nothing passes (OVS t +1.81; 52wh LOYO 60%; Monday Dip non-monotone); collinear with SPY rv21 in 52wh (neither significant jointly).

P/C fear percentile (lag-1): LT Trend +0.52/+0.27/+0.19 (t -2.63) on 5 usable LOYO years and walk-forward +7.1% 6/8, opposite in sign to the family P/C bands' washout logic; pooled t -1.41. Not a tier.

WCDS signal-day move size (move1_atr, t -2.81, LOYO 71% tercile) and sector breadth (t -2.73, LOYO 73%): fixed rules win 12-13/22 years, binary LOYO 61-63%, and the 2022-26 era reverses (+0.78/+1.12/+1.15). Near-miss, not proposed.
IOB vol-risk-premium (VIX minus SPY rv21) tercile +0.21/+0.22/+0.60 (t +2.40, LOYO 75%): walk-forward -3.3% (11/19 years, worst -$24.5k). Not proposed.
Sector BO breadth change (-0.68/+1.03/+2.10, t +2.15) and ATR Extended Gap Up 10d return (+0.27/+0.48/+1.59, t +4.40): N 73 and 71 with 1-4 usable LOYO years; walk-forward not estimable. Report only.
3x ETF Overbot Fade rank_2d (+0.41/+0.96/+1.21, t +3.29): 3 usable LOYO years, walk-forward 1/2. Report only.
OVS 252d rank (leader vs laggard): +0.51/+0.32/+0.31, t -1.98, LOYO 56%; adds nothing next to short-window extremity (multivariate t -0.82).
OLV pre-earnings override cell: no deficit (avgR +0.80 N 57 vs +0.75; worst R and sd equal). The override does not capture any expectancy gradient; the OLV earnings gradient is post-print.
caveats: Ledger basis: full-history rebuild on flat $750k with today's universe (survivorship flatters the overflow tier and long dip-buys); OVS scale-out tranches collapsed to one trade with R = sum PnL / sum risk; signal-count and recency features count FILLED ledger signals only (staged-but-unfilled invisible), so live counts run higher and any count-based cut-point needs re-basing on the scanner's staged counts.

Dial vintage: 'dial' = 10d MA of the 63d column of data/rd2_fragility.parquet (current-weights recompute before 2026-07-02, PIT append after), value at the signal date (engine convention); 'dial_pit' = the sibling analyst's per-year vintage-lagged reconstruction (cross_strategy_regime_pit_dial.parquet, 2017+). All dial gradients reported are current-vintage unless labelled PIT.

Multiple testing: 594 strategy x feature tercile tests; 46 monotone hits at |t| >= 2 against ~27 expected by chance; 14 pass the full pre-registered rule against ~1-2 expected. Weak passers (IOB vrp, LT Trend P/C, 52wh spy_rv21, WCDS sector breadth) sit inside that false-positive budget and were graded weak or negative accordingly.

Fixed-rule evaluations (R1-R8) use cut-points and the 0.5x multiplier chosen after seeing the tercile tables; the year-by-year consistency and the expanding-window walk-forward tercile sizing (multipliers refit each year) are the out-of-sample checks. Gains are quoted on EQUAL TOTAL RISK (multiplier rescaled so risk-weighted mean = 1), which assumes the freed risk is redeployed inside the strategy; the no-redeploy cost is quoted separately where it matters (OVS -$36k/24y).

Rule evaluations do not model the per-strategy 250 bps cap, the P2 aggregate cap, the ticker notional cap or fill-window interactions; an engine replay (process_signals_fast) is the confirmation step for anything proposed.

Episode clustering chains same-strategy signals while gaps <= 5 trading days; 63-day-hold strategies (52wh, Sector BO) still have overlapping holds inside separate episodes, so their t-stats remain optimistic.
Earnings calendar (FMP) coverage of OLV trades is 91-100% by era; pre-2010 dates are FMP backfill and may be less complete for small caps.

The family market-pullback finding is a beta/market-timing effect with base-rate support (post-2000 index mean reversion after pullbacks in uptrends), not idiosyncratic alpha; it must be judged jointly with the plan's L3 beta hedge and re-tested on hedged returns if that ships.

Seasonal-rank features were deliberately excluded: sznl_ranks.csv holds only 2025-2027 ranks computed from history, so mapping them onto pre-2025 trades would inject lookahead; the book's strategies do not use the seasonal filter (use_sznl False everywhere), so nothing is lost for the overlay-capture question.

findings.claim: The book runs at roughly 5-7% of its log-growth-optimal size. The growth-maximizing multiple of CURRENT sizing (m; GRM = 1.5 m) is 15.5x on the 2003+ daily series and 19.25x on 2016+ with the empirical distribution and no haircut; 13x / 17x at a 25% haircut on the daily mean; 9x / 11.75x at a 50% haircut. Fat-tail treatments pull it down but not to anything reachable: GPD-extrapolated tails give m* 6.25-9 (the optimum there is the single-day-ruin boundary, one simulated -11% to -15% day in 2M draws, and is haircut-insensitive); a flat-day/active-day Student-t mixture gives 11-14.
findings.method: Exact E[log(1+m r)] on the flat-$750k daily MTM (strategy_daily.json total_flat, 2003-01-17..2026-08-07), quadratic approximation, GPD fit beyond the 2.5%/97.5% quantiles with a 2M-draw semi-parametric mixture, Student-t fit on non-zero days mixed with the flat-day mass, and a 3000-path stationary block bootstrap (mean block 10) whose 3y growth-max lands at m 12-25 by window/haircut.
findings.n: 6146 daily returns (2003+), 2766 (2016+), 1400 (2021+); 3000 bootstrap paths per cell
findings.robustness: Three windows (2003+/2016+/2021+) and three haircuts move m* between 9 and 19; four tail models (empirical, quadratic, GPD, t-mixture) between 6 and 21. No version puts m* below 6 (GRM 9). The ordering is stable: haircut matters more than the tail model above m~6, the tail model dominates the ruin boundary. The naive Student-t fit on ALL days degenerates (df~1.0 because of the flat-day spike) and gives absurd 6-11%/yr ruin at m=1; the active-day mixture fixes this (0.25-0.32%/yr at m=1).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Growth theory has nothing to say against any GRM the account can physically carry: from m=1 to m=3 the compounding tax is invisible (g is linear) and the growth forgone by staying at 1x versus the reachable range is large (g(1.5)-g(1) = +10 to +16 pts/yr, g(2)-g(1) = +21 to +31 pts/yr, before haircut). The GRM decision is therefore decided entirely by the hard boundaries in findings 3-5, not by curvature or by drawdown appetite.
findings.caveat: Scaling daily PnL by m assumes every fill scales linearly and no cap/margin/impact binds; findings 3-5 remove that assumption. The daily series ends 2026-08-07 (the Aug-2026 high-dial episode is only partly inside). Backtest mean is in-sample; the 50% haircut row is the one to size to until the live-vs-ledger ratio is measured.

findings.claim: Drawdown distribution by multiple, so the point on the curve can be chosen with eyes open. Drawdowns scale close to linearly with m in the median and faster in the tail; time-to-recover barely moves with m because the book's drawdowns are short (median recovery 14-30 sessions from the trough of the year's worst drawdown; the longest underwater spell is 44-100 sessions median).
findings.numbers: 1y horizon, compounded %-of-peak maxDD, 2016+ no haircut: m=1 median 5.0% / p95 8.7% / P(>10%) 2.5% / P(>20%) 0.0%; m=1.5 7.5% / 12.9% / 25% / 0.3%; m=2 10.0% / 16.9% / 50% / 2.0%; m=3 14.7% / 24.6% / 82% / 23% / P(>30%) 1.4%; m=5 23.9% / 38.8% / P(>20%) 66% / P(>30%) 28% / P(>50%) 0.6%; m=8 36.3% / 56.6% / P(>30%) 69% / P(>50%) 20%. 2003+ with 50% haircut (the pessimistic cell): m=1 7.4% / 14.8% / P(>20%) 0.7%; m=1.5 11.0% / 21.5% / 7.3%; m=2 14.6% / 27.9% / 21%; m=3 21.4% / 39.5% / 57% / P(>30%) 18%; m=5 34.1% / 58.5% / P(>50%) 13%; m=8 50.9% / 78.2% / P(>50%) 52%. 3y horizon, 2016+ no haircut: m=1.5 median 10.7% p95 15.6% P(>20%) 0.6%; m=2 14.1% / 20.5% / 5.9%; m=3 20.8% / 29.4% / 58%. 3y 2003+ 50% haircut: m=1.5 16.4% / 28.9% / P(>20%) 28% / P(>30%) 4%; m=2 21.5% / 36.9% / 59% / 16%. Time to recover (sessions from trough of max DD to new high, 1y): median 14-30, mean 20-40, p95 61-112 across cells; 13-44% of paths have not recovered the year's max DD by year end (mostly because it occurs late). Flat-basis DD in % of the fixed $750k is 2-10% higher than the compounded figure at the same m. Actual 2003-2026 path compounded: m=1 maxDD 12%, m=1.5 17.0% (flat 18.2%, worst day -8.8%), m=2 22%, m=3 32%, m=5 50%, m=8 71%; 2016-2026: m=1 8%, m=1.5 11.9%, m=2 16%, m=3 23%, m=5 35%. Continuous-time fractional-Kelly check: at m=1.5 the book is c~8% of Kelly (2016+) so theory says P(ever DD>=20%) = 0.8^(2/c-1) ~ 0.5%, bootstrap 3y 0.6%; at 50% haircut c~13%, theory 4%, bootstrap 16% (the bootstrap is fatter than lognormal, as it should be).
findings.method: Stationary block bootstrap (mean block 10 sessions, 3000 paths) of the daily series at each m, 1y and 3y paths, compounded and additive equity; recovery measured from the trough of the path's maximum drawdown; theory row from the lognormal fractional-Kelly identity.
findings.n: 3000 paths x 19 multiples x 2 horizons x 6 window/haircut cells
findings.robustness: The 2016+ and 2003+ windows agree on the shape (2003+ is ~2 pts of DD worse at every m); the haircut adds 2-5 pts of median DD and doubles the tail probabilities; the actual historical path sits at the p50-p80 of the bootstrap at every m, so the bootstrap is not flattering the history.
findings.implication_for_sizing: If nothing but drawdown mattered, m=2 (GRM 3.0) buys a 10-15% median annual drawdown with a 2-21% chance of a 20% year, and m=3 (GRM 4.5) a 15-21% median with a 23-57% chance; those are the trades the principal said were acceptable. They are not the constraint. The margin table below makes m>1.6 infeasible on the historical tail day before any of these drawdowns is reached.
findings.caveat: Block bootstrap with a 10-session mean block preserves weekly clustering but understates multi-month regimes; the 2003+ window contains 2008 but the book's short-heavy composition made that a modest event for it. Recovery times are conditional on the edge persisting at the haircut level assumed.

findings.claim: The binding boundary is portfolio margin, and it binds far below anything the growth curve or the drawdown table would choose. Because the book sizes ATR risk with no notional dimension, low-ATR instruments produce enormous notional per unit of risk: the largest single-ticker open position at current sizing reaches 122% of NAV (XLP, 2017-04-27), SPY exceeds 50% of NAV on 89 days since 2016, gross open notional is p95 159% / p99 254% / max 418% of NAV (2016-06-14: all long, Weak Close 33% + Monday Dip 32% + MonFri 30% of the gross). At an IBKR-style portfolio-margin requirement of 15% (3x ETFs 45%, no concentration add-on) that day needs 62.7% of the $750k, so the requirement reaches 100% of equity at m=1.60 (GRM 2.39); the p99 day at m=2.46 (GRM 3.69); on the live ~$632k primary NLV the max day binds at m=1.34 (GRM 2.01). Any concentration add-on makes the CURRENT book marginal: with 30% charged on non-broad tickers above 25% NAV the max day needs 89% of NAV at m=1 (binds at m=1.12, GRM 1.68); with the add-on on every ticker 122% (already over at m=1); a 30%/40% stress array 165%; Reg T 209% (m 0.48).
findings.numbers: Requirement/NAV at m=1, 2016+: pm_15 p95 25% p99 41% max 63%; pm_15 + non-broad conc add-on p95 34% p99 55% max 89%; pm_25 + conc p99 62% max 92%; pm_30 stress p99 100% max 165%; Reg T p99 129% max 209%. Days/yr with a single ticker over 25/50/100% NAV at m=1: 86 / 22 / 2.2. Tickers on >50%-NAV single-position days: SPY 89, QQQ 26, DIA 25, XLV 12, IYR 12, GLD 9, XLP 7, XLF 6. Top-decile notional days 2016+ are owned by Weak Close Decent Sznls 26%, 52wh Breakout 16%, OVS 12%, MonFri 10%, IOB 9%, Sector BO 7%. On the top-1% requirement days broad-index ETFs are 38% of gross and |net|/gross is 87% (long-side clusters, not offsetting shorts). Joint bootstrap P(requirement > equity within 3y), flat basis, plain pm_15: m=1 0%, 1.25 0%, 1.5 0.1-0.4%, 2 14-23%, 2.5 37-53%, 3 59-74%; with a 15% equity cushion m=1.5 7-10%, m=2 33-48%; with the non-broad concentration add-on m=1 15-18%, m=1.5 55-73%. Compounding basis (notional scales with NAV) is worse: m=2 78-81% within 3y.
findings.method: Open notional per business day from the ledger (Entry..Exit inclusive, Shares_flat x Entry Price), classified single stock / broad-index ETF / sector-commodity ETF / 3x (strategy_config.LEV3X_ALL); requirement = sum notional x rate under seven scenarios; feasibility multiple = 1/(requirement/NAV) on the max, p99, p95 day; joint stationary block bootstrap drawing (return, requirement ratio) rows together, ruin = requirement above equity on any day (absorbing).
findings.n: 4696 ledger trades, 2660 business days 2016+ (6169 since 2003), 3000 bootstrap paths per cell, 813 tickers
findings.robustness: The boundary is set by 5-10 historical cluster days, all long dip-buy clusters on broad/sector ETFs, and it recurs in every era (2007-05, 2013-11, 2014-09, 2016-06, 2019-06, 2019-12, 2023-02, 2024-12). The 2003+ max day gives m 1.51 vs 1.60 for 2016+. The ranking of scenarios never changes; only the absolute multiple does (1.6 plain PM, 1.1-1.3 with concentration or live NLV, 0.5-0.6 stress/Reg T). Those cluster days are also the book's best days (gross>100% NAV days are 15% of days and 49% of PnL, 44 bps/day vs 8), so this tail cannot be trimmed cheaply.
findings.implication_for_sizing: The unconstrained recommendation is GRM 2.25 (m=1.5), the largest step that clears the plain-PM max day with a small cushion and the p99 day on the live NLV (2.46 x 632/750 = 2.07). GRM 3.0 (m=2) is reachable ONLY after the notional tail is moved to a lower-requirement instrument or guarded: routing the SPY/QQQ/DIA legs of the dip-buy family through index futures (~5-6% margin) removes about 38% of the gross on the tail days, and a margin-feasibility guard in order_staging (project the day's requirement on live NLV, scale new entries pro rata above ~70%) converts a forced liquidation into a planned haircut. Neither is an ATR-risk cap; both are broker constraints. The requirement should be verified against IBKR's actual what-if margin before any step, because the rate assumptions here are stylized.
findings.caveat: Rates are assumed (15% single/broad, 45% 3x, 30% concentration above 25% NAV); IBKR's real house rules use TIMS stress arrays with position-size and price tiers that were not queried. Intraday notional (both entry and exit day counted) is conservative by roughly one day of overlap. Live NLV of ~$632k is from a memory note dated 2026-08-18. Treating requirement > equity as total ruin overstates the loss (IBKR liquidates partially, at the worst prices); it is the right absorbing state for a feasibility test, not a PnL estimate.

findings.claim: The per-strategy 250 bps/day cap is the second real boundary: it converts any multiplier above ~2.5 into a much smaller effective one and clips the cluster days that carry the edge, so growth under the fixed cap bends away from the linear curve exactly where the margin boundary already sits.
findings.numbers: Signal-day strategy risk at m=1: p50 58 bps, p90 179, p99 239, max 250 (already capped). Share of strategy-signal-days where m x risk exceeds 250: m=1.5 2%, 2 4%, 2.5 12%, 3 15%, 4 22%, 5 54%, 8 73%. Realised risk-weighted multiple under the fixed cap: m=1.5 -> 1.48, 2 -> 1.93, 2.5 -> 2.33, 3 -> 2.68, 4 -> 3.28, 5 -> 3.69, 8 -> 4.08, 20 -> 4.59 (ceiling ~4.6). Growth 2016+: linear vs cap-fixed g at m=1.5 48.4% vs 47.4%; m=2 63.7% vs 60.5%; m=3 93.3% vs 81.9%; m=5 148% vs 112%; m=8 220% vs 133%. Cap-fixed maxDD 2016+: m=1.5 11.7%, m=2 15.2%, m=3 21.8%, m=5 33%. Scaling the cap with m (250 m) restores the linear curve exactly.
findings.method: Per-trade daily PnL vectors from dist/data/trade_mtm.json (same 2026-08-07 vintage as strategy_daily.json; rebuilt m=1 series reconciles to total_flat to the dollar) scaled by s_i(m) = min(m, 250 / B_sd) with B_sd the strategy's filled risk on that signal date at m=1; growth curve on the resulting series.
findings.n: 4765 MTM vectors / 4734 trades (Aug-7 ledger vintage), 6144 days
findings.robustness: Same shape on 2003+ (m=3: 61.8% linear vs 55.5% capped; ceiling 4.59). B_sd is post-cap filled risk, so cap binding is understated slightly (pre-cap staged risk is invisible in the ledger); the P2 aggregate cap is not modelled.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Below GRM 2.25 the cap costs nothing (1 pt of growth) and it is the one thing that bounds the worst day (-$44k vs -$118k uncapped per the 2026-07-10 study), so it should stay fixed at 250 through the recommended step. If GRM ever goes past 3.0 after the margin tail is fixed, the cap has to be the explicit second decision: scale it with GRM (accept the wider worst day) or accept a realised multiple that saturates near 4.6.
findings.caveat: Cap-aware series is on the Aug-7 ledger vintage (4734 trades) while the notional/liquidity work uses the Sep-2 vintage (4696); the m=1 reconciliation is exact for the daily series.

findings.claim: Liquidity and market impact are NOT a boundary anywhere near the feasible range. Square-root impact at a conservative k=1 costs 2.8% of NAV a year at current size (8% of gross), 5.2% at m=1.5 (10%), 8.0% at m=2 (11.5%), 14.7% at m=3 (14%); the book's average edge halves only at m~58 and the most liquidity-sensitive strategy (overflow ATR Extended Gap Up) halves at m~12.
findings.numbers: Participation of position notional vs trailing-20d $ADV at m=1: book p90 by strategy/tier: ATR Extended Gap Up overflow 2.7% (p99 6.5%), St OS Sznl overflow 1.6%, 52wh overflow 1.0% (max 7.1%), Weak Close liquid 0.9% (max 32% on one thin ETF), LT Trend overflow 0.9%, OLV overflow 0.5%, OVS overflow 0.24%, everything liquid <0.3%, SPY/QQQ strategies 0.01%. Trades over 5% ADV: 0.2% at m=1, 0.5% at m=2, 1.0% at m=3, 1.7% at m=5, 4.4% at m=10. Round-trip impact in R at m=1 (mean): book 0.032R on an avgR of 0.48; ATR Ext 0.150R, St OS Sznl 0.065R, 3x fade 0.064R, Weak Close 0.045R, LT Trend 0.042R, OLV 0.026R, OVS 0.030R, index strategies 0.005R. m at which impact halves the edge: ATR Ext 12, LT Trend 16, St OS Sznl 19, OVS 39, 3x fade 43, Weak Close 44, 52wh 58, OLV 238, index strategies >2000. Sensitivity: k=0.5 halves every drag figure, k=1.5 multiplies by 1.5; a hard 10%-of-ADV participation cap leaves the realised multiple at 2.99 for m=3 and 4.97 for m=5.
findings.method: Per trade: notional / 20d dollar ADV (Volume x Close, master_prices read with column + ticker filters, ^GSPC/^NDX aliased to SPY/QQQ) at the entry date; cost = 2 x k x sigma20 x sqrt(participation x m) x notional x m; aggregated per year of NAV and per strategy 2016+.
findings.n: 4696 trades / 813 tickers, ADV found for 100%; 2016+ subset for the drag table
findings.robustness: Conclusion is insensitive to k in [0.5, 1.5] and to the participation cap; the only cells with material impact are overflow-tier names in the three strategies named, all of which are below 5% ADV at p99 at m=1.
findings.implication_for_sizing: No liquidity reason to hold GRM below 3; the overflow-tier ATR Extended Gap Up, St OS Sznl and LT Trend are the only strategies that should NOT receive more than ~2x their current size without an ADV participation check (they are also the strategies whose overflow avgR is a survivorship upper bound).
findings.caveat: Square-root impact with k=1 is a base-rate model (Almgren et al. 2005 find 0.6-0.9 for temporary+permanent impact); limit-order entries may earn rather than pay spread, exits (MOC/stop market) pay it in full. Fill probability of the -0.25 ATR limits at larger size is not modelled and would fall for the thin overflow names.

findings.claim: Compounding (sizing off live NAV) dominates the flat basis in expectation and adds no %-of-peak drawdown, but two facts about THIS account reverse the practical conclusion for now: the live primary NLV (~$632k) is below the $750k constant, so the book already runs ~1.19x the risk a NAV basis would give (effective GRM ~1.78 in live terms) and a switch today would CUT risk 16%; and the flat basis is a hidden de-leveraging rule whose value shows up exactly in the bad first-year paths.
findings.numbers: 10y block bootstrap, 2016+ no haircut, m=1: flat median terminal 4.3x, compounding 25.6x (p5 14.7x), half-compounding 9.0x; %-of-peak maxDD median identical (9% vs 9%); max dollar drawdown in units of initial capital: flat p95 13%, compounding p95 274% (drawdowns scale with the larger NAV). m=1.5: flat 6.0x, comp 122x, half 20.8x. With a 50% haircut, m=1.5, 10y: flat 3.5x (dollar DD p95 34%), comp 10.2x (p5 4.2x, dollar DD p95 311%), half 5.6x. 3y, 50% haircut, m=1.5: flat 1.74x, comp 1.98x (p5 1.24x), P(comp < flat on the same path) 9% (2016+) / 24% (2003+); given a first-year drawdown > 15% (15-22% of paths) the medians are 1.62 vs 1.54 (2016+) and 1.37 vs 1.36 (2003+), i.e. no regret in the median even then. Effective m in NAV terms at the end of the median 10y flat path: 0.23-0.6 (the flat book de-levers as it grows).
findings.method: Same block bootstrap, five sizing-base policies (flat, full compounding, quarterly rebase, ratchet up-only, half-compounding 0.5 x base + 0.5 x NAV quarterly) applied to the same paths; sequencing regret measured pairwise on identical paths.
findings.n: 3000 paths x 2 windows x 2 haircuts x 2 horizons x 3 multiples
findings.robustness: P(comp < flat) is 0-2% over 10y in every cell and 9-24% over 3y only in the haircut cells; the half-compounding policy sits between the two in every metric.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Do not switch the base to live NAV now: the account is smaller than the constant, so the switch is a risk cut, not a growth step, and the margin boundary on live NLV (m 1.34) is the tighter of the two. When NLV exceeds $750k, move to a half-compounding base (0.5 x 750k + 0.5 x NLV, re-set quarterly, never below the prior quarter's base): it captures most of the median growth (9x vs 25.6x vs 4.3x at 10y) while keeping dollar drawdowns in the same order as today's. The quarterly re-set is also what keeps the margin feasibility multiple constant in NAV terms.
findings.caveat: Live NLV figure is from an 2026-08-18 memory note and covers the primary account only; the PA (~$66k) runs its own clamp. Compounding results assume the edge scales with size, which findings 3-5 bound; 10y compounding medians are theoretical numbers at a Sharpe the haircut cells already discount.

findings.claim: Base rates outside the repo support the haircut row, not the raw row, for the growth optimum: live Sharpe ratios of backtested strategies come in 25-75% below backtest (Suhonen-Lennkh-Perez 2017 median 73% Sharpe haircut on alternative-beta backtests; McLean-Pontiff 2016 26% out-of-sample / 58% post-publication decay; Harvey-Liu 2015 haircut ~50% for t<3), and practitioners who size by Kelly run 1/4 to 1/2 Kelly (Thorp; MacLean-Ziemba). At GRM 2.25 the book would still be at 8-13% of Kelly on the haircut curves, i.e. below every practitioner floor, so nothing in the sizing literature argues against the step.
findings.numbers: Fractional-Kelly theory: 1/4 Kelly captures 44% of max growth with P(ever DD>=20/30/50%) = 21% / 8% / 0.8%; 1/2 Kelly 75% growth share with 51% / 34% / 12.5%; full Kelly 100% with 80% / 70% / 50%. The book at m=1.5 is c~0.08-0.13 of Kelly (growth share 15-24%). To reach even 1/4 Kelly on the 50%-haircut 2003+ curve the multiple would be m~2.3 (GRM 3.4), already past the margin boundary.
findings.method: Closed-form lognormal fractional-Kelly identities (growth share 2c-c^2, P(ever losing fraction x) = (1-x)^(2/c-1)) applied to the m* from finding 1; literature figures cited from memory as base rates, not recomputed.
findings.n: n/a (theory + literature)
findings.robustness: The bootstrap tails are fatter than lognormal (finding 2), so the theory probabilities are a floor; the ordering of conclusions does not change.
findings.implication_for_sizing: The a-priori appetite argument for GRM 1.5 (the plan's P(DD>15%)<=5% rule) is stricter than any base-rate practitioner rule; removing it, as the principal asked, leaves margin as the only reason not to run 2.25.
findings.caveat: Literature numbers are recalled, not re-derived here; they describe published/alternative-beta strategies, and this book has live fills that could measure its own haircut (plan L5).

recommendations.change: Raise GLOBAL_RISK_MULTIPLIER from 1.5 to 2.25 (m = 1.5x current) with NO drawdown constraint attached.
recommendations.rule: GRM is set to the largest multiple at which the historical maximum portfolio-margin requirement day stays below 100% of the sizing base at plain PM rates (15% single/broad, 45% 3x) AND the p99 requirement day stays below 100% of live NLV. Today: m 1.60 (max day) and 2.07 (p99 on $632k) -> m 1.5, GRM 2.25. Re-derive whenever NLV moves 20% or the rate assumptions are replaced by IBKR's what-if numbers.
recommendations.expected_effect: Ann log growth +10 to +16 pts/yr before haircut (2003+: 21.9% -> 32.3%; 2016+: 32.7% -> 48.4%), +5 to +7.5 pts at a 50% haircut. Drawdown accepted: 1y median 7.5% (2016+) to 11.0% (2003+ 50% haircut), p95 12.9% to 21.5%, P(1y DD > 20%) 0.3% to 7.3%, P(3y DD > 20%) 0.6% to 28%, P(3y DD > 30%) 0% to 4%; the actual 2003-2026 path at this size had a 17.0% compounded / 18.2%-of-$750k maxDD and an -8.8% worst day. P(margin requirement > equity within 3y) 0.1-0.4% on plain PM, 7-10% with a 15% equity cushion. Per-strategy 250 bps cap costs ~1 pt of growth at this m. Liquidity drag rises from 2.8% to 5.2% of NAV/yr.
recommendations.confidence: moderate-high on the growth and drawdown numbers (bootstrap, three windows, two haircuts agree); moderate on the boundary (stylized margin rates; must be verified against IBKR what-if before the step)

recommendations.change: Before ANY step past GRM 2.25 (toward 3.0, m=2), control the gross-notional tail with broker-constraint tools, not ATR caps: (a) route the SPY/QQQ/DIA legs of Weak Close, Monday Dip, MonFri, IOB and Monthly Weak Close through ES/NQ/MES/MNQ futures at ~5-6% margin; (b) a margin-feasibility guard in order_staging that projects the day's requirement (open book + staged entries, on live NLV) and scales the day's NEW entries pro rata above ~70% of NLV.
recommendations.rule: Feasibility test: the p99 requirement day at the target m must stay below 100% of live NLV and the max day below 100% of the sizing base; at m=2 today those read 123% / 82% (p99 on live NLV / max on $750k), so m=2 fails until (a) or (b) is in place.
recommendations.expected_effect: Broad-index ETFs are 38% of gross on the top-1% requirement days; moving them to futures cuts the requirement on those days by roughly a third and lifts the plain-PM boundary from m 1.60 to ~2.3 (GRM ~3.5). The guard converts the residual forced-liquidation tail (P 14-23% within 3y at m=2 on plain PM, 33-48% with a cushion) into a planned same-day haircut. Cost: the guard trims the book's best days (gross>100% days = 49% of PnL) on the few days it binds; that cost is unmeasured here and needs its own replay.
recommendations.confidence: moderate; the mechanism is arithmetic, the cost of the guard is not yet measured

recommendations.change: Keep the flat $750k sizing base until live NLV exceeds it; then move to a half-compounding base: base = max(prior base, 0.5 x 750k + 0.5 x NLV), reset quarterly, never below the prior quarter.
recommendations.rule: Do not rebase downward while NLV < 750k (a switch today is a 16% risk cut, not a growth step). Above 750k, the half-compounding rule; full compounding only if the measured live-vs-ledger haircut comes in under 25%.
recommendations.expected_effect: 10y median terminal 9x vs 4.3x flat vs 25.6x full compounding (2016+, no haircut, m=1); 5.6x vs 3.5x vs 10.2x at a 50% haircut, m=1.5. %-of-peak drawdowns unchanged; dollar drawdowns grow with NAV but at half the rate of full compounding. Sequencing regret at 3y horizon: P(comp < flat) 9-24% in the haircut cells, ~0% over 10y.

recommendations.change: Leave the per-strategy 250 bps/day cap fixed through the GRM 2.25 step; make scaling it an explicit second decision only if GRM ever exceeds 3.0.
recommendations.rule: Cap stays at 250 effective bps while m <= 1.5 (cost 1 pt of growth, binds on 2% of strategy-signal-days). Past m=2.5 the cap binds on 12%+ of days and the realised multiple saturates at ~4.6; scaling it with GRM restores linear growth but widens the worst day the cap exists to bound.
recommendations.expected_effect: At m=1.5: cap-fixed g 47.4% vs 48.4% linear, maxDD 11.7%. At m=3: 81.9% vs 93.3%, realised multiple 2.68.

recommendations.change: Measure the live-vs-ledger haircut (plan L5) and re-run this study's haircut row with the measured number; the growth optimum moves 2x across the 0-50% haircut range while every boundary is haircut-invariant.
recommendations.rule: Until >=150 matched live trades exist, size to the 50%-haircut row (g at GRM 2.25: 15.4% 2003+ / 23.4% 2016+).
recommendations.expected_effect: Turns the growth-side numbers from in-sample to measured; no change to the recommended GRM (margin-bound either way).
recommendations.confidence: high that it matters, n/a on direction

negative_results: Drawdown appetite is not what limits this book: at every multiple up to m=2 the drawdown distribution the principal said is acceptable (10-15% median, 2-21% chance of a 20% year) is reached only AFTER the margin boundary (m 1.6 on the max day) has already been crossed.
The compounding tax is irrelevant in the feasible range: g(m) is linear to within 1 pt through m=3 on every window and haircut; nothing about curvature argues for or against GRM 1.5 vs 2.25 vs 3.0.

Liquidity / market impact is not a boundary: the book's edge halves only at m~58 (k=1 sqrt impact); the worst strategy (overflow ATR Extended Gap Up) at m~12. The 10%-of-ADV participation cap leaves the realised multiple at 2.99 for m=3.

Single-day ruin from the return distribution is not a boundary: first ruin at m=17 (2003+) / 20.5 (2016+) empirically, 6.5-9.25 with GPD-extrapolated tails, annual single-day-ruin probability 0.3-0.7% at m 1-1.5 on the t-mixture; all far past the margin boundary.

A naive Student-t fit on all days is unusable for this book (df ~1.0 from the 16-19% flat-day spike; implies 6-11%/yr ruin at current size, which 23 years never showed); only the active-day mixture is meaningful.

Switching the sizing base to live NAV today is not a growth step: the primary NLV (~$632k) is below the $750k constant, so it is a 16% risk cut, and the live-NLV margin boundary (m 1.34) is tighter than the flat-basis one.

A beta hedge via index futures does not relax the margin boundary (futures margin is additive on top of the equity leg); only moving the equity legs themselves to futures, a feasibility guard, or NAV growth does.

Full-Kelly and half-Kelly sizes (m 9-19 / 4.5-9.5) are unattainable in any scenario; even 1/4 Kelly on the pessimistic curve (m~2.3) sits past the margin boundary, so the fractional-Kelly literature is moot for the GRM choice and only informs the haircut.
caveats: Margin model is stylized: 15% single/broad, 45% 3x, 30% concentration above 25% NAV, 30/40% stress array, Reg T 50%. IBKR's real portfolio-margin house rules (TIMS stress arrays, price/size tiers, per-symbol exceptions) were not queried; the right next step is an IBKR what-if margin call on the 2016-06-14, 2019-06-26 and 2023-02-03 books scaled by m before any GRM change.

Vintages: daily series and per-trade MTM vectors are the 2026-08-07 ledger (4734 trades, dist/data); notional and liquidity use the 2026-09-02 ledger (gha:33608560596, 4696 trades). No dial series is used in this topic. Live NLV ~$632k is from a 2026-08-18 memory note (primary only).

Scaling the daily series by m assumes fills, cap behaviour and impact scale linearly; the cap-aware (finding 4) and liquidity (finding 5) corrections are applied separately, not jointly, and the P2 aggregate cap and the OLV ticker notional cap are not modelled at higher m.

Block bootstrap (mean block 10) preserves weekly clustering, not multi-month regimes; the 2003+ window is the only one with 2008 and the book's composition then was short-heavy OVS, so a long-cluster crash regime like 2020-03 at m=1.5 is under-sampled.

'Ruin' in the margin bootstrap means requirement above equity on some day (a forced-liquidation event), not total loss; the realised cost of such an event is unmeasured and would land on the worst possible day.

The backtest mean is in-sample and the overflow tier carries survivorship (21 of 22 major 2020s delistings absent); the 50%-haircut rows are the ones to cite until the live-vs-ledger ratio is measured. Literature base rates in finding 7 are recalled, not re-derived.
Open notional counts both the entry and the exit day (inclusive), a roughly one-day conservative overlap; single-ticker concentration figures inherit it.
Nothing here conditions on the dial or proposes dynamic scaling; the static GRM and the two boundary controls are the whole scope, consistent with the repo's negative results on book-level throttles.

findings.claim: There is essentially no true out-of-sample record. strategy_config.py was created 2025-12-18 and every live strategy's signal rules were rewritten or tuned between 2026-04 and 2026-07 on the full 2003-2026 history; the honest OOS window per strategy (signal date >= last rule change) is 1 to 4 months and holds 108 trades book-wide.
findings.numbers: Repo first commit 2025-12-18; 149 commits to strategy_config.py; rule-freeze dates: OVS 2026-06-05, OLV 07-20, 52wh 07-07, WCDS 05-19, LT Trend 05-01, St OS Sznl 04-23, 3x fades 07-28, 3x Leader 07-10, IOB 05-12, MonFri 06-09, Sector BO 05-01, Monday Dip 05-12, ATR Ext 05-11, Monthly WC 07-31. Pooled post-freeze: N=108, avgR 0.185 vs in-sample 0.516 at the same strategy mix (ratio 0.36), day-block bootstrap 95% CI on the ratio [-0.57, 1.22]. Six strategies have ZERO post-freeze trades (52wh, 3x Leader, IOB, Monthly WC, Sector BO, St OS Sznl, WCDS).
findings.method: git history of strategy_config.py hashed per strategy dict (03_freeze_dates), hand classification of rule vs sizing commits, ledger split at each strategy's freeze date (05_oos), day-block bootstrap of the pooled OOS mean
findings.robustness: The CI spans zero to more than the in-sample value; the post-freeze window cannot discriminate a 50% haircut from none. Reported for completeness; the 2026 calendar year is used instead (next finding).
findings.implication_for_sizing: Any haircut has to come from structural arguments (selection, survivorship, costs) plus the 2026 pseudo-OOS year, not from a measured OOS ratio. Treat every 'OOS record' claim in the repo as in-sample until the live reconciliation exists.
findings.caveat: Rule-vs-sizing classification of commits is by hand from commit messages; sizing-only commits (frag bands, ladders, derates) do not change the signal set and were ignored.

findings.claim: 2026 (the only pseudo-OOS year: rules designed after 2025-12 but tuned through 2026-08) realized about half of the ledger edge per unit of risk, is the 4th-worst of 19 years on that ratio, and is fully consistent with the in-sample midterm-year base rate rather than with a broken book. Dollar PnL was nevertheless above average because signal flow was 1.6x normal.

findings.claim: Deflated-Sharpe (Bailey and Lopez de Prado) selection deflation keeps 63-79% of the book Sharpe depending on how many trials are counted; significance is never in doubt (DSR ~ 1.0 at T > 2,700 days), the deflation is a level correction to the mean.

findings.claim: Cost realism: the engine charges nothing on limit entries, target limits or time exits and no commissions; a realistic commission + market-exit spread model costs 5.6% of the ledger mean book-wide, and the bar-touch fill convention costs a further 2-4%. The 2 bps assumption should be replaced by roughly 6-10% of the mean.
findings.numbers: Model: $0.005/share, $1 floor, both sides, plus half-spread on MKT/MOC exits by 63d dollar ADV (1.5 bps >$100M, 3 bps $25-100M, 6 bps $5-25M, 12 bps below). Book cost 0.025 R/trade = 5.6% of avgR 0.453. Tier: liquid 0.021 R (4.3%, comm 3.8 bps + exit 1.2 bps), overflow 0.028 R (6.6%, 7.3 + 2.4 bps). By strategy (cost share of avgR): WCDS 9.7%, OVS 8.5% ($1 minimum on small scale-out tranches), LT Trend 6.3%, St OS 4.8%, Monday Dip 4.3%, Sector BO 3.1%, MonFri 3.0%, ATR Ext 2.9%, IOB 2.6%, 52wh 1.8%, OLV 1.7%, 3x ETF Fade 1.6%, 3x Bear 1.1%, 3x Leader 0.6%, Monthly WC 0.5%. Marginal target fills: 3.8% of target exits (1.0% of trades), R 1.49 at target vs 1.05 at that day's close (~0.5% of book R). Short borrow scenario 0.0006 R/trade. Stops already carry 3/13 bps; adjusted bars handle dividends correctly on both sides (not optimistic).

findings.robustness: Judgement overrides on the two mechanical outliers: OVS's 70% is driven by 51 config versions and a midterm 2026 that matches its own midterm base rate (0.10 vs 0.15 avg); a judgement range is 45-60%. 52wh's 69% is driven by its structurally low per-trade SR (0.26 on a 63d hold with right skew); judgement 50-65%, but it has ZERO trades since 2025-08 (dial gate), owns 27% of worst-day losses and is long single-stock, so it stays in the less-trust tier either way.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Use keep_s as the mu shrinkage in the L1 tilt (Sigma^-1 mu on shrunk means) instead of a flat 50%: it moves risk toward MonFri, IOB, the 3x fades, ATR Ext and Monday Dip and away from WCDS, 52wh, LT Trend ST OS, St OS Sznl and the two pilots. OVS is bounded by its caps, not base bps, so its haircut mostly matters for the book total.
findings.caveat: The composite is a transparent formula, not a fitted model; ranges are the product of each component's generous/pessimistic bound and are wide by construction.

findings.claim: Book-level haircut on the ledger mean: recommended 40% (keep 0.60), range 27% to 71%. The 50% placeholder is inside the range and slightly pessimistic on the central estimate; nothing here supports raising GRM.
findings.numbers: Bottom-up PnL-weighted keep 0.51 [0.29, 0.73]. Direct: structural keep 0.63 (DSR keep 0.72 at N=250 x cost 0.92 x survivorship 0.95), realized-2026 keep 0.76 (average of the risk-weighted 2026 ratio 0.52 and the midterm-conditioned ratio capped at 1.0); direct blend 0.70. Recommended = mean of bottom-up and direct = 0.605 -> haircut 39.5%. Range low 27% (every component generous), high 71% (bottom-up pessimistic, and the raw unweighted 2026 ratio 0.41 sits inside it). Against the plan's L4 frontier: at a 50% haircut GRM 1.5 gives P(1y maxDD > 15%) 3.3% and 1.875 gives 9.1%; a 40% haircut lands between the 'none' and '50%' rows (1.875 roughly 5-6%), so GRM 1.5 remains the largest value inside the 5% budget.
findings.method: 09_synthesis combining the per-strategy composite (PnL-weighted) with the book-level direct evidence from 06 (DSR grid), 05c (risk-weighted 2026 ratios) and 08 (costs)
findings.n: 4,696 trades; 2,766 daily observations 2016+; 19 yearly ratios
findings.robustness: Bottom-up (0.51) and direct (0.70) disagree by 0.19: the bottom-up view is dragged by OVS's mechanical 0.30 keep at 15% of PnL and by the long-stock family; the direct view is lifted by the midterm-conditioned 2026 reading. The recommended 0.60 is the midpoint; both bounds of the range are defended by at least one estimator.
findings.implication_for_sizing: Replace the 50% placeholder with 40% central and carry the 27-71% range into the L4 rule's sensitivity; GRM stays 1.5. Re-derive after the first 150 broker-matched fills and again after 2027 Q1 (first non-midterm OOS quarters).
findings.caveat: The two halves are not independent (both use the 2026 year); the range is a judgement envelope, not a confidence interval.

findings.claim: Strategies that deserve MORE trust than the book average: SPY QQQ MonFri Reversion, Indices Oversold Bounce, 3x ETF Overbot Fade, Overbot Vol Spike (as a strategy, not as a version), ATR Extended Gap Up. LESS trust: Weak Close Decent Sznls, 52wh Breakout, LT Trend ST OS, St OS Sznl, and the pilots 3x Leader Gap Fade and Monthly Weak Close. Oversold Low Volume, Monday Dip, 3x Bear Fade and Sector BO are average.
findings.numbers: MonFri: N=348, 5 versions, index ETF (no survivorship), highest daily Sharpe in the book (1.32), era avgR 0.28/0.51/0.51/0.63 (2003-09/2010-16/2017-21/2022-25), cost 3%. IOB: N=290, 5 versions, index, era 0.19/0.09/0.72/0.64. 3x ETF Fade: N=87, 6 versions, ETF, DSR keep 0.90 but era 1.0/1.68/0.33. OVS: N=2,483, edge in every era 0.52/0.34/0.41/0.42, 2026 (0.10) in line with its midterm cells, but 51 versions. ATR Ext: 4 versions, 2026 PnL/risk 1.15 vs 1.09 (N=11), short. WCDS: 17 versions, era 0.02/0.11/0.35/0.91 (edge is a 2017+ phenomenon; N=61 in the last era), cost 9.7%, 12.5% of worst-day losses. 52wh: 17 versions, 0 trades since 2025-08-06, era 0.17/0.61/0.49/1.48, 27% of worst-5%-day losses for 14.5% of PnL, long single-stock 77% overflow. LT Trend: 11 versions, 2026 0.01 PnL/risk on 23 trades (P below half of trailing 0.84), 75% overflow long, 7.7% collapse share. St OS Sznl: N=58, PSR(0) 0.89 (weakest evidence in the book), overflow 0.18 vs liquid 1.02, 17% collapse share. OLV: 27 versions, 2026 0.36 vs 1.05 (P below half 0.96) but still +$50k in 2026, 72% overflow long. Pilots: 3x Leader N=24; Monthly WC N=14 with per-trade SR 3.5 (not a believable number at N=14; base-rate prior 0.5).
findings.method: Trust tiers from the composite keep plus era stability (05_oos era table), tail ownership (plan L1e), version count, instrument class and the 2026 per-strategy realization
findings.n: 15 strategies
findings.robustness: Every 'more trust' name is either an index/ETF strategy with <= 6 versions or the strategy with the largest N and era-stable edge; every 'less trust' name has at least two of: 17+ versions, era-concentrated edge, overflow long exposure, 2026 failure, N < 30.
findings.implication_for_sizing: The L1 tilt's cuts (52wh, IOB, Sector BO, WCDS) and raises (LT Trend, 3x fades, OLV) are about efficiency, not trust; layering the trust keeps on top would keep the 52wh and WCDS cuts, soften the IOB cut (its lower edge is real but well-estimated), and temper the LT Trend and OLV raises until 2027 confirms them.
findings.caveat: Era tables are in-sample for every era; tier assignment is judgement over the numbers.

recommendations.change: Replace the plan's 50% placeholder haircut on the backtest mean with 40% central (keep 0.60) and a 27-71% range; feed the range into the L4 GRM rule as a sensitivity row.

recommendations.confidence: moderate: both estimators bracket 0.60; neither is independent of the 2026 year

recommendations.expected_effect: Ledger avgR 0.453 -> ~0.428; OVS P2/near tranches show their true cost; no live behaviour change.

recommendations.change: Apply a standing 15% survivorship haircut (keep 0.85) to the long single-stock overflow-heavy strategies (OLV, LT Trend ST OS, St OS Sznl, 52wh overflow) and 5% to long liquid single-stock strategies until the point-in-time overflow universe lands; none for index/ETF strategies; none for shorts.

recommendations.change: Treat 2026's realized 0.52x edge per unit risk as consistent with the midterm base rate, not as decay: no additional book-wide cut, but flag OLV and LT Trend ST OS for a 2027 Q1 re-read (their 2026 is the least explained by cycle or dial).
recommendations.rule: Re-read trigger: first two non-midterm quarters; if OLV PnL/risk stays below 0.5 and LT Trend below 0.15, retire the plan's raises for them.
recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids a second sizing reaction to a regime the book has already priced (OVS 0.75x midterm mult) while keeping the two genuine 2026 laggards on watch.

negative_results: The post-rule-freeze OOS window (108 trades, 1-4 months per strategy) is uninformative: ratio 0.36 with a day-block 95% CI of [-0.57, 1.22]; it cannot discriminate a 50% haircut from none.

The dial mix does not explain the 2026 shortfall: expected 2026 avgR at the strategy x signal-date-dial mix is 0.49 vs realized 0.19 (ratio 0.39); the 30-50 and 65+ buckets in 2026 ran 0.19 and 0.03 vs 0.54 and 0.33 historically.

Overflow tier is NOT inflated relative to liquid: for every shared strategy overflow avgR <= liquid (OVS 0.390 vs 0.397, OLV 0.68 vs 0.97, LT Trend 0.29 vs 0.40, St OS 0.18 vs 1.02, 52wh 0.52 vs 0.54, ATR Ext 0.69 vs 1.25); survivorship conditions both tiers, so the tier split cannot measure it.

Marginal bar-touch limit fills are a small optimism (4.5% of entries at <= 0.02 ATR; -1.8% of avgR if half fill live, -3.8% if none), not the large fill-assumption problem sometimes assumed; the marginal fills are the best trades, which bounds the loss.

No broker-fill R series exists: ~/trading_journal/trade_journal.csv is absent, the Sheets Fill_Status is yfinance-modeled (same bars as the engine), the DO fills ring keeps 14 days, and the 27-row Trade_Journal tab predates the current book. Live-vs-ledger R on matched trades cannot be computed today.

Deflated Sharpe significance is trivially passed (DSR ~ 1.0 for every book window at T > 2,700 days); the multiple-testing question is about the LEVEL of the mean (keep 0.63-0.79), never about whether the book has an edge.
Short borrow cost is immaterial (0.0006 R/trade scenario) and the adjusted-price basis is correct on both sides; neither belongs in the haircut.

The per-strategy DSR at trials = git versions penalizes OVS (51 versions) and 52wh (per-trade SR 0.26) beyond what judgement supports; the mechanical central for those two is reported but flagged, not adopted as-is.
caveats: Ledger vintage gha:33608560596 built 2026-09-02 (last signal 2026-08-28); the per-strategy daily series (dist/data/strategy_daily.json) ends 2026-08-07, so the August 2026 high-dial episode is only partly inside the daily checks.

Dial series used for the dial-mix check is the current-weights vintage (rows before 2026-07-02 are the recompute vintage, drift up to ~7 points); the finding that the dial does not explain 2026 is robust to that but the bucket counts are not point-in-time.
2026 is one partial midterm year; the midterm effect it is compared against was discovered in-sample (6 of 6 windows) and is supported only by the external presidential-cycle base rate.

Trials count for the deflated Sharpe is a judgement (versions/3 central, versions to versions/8 range); the Bailey/LdP frame assumes independent null trials with the best picked, which is the most conservative reading of nested variants.
Survivorship magnitudes are scenario-based (external delisting base rates x the ledger's own collapse-bucket avgR); no delisted-name history exists in the cache to measure them directly.
Cost model uses an ADV-bucketed half-spread proxy and $0.005/share; MOC auction prints likely cost less than the proxy, overflow opens can cost more.
All dollars are flat $750k; the per-strategy composite keep is a transparent multiplicative formula, not a fitted model, and its ranges are component-bound products rather than confidence intervals.
Sheets were read via the OneDrive service-account credentials in read-only scope; no repo code, config, tests or committed data were modified and nothing was committed.

outside_evidence.topic: Base rates for backtest-to-live decay and overfitting haircuts (McLean-Pontiff, Suhonen et al., Harvey-Liu, Bailey-Lopez de Prado, smart-beta launch studies, short-term reversal / breakout evidence, survivorship), with recommended haircut ranges for (a) 15-20y backtest + 1-3y live, (b) <30-trade pilots, (c) overflow small-cap tier

base_rates.claim: Published cross-sectional predictors lose 26% of in-sample return out-of-sample (pre-publication, pure statistical/data-mining upper bound) and 58% post-publication; the 32-pt difference is attributed to publication-informed arbitrage. Decay is LARGER for predictors with higher in-sample returns and SMALLER for portfolios concentrated in high-idiosyncratic-risk, low-liquidity stocks.
base_rates.number: -26% OOS; -58% post-publication; 97 predictors
base_rates.source: McLean & Pontiff, Journal of Finance 2016, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2156623
base_rates.applicability: Direct. This book's rules are unpublished, so the 26% OOS number (not 58%) is the right anchor for pure selection/data-mining decay of a simple rule; the extra 32% arbitrage component applies only insofar as the same edges are widely known (short-term reversal and 52wh breakout are textbook). The 'high in-sample return decays more' finding argues for haircutting the book's best-looking cells (OLV avgR +0.6, Monthly Weak Close 15-for-15) harder than the mediocre ones.

base_rates.claim: Publication bias alone explains only a 12.3% (SE 1.7pp) overstatement of in-sample anomaly returns; the remaining post-publication decline (~35% of returns) is mispricing that gets traded away. Post-publication decay is reliably present ONLY in the US (241 anomalies, 39 markets).
base_rates.number: 12.3% bias; ~35% traded away; US-only decay
base_rates.source: Chen & Zimmermann, Review of Asset Pricing Studies 2020, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2802357; Jacobs & Müller, JFE 2020, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2816490
base_rates.applicability: Sets a FLOOR on the statistical haircut (~12%) for a single simple rule with a long sample, and confirms that in liquid US equities the crowding component dominates. This book trades US names exclusively, where decay is largest.

base_rates.claim: Across a large set of published stock anomalies, post-publication Sharpe ratio drops 43% on average. Publication year alone explains 30% of the cross-sectional variance in decay (each later year adds +5 pp of decay); overfitting proxies (number of operations to compute the signal, sensitivity of in-sample Sharpe to outliers) add 15%; arbitrage-capital variables are statistically significant but marginal.
base_rates.number: -43% Sharpe; +5 pp decay per publication year; complexity +15% R2
base_rates.source: Falck, Rej & Thesmar (Capital Fund Management), Quantitative Finance 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.01380
base_rates.applicability: Two direct implications: (1) rules built on recent data decay more than old ones (recency of discovery = crowding proxy), so the 2026-vintage overlays deserve more haircut than the 2003-era core rules; (2) signal complexity (operation count) and outlier-driven in-sample Sharpe predict decay. Several repo strategies have many stacked conditions and small-N episode concentration (3x Leader Gap Fade: 31 trades / 15 episodes; bear-fade marginal legs 'mostly Apr 2024'), which this evidence says decay hardest.

base_rates.claim: Anomaly returns approximately halved after decimalization (2001) as liquidity and arbitrage activity rose; both cross-sectional coefficients and hedge-portfolio returns trend toward zero.
base_rates.source: Chordia, Subrahmanyam & Tong, Journal of Accounting and Economics 2014, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2029057
base_rates.applicability: The repo's 2003-2026 ledger already sits mostly in the post-decimalization era, so this halving is largely baked into the sample; it is a warning against weighting pre-2010 sub-periods equally with recent ones when estimating forward expectancy.

base_rates.claim: Accounting for effective bid-ask spreads, post-publication decay and the modern trading era, the average anomaly's expected net long-short return post-2005 is about -1 bp/month under original implementations and only ~4 bps/month under cost-minimizing execution (204 anomalies); decay reaches ~93% after trading costs.
base_rates.number: -1 to +4 bps/month net; ~93% decay net of costs
base_rates.source: Chen & Velikov, JFQA 2023, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3624932
base_rates.applicability: Worst-case base rate for generic, publicly known anomalies in liquid US stocks. The book's edges are conditional and short-hold (not monthly-rebalanced factor portfolios) so this is not the central estimate, but it is the number to beat for any strategy whose signal is close to a textbook anomaly (plain short-term reversal, 52wh breakout).
